docs.title: Commol
docs.text:
Commol builds, simulates and calibrates compartment models: amounts move between states (compartments) at rates you write as formulas. An amount can be a count, a mass or a concentration. You describe the model in Python; a Rust engine expands it over your stratifications, compiles every rate to machine code, and runs it or fits it to your data.

Before version 1.0

The API can change between minor versions (0.2 → 0.3). The changelog marks every change that breaks code as Breaking.

docs.title: How Commol works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[ModelBuilder] -->|build| B[Model]
    B --> C[Simulation]
    C -->|run| D[Results]
    B --> E[CalibrationProblem]
    E --> F[Calibrator]
    F -->|run| G[CalibrationResult]
    G -->|apply_calibration_parameters| B
  1. Build a Model with ModelBuilder: bins, parameters, transitions, stratifications and initial conditions. Commol validates it as you go.
  2. Simulate it with Simulation: one series per compartment and accumulator.
  3. Calibrate unknown values against observations with Calibrator, and write the result back into the model.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=100)

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Local approximations through Calibrator.uncertainty, on the unbounded scale of the parameters, with a fit on a bound refused: Laplace(draws), the normal N(θ̂, H⁻¹) of the observation models, and Calibrator.delta_band(result, positions, level), the band of the outputs by the delta method; Sandwich(block_length, draws), the covariance H⁻¹ B H⁻¹ with the scores summed over blocks (CR1) and a Student t with G − 1 degrees of freedom, which needs no noise model and refuses loss_function="mae" and too few blocks; LaplaceMixture(starts, draws, target), a Laplace approximation at each optimum of a multi-start fit as the proposal of Pareto-smoothed importance sampling of a LikelihoodTarget(priors) or GibbsTarget(priors, eta), which reports k_hat and marks a sample with k_hat > 0.7 as unreliable. curvature is "gauss_newton" (the expected Fisher information of each observation model, by default) or "hessian". See Local Approximations.

  • GibbsPosterior: the Gibbs posterior prior(θ) · exp(−η · loss(θ)) of the problem's loss, sampled by sequential Monte Carlo from the priors to the posterior; it returns a GibbsResult with the η it ran with. eta is required: a number above 0, EtaCalibration.information_matching(block_length) (the curvature of the sum of squares or of observation models against the variance of the scores of its terms summed over blocks, with a deterministic engine) or EtaCalibration.bootstrap_coverage(replicates, block_length, confidence_level) (any loss). See Sequential Monte Carlo.

  • AbcSmc and AbcRejection: approximate Bayesian computation on a required distance, LossDistance() or SeriesDistance(metric). With a stochastic engine each distance reads one fresh replicate of its particle, so the problem's replicates and replicate_summary do not apply, and the result says so. See ABC.
  • SmcResult: the sample, the level of each step, the log evidence, the value each particle keeps and the diagnostics of each step (SmcDiagnostics: effective size, resampling, acceptance rate and move count).
  • Priors: Uniform(), LogUniform(), Beta(a, b), Normal(mean, sd), LogNormal(mu, sigma) and Gamma(shape, rate), each truncated to the bounds of its parameter, and Priors (a mapping of parameter to distribution, or Priors.uniform_on_bounds()). Every sampling method takes priors with no default, and a prior whose bounds do not fit raises a ValueError that names the distributions that fit them. Their draws are the same on every platform. See Priors.
  • SampleIdentifiability(reference="prior", priors=...): the contraction of each parameter against its prior. See Identifiability.
  • Conformal prediction intervals through Calibrator.uncertainty: intervals for observations with a coverage guarantee that needs no noise model, no prior and no correct model. SplitConformal scores held-out observations; RollingConformal gives intervals ahead of the data, one quantile per horizon (the k-th observation after an origin); JackknifePlus refits once per block left out, with the CV+ bound for blocks of more than one observation; EnbPI draws its own replicates of blocks for series with dependent errors; AdaptiveConformal walks a stream of new observations with a working level that moves with each miss. Each takes a required score ("absolute", "normalized" or "spread"), by ("series" or "all") and level, and returns a ConformalResult (PredictionIntervals, the scores and the guarantee). See Conformal Prediction Intervals.
  • SimulationPlotter.plot_series(prediction_intervals=...) draws the band of conformal intervals, and simulation_report(..., prediction_intervals=...) reports them.
  • Observation models: CalibrationProblem(observation_models={series: model}) takes one model per series label, NormalObservations(sd), LogNormalObservations(sigma, center) (center="mean" or "median", no default), StudentTObservations(df, scale), PoissonObservations(), NegativeBinomialObservations(overdispersion) (variance μ + φμ²) or BinomialObservations(trials) (or the new ObservedDataPoint.trials of each observation), and the problem fits by maximum likelihood. A noise argument is a number or a calibration parameter of the new type "noise", which never reaches the engine. Observed values outside a model's support raise a ValueError that names the observation. A stochastic engine and normalize_observations need a loss. See Observation Models.
  • BayesianPosterior: the posterior of the observation models and its log evidence, on the sequential Monte Carlo sampler. GibbsPosterior on observation models is the fractional posterior prior · L^η.
  • DistributionNoise(): prediction intervals that draw from the observation models; commol.scores.log_score, the log density of held-out observations under the predictive, which needs DistributionNoise().
  • ParametricBootstrap(replicates): fits to data sets drawn from the observation models at the fit. ResamplingDiagnostics.block_length is None for it.

  • A model can hold bins of different units, such as people and the concentration of bacteria in water: each bin starts at an amount in its own unit, a model whose bins all start at 0 builds and runs, and the Calibrator rejects an initial-condition remainder whose unit is not the unit of a calibrated amount. See Bins of different units.

  • Sensitivity analysis with no data: SensitivityAnalysis(simulation, inputs, replicates=None, seed=None).run(method), the third entry point of the registry, with methods that subclass SensitivityMethod[R]. What varies is an InputSpace of calibration parameters (model parameters or initial conditions): independent distributions (InputSpace.independent, InputSpace.uniform_on_bounds) or a weighted sample (InputSpace.from_sample). Each run is reduced in Rust to quantities of interest: ValueAt, Gain (as an observation with a window), Peak, PeakPosition and Trajectory. With a stochastic engine replicates and seed are required; a point of a design holds the mean of its replicates on common seeds, and a propagation keeps every replicate. See Sensitivity Analysis.

  • Propagation: the draws of the inputs and the quantities of each run (PropagationResult, with summary(confidence_level)); its sample gives the bands of a Predictive, which runs the same replicates.
  • PRCC: partial rank correlation coefficients and their p-values (PRCCResult), weighted for a sample, with Kish's effective size in the test.
  • Morris: elementary effects, mu, mu_star and sigma (MorrisResult), on levels at the centres of strata of equal probability.
  • Sobol: first-order and total indices on the design of Saltelli, with bootstrap intervals (SobolResult).
  • PolynomialChaos: a Legendre expansion of F(x), its leave-one-out error, its Sobol indices and predict as a surrogate (ChaosResult); the number of terms is checked before any run.
  • SimulationPlotter.plot_prcc, plot_morris and plot_sobol.
  • ProfileLikelihood(parameters, threshold, max_steps): the profile of each parameter, refitted with the problem's own optimizer at values that step away from the fit by the adaptive step of Raue et al. (2009), its pointwise interval and its verdict (identifiable, practically_non_identifiable, structurally_non_identifiable), in a ProfileResult; ProfileResult.report() gives the verdicts as an IdentifiabilityReport with a profile section. A profile is read by resetting the other parameters to their fitted values (ProfileResult.structure), against the floor of two evaluations (ProfileResult.evaluation_floor): it gives the structural verdict in_combination or non_identifiable, and names the parameters that compensate it. A crossing made by the bound of another parameter counts as an open side (Profile.box_crossings), and Profile.refit_error measures the error of a refit at the fit. See Profile Likelihood.
  • PredictionProfile(specs, threshold): the interval of each prediction (PredictionSpec), held at each value as an equality constraint by an augmented Lagrangian. See Prediction profiles.
  • Threshold.chi_square(level) (observation models), Threshold.beale(level) (a sum of squares of independent Gaussian errors) and Threshold.bootstrap_calibrated(bootstrap, level) (any loss, calibrated by the replicates of a bootstrap).
  • SimulationPlotter.plot_profiles.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Nelder-Mead with an infinite bound fails with the message Nelder-Mead needs finite bounds, instead of a rate that is not a number. The sine transform of the bounds and the root finder of the quantiles come from the argmin fork; calibrations, profiles, quantiles and draws give the same results.
  • Breaking: EtaCalibration.information_matching(block_length) takes a required block_length, an int or "auto": the variance of the scores is summed over blocks of positions, as the meat of Sandwich, so it holds under dependence; block_length=1 gives the independent version. It also takes a problem with observation models, where a correct model gives η ≈ 1.
  • Breaking: Predictive(source, sample, positions) takes a Calibrator or a SensitivityAnalysis (any PredictiveSource), and its attribute calibrator is now source. Predictive.at_observations of an analysis takes only NoNoise(), and scores.log_score refuses its predictive.
  • With a stochastic engine, every replicate of every draw of a Predictive, of Predictive.at_observations and of scores.log_score has a seed of its own, derived from the calibrator's seed; before, every draw ran the same replicates of the problem, so a predictive with few replicates showed the same few noise paths for every draw. The bands and scores of a stochastic predictive change; a seed still repeats them.
  • Breaking: ModelStructure.check_calibration_values(model, engine, parameters, remainder) takes the values and the remainder instead of a calibration problem; a model kind that implements it changes its signature.
  • A prior whose family does not fit its bounds is named "The distribution ... of" in its message, instead of "The prior ... of".
  • The starts of Calibrator.run(starts=n) come from the Latin hypercube of commol-random; a seed gives the same starts as before.
  • Breaking: an Aggregate states the initial amount of each bin in the unit of the bin, not fractions of one total. A structure that states total, bin_fractions or compartment_fractions is rejected with the fields to use.
Before Now Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"S": 0.99, "I": 0.01}) Aggregate(bin_amounts={"S": 990, "I": 10}) compartment_fractions={"I_g1": 0.005} (of the total) compartment_amounts={"I_g1": 5} (in the unit of its bin) model.structure.total No declared total: sum(model.structure.bin_amounts.values()) for bins of one unit update_bin_fractions({...}), which kept the sum at 1 update_bin_amounts({...}); the other bins keep their amounts update_compartment_fractions(process, {...}) update_compartment_amounts(process, {...}) stratification_fractions Unchanged: the split of the amount of every bin a stratification applies to
  • Breaking: a calibrated initial condition of a bin, a bin prefix or a compartment is an amount in the unit of its bin, not a fraction of the total; its bounds are amounts too. A category value is still a split. The remainder takes the sum of the amounts the model states less every other compartment, so a bin that no value covers keeps its amount; with a bin left None, the remainder holds the sum ({"S": 1000, "I": None}). Without a remainder no initial state is infeasible. A remainder below zero is measured as a share of the amounts the values set. The write-back updates the amount of a bin only when the values and the remainder set every compartment of it.
  • Breaking: applied_parameters_report gives an aggregate model the sections initial_amounts (amount, unit, calibrated) and category_splits (group, a list of categories, fraction, calibrated) in place of initial_conditions, with no total row. A category split is reported as the fraction of its group, with no rescaling of its interval.
  • Breaking: a stochastic engine needs a whole amount in each bin, not a whole total, and largest_remainder and random round within each bin, so a unit never moves to another bin.
  • Breaking: the description of an aggregate model shows the bin amounts and their units, and the initial state with the unit of each compartment.
  • Breaking (Rust): InitialConditions has bin_amounts and compartment_amounts in place of total, bin_fractions and compartment_fractions; CompartmentalEngine::total is the sum of the amounts the model states; check_model_values returns the plan it resolves, and InitialConditionPlan::coverage gives the compartments each value sets.
  • Breaking: CalibrationProblem.loss_function has no default: a problem needs loss_function or observation_models, exactly one, and raises a ValueError with both or neither. Write loss_function="sse" where a problem relied on the default.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The finite-difference step of a parameter with an infinite bound was infinite, so its sensitivities, identifiability and curvature failed: the width of its bounds now counts as 1 in the step.
  • The quantile of a distribution hundreds of orders of magnitude below 1, such as Beta(0.01, 1) at 1e-3, was far from it, so a prior or a draw of such a shape was wrong: when its Newton and halving steps run out, the quantile now bisects the floating-point numbers between the two ends.
  • A particle swarm whose first particle had a NaN cost kept no best particle and returned its start point: a NaN cost now counts as the worst.

This release replaces the ensemble calibration with uncertainty methods that have a stated meaning. Calibrator.uncertainty resamples the data (bootstraps and the jackknife) and returns a ParameterSample; a Predictive runs its draws, and commol.scores scores its bands. Calibrator.identifiability tells which parameters the model and the data determine, and Calibrator.run(starts=n) fits from several start points. Before you upgrade, read the Breaking entries: the ensemble calibration is removed (use BayesianBootstrap in its place), and every interval uses one quantile, so the intervals of member_statistics and SimulationReplicates.quantiles move slightly. See Uncertainty and Resampling.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Calibrator.run(starts=n) runs the optimizer from n start points in parallel and returns the best: the initial guess, then rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds drawn from the problem's seed. CalibrationResult.starts lists every start (StartSummary: start, end, loss, converged); distinct ends with equal losses show that the data do not identify the parameters. See Several starts.
  • CalibrationResult.failed_runs: why each failed start failed, also logged as a warning.
  • ParameterSample: weighted draws of the parameters of a problem, with their invariants checked at construction and weighted statistics computed in Rust (mean, covariance, correlation, quantiles, interval, effective_size, draws, resample, summary). It saves to JSON and loads back equal.
  • Predictive(calibrator, sample, positions): the run of every draw, in parallel, its band (band, series_band) and every draw's value of a set of observations through the observation operator of the loss, with an observation noise that has no default (at_observations(observed_data, noise): NoNoise() for a band of the model, ResidualNoise(...) for a prediction interval). SimulationPlotter and simulation_report take a predictive.
  • commol.scores: empirical coverage, interval score, weighted interval score, the CRPS of a weighted sample and PIT values of a predictive, per observation and per series. Each takes the observation noise, so a band of the model is never scored as a prediction interval by accident.
  • Calibrator.uncertainty(method): one entry point for every uncertainty method. A method's configuration subclasses UncertaintyMethod[R] and registers its runner; the result type follows the configuration's type.
  • Calibrator.identifiability(method): which parameters the model and the data determine, and which combinations they determine in their place. StructuralRank (the rank of the sensitivities at random points, on the design of the observations or a dense one), Collinearity (Brun's indices at a fit or over a sample), SampleIdentifiability (contraction, correlations and modes of a sample) and StartsIdentifiability (starts of equal loss that end apart). Each returns an IdentifiabilityReport with a structural and a practical verdict per parameter; merge joins reports and identifiability_report gives one as plain data. See Identifiability.
  • InferenceMethod[R], the common base of UncertaintyMethod[R] and IdentifiabilityMethod[R]; each entry point refuses the other kind with a TypeError.
  • weighted_quantiles, and a weights argument for member_statistics.
  • CalibrationHistory and CalibrationEvaluation, returned by Calibrator.run_with_history().
  • The crate commol-inference: the parameter sample, the one quantile, the predictive and the scores. See Uncertainty.
  • Resampling methods with no noise model, through Calibrator.uncertainty: BayesianBootstrap, ResidualBootstrap and WildBootstrap return a BootstrapResult (the fit, one draw per replicate, diagnostics, and the Monte Carlo error of each interval bound, interval_error); BlockJackknife returns a JackknifeResult (estimate, bias, standard error, pseudo-values and the influence of each block). Blocks of consecutive positions span every series; block_length is an integer or "auto" (Politis and White). See Resampling.
  • ResidualNoise: observation noise made of blocks of residuals of a fit, which gives a prediction interval with no noise model; NoNoise gives a band of the model.
  • CalibrationProblem::with_data (Rust): a copy of a problem with other observed values and weights.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The latest version of the documentation site is the documentation of the last release, published from its tag; the dev version follows main.
  • Breaking: every interval uses one quantile: the weighted inverse of the empirical distribution between the midpoints of the cumulative weights, NumPy's method="hazen" with equal weights. member_statistics and SimulationReplicates.quantiles used NumPy's linear; their intervals move slightly.
  • Breaking: CalibrationResult.best_parameters keeps the order of CalibrationProblem.parameters.
  • Breaking: Calibrator.run_with_history() returns a CalibrationHistory instead of the extension's object.
  • Breaking: applied_parameters_report(..., sample=, confidence_level=) reads the statistics of a ParameterSample; parameter_statistics is gone.
  • Breaking (Rust): CalibrationProblem is split into layers (ForwardModel, ObservationOperator, Feasibility, Discrepancy, OptimizationObjective); optimize takes the problem by reference, and the optimizer configurations have no verbose field. CalibrationEvaluation has no predictions.
  • A verbose optimizer writes its table to Python's sys.stdout only, and needs one start; the library never writes to the standard error.
  • A rate, a formula parameter or a constraint that the expression compiler cannot compile, such as typeof(k), is rejected when the model or the calibration problem is built, with the reason; it no longer fails when it is evaluated.
  • The functions erf, erfc, tgamma, lgamma, j0, j1, y0, y1, fdim and remainder of a rate come from the libm crate, so they give the same values on every platform; the other functions still come from the system's math library.
  • AxisPattern is abstract: AxisPattern() raises TypeError. Build a pattern with one of its class methods.
  • Error messages that list ids (the stratifications of a transition, the missing and extra keys of the fractions of an Aggregate) list them in sorted order.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Several starts of Nelder-Mead began at the same point: each start now comes from the run seed.
  • A parameter value could land on another parameter when results were read by name from an unordered mapping.
  • A failed run of a multi-start optimization was written to the standard error and dropped; it is now part of the result.
  • An error of the model at a vertex of the initial Nelder-Mead simplex made the optimizer panic; it now stops the calibration with its message (the argmin fork returns the error).
  • A to condition on a transition without a source was ignored by its flow but applied by its accumulators; build now rejects it, and a category condition chooses the compartment the flow enters.
  • Model.from_json read a file in the encoding of the system; it now reads UTF-8, the encoding of JSON.
  • Model.check_unit_consistency checked every flow of a category transition in the unit of the first bin of the model; each flow is now checked in the unit of its own bin. In a model of bins of different units, a rate that reads total, a subgroup total, a category or neighbors fails the check: these add amounts of different units.
  • The LaTeX description wrote a part of a rate in parentheses, such as (I / N) or the argument of sin(t / T), as upright text, and wrote a unit inside the name of another variable (A_{g1(\text{item})}); only units are text now, each after its variable. The expanded form merges k * p and k * (1 - p) also when a third term shares another factor, and a merged term keeps the place of its first term.
  • ModelBuilder and Simulation logged to the root logger of the application; they log to the commol logger, as the rest of the library does, so add_stderr_logger shows their messages.
  • AxisPattern.combine(mode="max") raised "Unknown combine mode": a mode may be given by its value.
  • A quantile level outside [0, 1], or NaN, gave the smallest or the largest value; ParameterSample.quantiles and weighted_quantiles now raise ValueError.
  • AxisPattern.from_formula and AxisPattern.combine with a config that allows formulas longer than the default rejected them anyway; the configuration now applies.
  • A rate of StochasticSteps that is not a number raised InfeasibleStateError and said that a rate cannot be negative; it now raises RuntimeError, as StochasticEvents does, and says that the rate is not a number.
  • A rate that is not a number gave amounts that are not numbers in DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations, and a calibration only penalized the run; the run now stops with RuntimeError that names the flow and the position, as in the stochastic engines.
  • A rate that read an id with digits, such as e1, E2 or c1star, was rejected as a malformed number; and the exponent of a number such as 1e1 was read as the undefined variable e1. An identifier now starts only after a character that is not a letter, a digit or _, so the digits of an id belong to its name and an exponent belongs to its number.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• commol.api.model_loader.ModelLoader: a copy of Model.from_json that no page documented and nothing called.
  • Breaking: the ensemble calibration: Calibrator.run_probabilistic, ProbabilisticCalibrator, CalibrationProblem.probabilistic_config, ProbabilisticCalibrationConfig, ProbabilisticCalibrationResult, EnsembleSolution, EnsembleSelectionSummary, ParameterSetStatistics and their settings classes. Its intervals had no statistical meaning: its members were points the optimizer visited, and the selection maximized the coverage of the data it was fitted to. The closest replacement with no noise model is Calibrator.uncertainty(BayesianBootstrap(replicates=..., block_length=...)): the same parallel fits, each on randomly weighted data, with a stated meaning.
  • The dependency on scikit-learn.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Model.describe(layout="default") returns a ModelDescription: the model as data, sections of tables, equations, state graphs and text, for every kind of model. render(format) gives text, Markdown (with the state graph as a Mermaid diagram), a LaTeX document, JSON or Graphviz DOT, and save(path) writes it in the format of the suffix (.txt, .md, .tex, .json, .dot). In a notebook it shows as Markdown. See Describing a Model.
  • layout="odd": the description follows the ODD protocol for describing individual- and agent-based models (Grimm et al. 2006, 2010, 2020), and marks what commol cannot fill "To be written by the modeller.".
  • EngineType.dynamics_form and EngineType.schedule: how an engine advances (difference_equation, differential_equation, stochastic_events, rules), as a description shows it.
  • The process of a model apart from its structure: Model.process (Process: bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is written once, and Model.structure lays it out. Aggregate is the structure of amounts per compartment, the kind aggregate.
  • neighbors_<bin> and neighbors in a transition rate: the amount of a bin among the neighbors of a unit and their total. A rate that reads them and no compartment is proportional. Aggregate(neighbors=Complete()) makes every unit a neighbor of every other; Groups(stratification, weights) makes units neighbors by the categories of a stratification. A rate that reads them needs neighbors, with no default.
  • Variants of a structure: a subclass with the same kind, fields and engines, saved with its variant and loaded back as its own class.
  • Seeds and replicates for stochastic engines: Simulation.run(…, seed=) and run_at(…, seed=) (SimulationResults.seed keeps the seed, drawn when none is given), Simulation.replicates(n, seed=) with run and run_at that return SimulationReplicates (runs in parallel, one seed each; mean, quantiles, member_statistics), Simulation.is_stochastic, and EngineType.is_stochastic. SimulationPlotter draws the mean and a band of replicates, and simulation_report takes them as ensemble_runs.
  • CalibrationProblem(replicates=…, replicate_summary=…) calibrates a stochastic engine with common random numbers: "mean", "median", Quantile(q) or "crps" (the continuous ranked probability score). A stochastic engine needs them and a seed; there is no default summary.
  • The crate commol-random: a portable generator (Xoshiro256PlusPlus), the derivation of replicate seeds, samplers and a sum tree of rates, for every stochastic engine.
  • Two stochastic engines of an aggregate model, in the crate commol-stochastic, that run the process of any model as whole units moved at random, with no change to it: "StochasticEvents" (continuous time: Gillespie's direct method, exact also when a rate reads t, or method="tau_leaping") and "StochasticSteps" (the chain binomial, with per-step probabilities). Their settings are StochasticEventsSettings and StochasticStepsSettings. A total must be whole, and initial amounts that are not whole need rounding="largest_remainder" or "random", with no default. A per-step probability outside [0, 1], or probabilities out of one compartment that sum to more than 1, raise InfeasibleStateError. See Stochastic Simulation.
  • The dynamics section of a stochastic model is an event table: each flow, the change of one event and its propensity or its draw; the schedule section lists the settings of the engine.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: a model is built from a process and a structure. ModelBuilder writes the process, and build(structure, engine, settings=None) joins it with a structure; the model is a Model of the class of the structure.
Before Now builder.set_initial_conditions(total=…, bin_fractions=[{"bin": "A", "fraction": 0.9}, …], stratification_fractions=[…], compartment_fractions=[…]) then builder.build(engine=…) builder.build(Aggregate(total=…, bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, …}, stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, …}}, compartment_fractions={"A_g1": 0.0}), engine=…) CompartmentalStructure, Model[CompartmentalStructure] Aggregate, Model[Aggregate] model.structure.bins, stratifications, transitions, accumulators model.process.bins, … model.structure.initial_conditions.total, bin_fractions, … model.structure.total, bin_fractions, … (mappings by id) model.structure.initial_state(), subgroup_total(…), get_conditioning_categories(…), update_compartment_fractions(…) The same methods, with the process first: model.structure.initial_state(model.process), … model.structure.update_initial_conditions(…) model.structure.update_bin_fractions(…) model.structure.outputs_by_source(), series_label(id) outputs_by_source(model), series_label(model, id) CompartmentFraction, BinFraction, StratificationFraction(s) Mappings in Aggregate CompartmentalEngineType EngineName
  • Breaking: the model file has process and structure, the structure has kind: "aggregate" and variant, and the fractions are objects keyed by id. A file of 0.3 does not load; rebuild the model and save it again.
  • Breaking: an engine names a method, not a kind: EngineType.kinds replaces EngineType.kind, and the error of an engine that does not run a kind lists the engines of that kind.
  • Breaking: neighbors and the names that start with neighbors_ are reserved: no parameter, bin or accumulator may take them.
  • EngineType.equation_lhs comes from the form of the dynamics of the engine (DynamicsForm in Rust), and returns None for an engine without equations.
  • Python names follow PEP 8: ruff checks them (N rules).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • The unit check reads the flows the engine plans, so a proportional rate is checked as its flow, the rate times its source: k2 in 1/day from a bin in item passes as item/day instead of failing as 1/day.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Breaking: Model.print_equations, ModelStructure.print_equations and PrintEquationsOutputFormat. model.describe().render("text") shows the same compact and expanded forms, and render("latex") writes them in LaTeX; a description with some units missing shows none instead of raising.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• An ODE engine: a model built with engine="DifferentialEquations" runs in continuous time, dX/dt = Σ flows, integrated by diffsol (commol-differential). It has the same flows, outputs, accumulators, calibration, ensembles, reports and plots as a difference model. On [n, n + 1) a rate sees step = n and the continuous t. The engine restarts its integration at each integer when a rate reads step, and where t reaches a value a rate compares it with (t >= t_on), so the solver cannot step over a jump.
  • OdeSolver (method "tsit45" or "bdf", rtol, atol), the settings of the DifferentialEquations engine, stored in the model as Model.engine.settings and set with build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...).
  • One list of engines in the Rust engine (EngineType): each entry names the model kind it runs, validates its settings, and says the form of its equations and what a rate means (per_step or continuous). Python asks it through commol_rs.engine.EngineType instead of branching on engine names.
  • Simulation.run_at(at): the outputs at the given sorted positions. A differential model takes any position, such as 0.5.
  • SimulationResults: what Simulation.run and run_at return. A dict from output name to values, as before, with the positions in positions and the rows in rows().
  • The window grid as module functions: window_start, window_end, window_index and window_ends, beside windowed_totals.
  • A public Pydantic class rejects an unknown field and names it (extra="forbid" on every class of commol.__all__), so a misspelt or an old name is an error instead of being dropped.
  • Impulses: add_transition(..., impulse_at=[...]) or impulse_every=(period, offset) moves the rate (a fraction or an amount) at once at those steps, in both engines, before the flows of the step. print_equations lists impulses apart.
  • ModelBuilder(..., step_unit=...) (Model.step_unit): the unit of one step for the unit check, of any single dimension: the axis is the independent variable of the model, which need not be time (for example "meter"). Without it, the step unit is step, the default increment of any axis.
  • AxisUnits(step_unit, engine) and Model.axis_units(): steps(value, unit) converts a value in any unit of the step dimension to steps on pint (3 day with a step of hour is 72.0; 2 km with a step of m is 2000.0), and raises, naming both units, for a unit of another dimension. rate_from_mean_span(span, unit) and rate_from_probability(probability, period, unit) ask the engine what a rate means: the per-step rate for DifferenceEquations (1 - exp(-1/n), 1 - (1 - p)^(1/n)) and the continuous rate for DifferentialEquations (1/n, -ln(1 - p)/n).
  • EngineType.rate_from_mean_span and rate_from_probability in the engine's list (RateMeaning in Rust), which hold those formulas.
  • The unit check reads if(condition, a, b): both branches share a unit.
  • One interface for every kind of model: ModelStructure, an abstract base class that the structure of each kind inherits. Simulation, Calibrator, ProbabilisticCalibrator, the reports and SimulationPlotter use only it, so another kind (for example an agent network) is a new subclass with its engines in the engine's list. CompartmentalStructure is the structure of a compartmental model. A subclass that misses a method cannot be made, and the error names the method.
  • An engine runs one model kind, and a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine and both kinds.
  • Each kind declares the values calibration may set besides parameter and factor (ModelStructure.calibration_value_types); a compartmental model accepts initial_condition. A type the kind does not accept raises an error that names the kind.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: a DifferenceEquations step that leaves a compartment below zero (by more than 10⁻¹² of the total) raises InfeasibleStateError, a ValueError. The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows out of it. Before, the run went on with negative amounts. A calibration gives such a run a penalty and goes on; any other error of a run still stops it. See Amounts below zero.
  • Breaking (Rust): SimulationEngine::run_at_positions_into_buffer, run_at, run and step return SimulationError (Infeasible or Failed) instead of String.
  • A position on the axis is a float everywhere, and the engine alone decides which positions its model type accepts: a difference model integer steps, a differential model any non-negative position. Its error names the observation, constraint, impulse transition or series parameter that holds a rejected position. The engine trait runs only at positions (run_at_positions_into_buffer); run(n) returns the grid it ran on.
  • The engine of a model and its settings are one field, Model.engine = {type, settings} (ModelEngine), which replaces Model.dynamics.typology. The builder takes the engine where it builds, so one builder builds the model for each engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both. A model file saved before has dynamics.typology and does not load: move it to "engine": {"type": …, "settings": null}.
Before Now builder.build(typology="DifferenceEquations") builder.build(engine="DifferenceEquations") model.dynamics.typology model.engine.type commol_rs.difference.DifferenceEquations(model), commol_rs.differential.DifferentialEquations(model) commol_rs.engine.Engine(model), the engine the model names - A model is a header, an engine and a structure: Model.structure, tagged in JSON by kind, replaces Model.population and Model.dynamics, and the transitions are held once. Model is generic in its structure class: ModelBuilder.build returns Model[CompartmentalStructure], and Model.from_json reads the class from the kind. The methods that only a compartmental model has moved to its structure. A model file saved before has population and dynamics and does not load: move the fields of population and dynamics.transitions into "structure": {"kind": "compartmental", …}. Before Now model.population.bins, .accumulators, .stratifications, .initial_conditions model.structure.bins, … model.dynamics.transitions (and model.population.transitions) model.structure.transitions model.initial_state() model.structure.initial_state() model.update_initial_conditions(…), update_stratification_fractions(…), update_compartment_fractions(…) model.structure.update_initial_conditions(…), … model.subgroup_population(…), model.get_conditioning_categories(…) model.structure.subgroup_total(…), model.structure.get_conditioning_categories(…) model.get_outputs_by_source() model.structure.outputs_by_source() model.get_uncalibrated_initial_conditions() model.structure.uncalibrated_values() commol.context.dynamics (Transition, StratifiedRate) commol.context.transition commol.context.engine.EngineType CompartmentalEngineType; ModelEngine.type is a str that the engine's list checks commol_rs.core.Model(population=…, dynamics=…) commol_rs.core.Model(structure=commol_rs.core.CompartmentalStructure(…)) commol_rs.model.initial_state(model), expanded_outputs, transition_flows they take a commol_rs.core.CompartmentalStructure commol_rs.calibration.check_initial_conditions check_model_values commol_rs.calibration.calibrate(…, initial_population_size, …) and the other calibration functions no initial_population_size: the engine knows it
  • applied_parameters_report returns parameters and the sections of the kind of the model; a compartmental model adds initial_conditions, with the same keys as before.
  • The Rust engine trait (SimulationEngine) is the same for every model kind: compartments, state (was population), set_initial_condition and output_labels moved to CompartmentalEngine (commol-model), and the engine resolves and writes the values of its kind (plan_values, apply_values). The initial-condition plan moved from commol-calibration to commol-model. The crates are not published.
  • Names of positions, lengths and counts, and names with more than one meaning. No old name is kept; an old keyword raises an error that names it.
Before Now ObservedDataPoint(step=…) ObservedDataPoint(at=…) ObservedDataPoint(window_steps=…) ObservedDataPoint(window=…) ObservedDataPoint(compartment="B") ObservedDataPoint(output="B") ObservedDataPoint(compartment="label", compartments=[…]) ObservedDataPoint(label="label", outputs=[…]) ObservedDataPoint(scale_id=…) ObservedDataPoint(factor_id=…) CalibrationParameter(parameter_type="scale"), CalibrationParameterType.SCALE "factor", CalibrationParameterType.FACTOR CalibrationConstraint(time_steps=…) CalibrationConstraint(at=…) NelderMeadConfig(initial_step=…) NelderMeadConfig(initial_simplex_size=…) Simulation.run_at(steps) Simulation.run_at(at) Simulation.windowed_totals(results, source_ids, window_steps, at_steps) Simulation.windowed_totals(results, ids, window, at) Simulation.total_series(results, source_ids), group_outputs(source_ids), outputs_for(source_id) ids, id windowed_totals(series, window_steps, at_steps) windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at) window_end_steps(window_steps, num_steps) window_ends(window, end) TimeScale.window_start, window_end, window_index commol.window_start, window_end, window_index simulation_report(…, steps, window_steps, …), series_report, accumulators_report, observed_report at, window SimulationPlotter.plot_series(step_to_label=…) position_label=…, which takes a float TimePattern (commol.api.time_patterns) AxisPattern (commol.api.patterns) TimePattern.window(start, end, amount) AxisPattern.interval(start, end, value) TimeSeriesValue, "time-series parameter" SeriesValue, "series parameter" EnsembleSolution.windowed_prediction_steps windowed_prediction_positions engine.current_step() engine.current_position() simulation.run(n, output_format="list_of_lists") simulation.run(n).rows()
  • Reports, windows, plots and ensemble statistics read a value at a position of the results, not at a list index, so a differential model windows and reports at non-integer positions once its results hold them. The report key scale_id is factor_id, and compartments is outputs.
  • EnsembleSolution has prediction_positions; its prediction series hold the unit grid and every observation position and window start.
  • Series parameters take (position, value) points with float positions. "linear" interpolates in t and "step_function" holds from any position; a differential engine restarts its integration at their points, so a "linear" series is a ramp, not a staircase. "pulse" keeps integer positions. A difference model gives the same results and rejects a point between integers.
  • AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp read t and take float bounds. A difference model gives the same results; in a differential model an interval opens at any position and a ramp is continuous.
  • A pattern parameter that the builder generates is named _series_<n> (was _ts_<n>).
  • The model compiler moved from commol-difference to the new crate commol-model, which both engines use; commol_rs.difference no longer has initial_state, expanded_outputs, transition_flows and check_names, which are in commol_rs.model. No public Python name changes.
  • SimulationPlotter.plot_series and plot_cumulative take series instead of bins. An entry is an output name or a bin or accumulator id; an id plots the sum of its outputs, so a bin of a stratified model can be plotted. There is no bins alias: rename the argument.
  • Every loss uses the observation weights the same way: "sse" is Σ w·r², "rmse" is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w) and "mae" is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. Before, "sse" squared the weight and "rmse" and "mae" ignored it. With every weight at 1 nothing changes. The ensemble central loss follows the same rule.
  • Simulation.run starts from the initial state at every call, so two calls give the same result. Before, a second run continued the first one. To continue a run, call simulation.engine.step().

  • Model.check_unit_consistency infers one step unit from the parameter units (day, week, step, …; step when there is none) and requires every flow to be exactly <bin unit>/<step unit>. A model in "1/step" now passes. Rates in two units of time, such as "1/day" and "1/week", are an error that names each parameter, because the engine converts nothing. Before, the check accepted any convertible unit and defaulted to day.

  • Nelder-Mead searches inside the bounds: it optimizes an unbounded coordinate and scores x = lo + (hi − lo)·(sin u + 1)/2. Its first simplex is set by NelderMeadConfig.initial_simplex_size (a fraction of each bound width, default 0.1), which replaces simplex_perturbation; there is no alias. Every Nelder-Mead result can change.

  • The library names what the compartments hold without assuming individuals: the state (the amount of every compartment), the amount (the value of one compartment), the total (their sum, which the initial fractions are taken of) and a subgroup total (the sum of the compartments with some categories). The total is a float, finite and greater than 0, so a model of a mass or a concentration can be stated; before, it was an int. The rate variable N is total and N_<cat>… is total_<cat>…, so N is a free id (a bin may be named N). AxisPattern takes a value. No old name is kept: a model file with population_size does not load, and the error names the field; rename it to total, and N to total in every rate, formula and constraint.

Before Now set_initial_conditions(population_size=…), InitialConditions.population_size: int, JSON key population_size set_initial_conditions(total=…), InitialConditions.total: float, JSON key total Rate, formula and constraint variables N, N_<cat>… (N_g1, N_g1_t1) total, total_<cat>… (total_g1, total_g1_t1) RESERVED_VARIABLE_NAMES = ("N", …) ("total", "step", "t", "pi", "e") InitialConditions.subgroup_population(…), CompartmentalStructure.subgroup_population(…) subgroup_total(…) InitialCompartment.population InitialCompartment.amount applied_parameters_report: row "N", group "population" row "total", group "total" AxisPattern.pulse(at, amount), pulses(at, amount), periodic(period, amount, offset), interval(start, end, amount) value instead of amount get_predefined_variable_units(stratifications, bin_unit) get_predefined_variable_units(subgroup_totals, bin_unit), with the names the engine gives commol_rs.engine.Engine.population Engine.state commol_rs.core.InitialConditions(population_size=…) InitialConditions(total=…) commol_rs.calibration.calibrated_initial_population calibrated_initial_state — commol_rs.model.subgroup_total_names(structure) Rust: CompartmentalEngine::population, population_size; DifferenceEquations::population, DifferentialEquations::population state, total
  • The library and its documentation assume no application and no axis: text says "along the axis" or "position", not "over time", and examples use abstract names. A rate that names no compartment is proportional (was "per-capita"), because a source can hold a mass or a concentration. The errors of a constraint at positions say "Constraint '…' evaluation failed at position …" and "Position … not found …" (were "Time-dependent constraint" and "Time step").
Before Now AxisPattern.seasonal(amplitude, period, phase, baseline) AxisPattern.sinusoid(amplitude, period, phase, baseline) TransitionFlow.per_capita_of (commol.context._model.engine_state) TransitionFlow.proportional_to Guide anchor #absolute-and-per-capita-rates #absolute-and-proportional-rates Guide anchor #time-dependent-rates #rates-that-change-along-the-axis
  • The unit check no longer infers the step unit from the parameter units: it is the declared step_unit or else step. A model with rates in 1/day and no step_unit fails the check, and the message says to declare it: add step_unit="day" to ModelBuilder.
  • A unit means what pint defines. The list of time aliases (decade, quarter, semester, mo, wk, …) is gone: pint reads quarter as a mass and decade as a number, so 1/quarter was a mass without error. A name that pint does not define is a unit of its own dimension.
  • In the unit check, t has the step unit (it is a position on the axis), and a number written beside it in a sum, a difference or a comparison is read in that unit. step stays dimensionless. A rate such as sin(2 * pi * t / 365) now fails the check; write sin(2 * pi * t / period) with period in the step unit.
  • Guides and docstrings say what a rate means for each engine (What a rate means) instead of "every flow applies once per step".

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• TimeScale (commol.api.time_scale). Its rate conversions gave per-step rates only, which a differential model reads as too small.
Before Now TimeScale(step_seconds=3600), TimeScale.from_step_unit("hour") AxisUnits(step_unit="hour"), or model.axis_units() steps_from_seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks(x) steps(x, "second"), steps(x, "minute"), … steps_per_hour, steps_per_day, steps_per_week steps(1, "hour"), steps(1, "day"), steps(1, "week") rate_from_mean_duration(seconds) rate_from_mean_span(span, unit), which asks the engine rate_from_probability(p, period_steps) rate_from_probability(p, period, unit), which asks the engine window_start, window_end, window_index commol.window_start, window_end, window_index

steps returns a float and does not raise for a fraction of a step; the engine rejects a position it does not accept where the position is used.

  • Transition conditions: Transition.condition, the condition argument of ModelBuilder.add_transition, ModelBuilder.create_condition, the Condition and Rule types, and the LogicOperators and VariablePrefixes enums, in Python and in Rust. The engine never evaluated them, so a condition that was never true still moved population. Write the condition in the rate ("if(step > 30, k, 0)"), or use an AxisPattern or a stratified rate. A model file with a condition key raises an error that names it.
  • Simulation.run(..., output_format=...) and run_at(..., output_format=...): both return SimulationResults; use rows() for one row per position.
  • commol_core::integer_steps, SimulationEngine::run_into_buffer and run_at_steps_into_buffer; the Python checks that repeated the engine's rules on positions (check_steps_for_typology, the impulse check of Dynamics, the order check of Simulation.run_at).
  • The "weighted_sse" loss and LossConfig.weighted_sse(). Use "sse", which uses the weights.
  • commol.constants.ModelTypes. The names of the compartmental engines are the Literal commol.context.engine.CompartmentalEngineType.
  • Population and Dynamics, in Python (commol.context.population, commol.context.dynamics) and in Rust, and their PyO3 classes; the structure of a model is CompartmentalStructure.
  • Model.get_uncalibrated_initial_conditions, Model.initial_state, and the other methods of a compartmental model on Model: they are on model.structure (see Changed).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Examples 6 to 9 of the guide (examples.md) no longer go below zero. Example 6 writes the rate it describes, k2_max * B * max(0, 1 - C / capacity); Examples 7, 8 and 9 set per_compartment=True on flow_AB, so each compartment of A loses an amount computed from its own amount.

  • A differential model: on a piece of integration that ends where a rate jumps (a value t is compared with, a series point), the right-hand side sees t below the end. Before, the last solver step of the piece already saw the rate after the jump, so a rate of 0.5 that starts at 2.5 moved 3·10⁻⁸ of the state before 2.5.

  • CalibrationResult.converged is True only when the optimizer met its convergence test or target_cost. Before, every finished run reported True, also one that stopped at max_iterations.

  • Nelder-Mead from a start value of 0 builds a real simplex, and no longer stops at a bound where the clamped loss is flat. Before, the simplex was degenerate at 0, and could collapse on a bound and report converged=True.
  • The verbose Nelder-Mead run uses the configured simplex. Before, it always used a 10% perturbation.
  • Model.check_unit_consistency names every bin without a unit. Before, it failed with "'None' is not defined in the unit registry".
  • A Simulation follows its model: run and engine rebuild the engine when the model changed after the Simulation was created, for example with update_parameters or apply_calibration_parameters. Before, it used the old values, or failed with "Parameter index … not found" for a parameter that was None.
  • pi and e work in every transition rate, such as "pi * k * A". Before, outside a function argument, the simulation failed with "Variable 'pi' not found".
  • % (remainder) works as the only operator of a rate, as in "step % 7". Before, the rate was read as a parameter name.
  • A total_… variable that names no subgroup total, such as total_t1_g1 when group is declared before type, is a build error that lists the valid names. Before, a formula parameter or the engine gave it the value 0.
  • A bin or an accumulator id cannot be total, step, t, pi or e, and a bin cannot expand into a name that is also a total_<categories> subgroup total. Before, the engine variable hid such a bin, and the two sums shared one value.
  • A parameter id cannot be total, step, t, pi, e, an expanded compartment or a subgroup total. Before, only bin ids were rejected, and the parameter and the engine variable shared one value.
  • ModelBuilder.reset removes the accumulators, and ModelBuilder.clone copies them and the bin_unit. Before, reset kept the accumulators and a clone lost them.
  • An initial_condition id is resolved by the engine when the Calibrator or the ProbabilisticCalibrator is created. A category of a non-binary stratification now gives "needs a binary stratification" instead of "not found", and bin prefixes ("B_g1") and qualified categories ("group:g1") are accepted, as documented. Before, both were rejected as "not found".

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• The guide is rewritten and split into pages with one job each (building models, transitions, expressions, time patterns, units, simulations, and six calibration pages). Every example runs in CI, and every claim was checked against the engine. Behaviors that were described wrongly are now documented as they are, among them: a violated constraint replaces the loss with a penalty.
  • The API reference documents every public name, and Model, plotting and reports have their own pages.
  • The site publishes llms.txt and llms-full.txt for AI agents, and marks the pages of the dev version.
  • README.md presents Commol as a library for declarative dynamical modelling: the idea behind it, what it can model and its limits, an example that derives, calibrates and simulates a model, and links to the guides. The citation title is "Commol: High-Performance Declarative Dynamical Modelling in Python".
  • The package metadata on PyPI has the same description, and keywords and classifiers (Python versions, audience, topic, development status).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Per-compartment initial conditions: InitialConditions.compartment_fractions (Python and Rust) accepts overrides keyed by expanded compartment name, expressed as fractions of the total population and applied after the uniform expansion. Includes ModelBuilder.set_initial_conditions(compartment_fractions=...), Model.update_compartment_fractions, and Model.initial_state(), which returns each expanded compartment with its bin, categories and initial population as the engine builds it. The Rust engine is the single source of truth for the expansion and validates the overrides (unknown or repeated name, fraction outside 0.0..=1.0, total above population_size).
  • Rust commol_difference::initial_state and commol_calibration::calibrated_initial_population, exposed to Python. The calibration objective, the calibrated predictions and the model write-back share one implementation of how calibration values reach the engine.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: calibrated initial conditions no longer auto-calculate the last population-fraction value as the remainder of the population. The new CalibrationProblem.initial_condition_remainder names the compartment or bin that absorbs the difference; it is not calibrated and keeps its own split. Without it, values are applied as given and only an initial population above population_size is penalized. A single exact compartment, such as a composite state, can now be calibrated on its own.
  • Breaking: calibrated initial conditions are applied in fixed layers — bins, category splits, exact compartments, remainder — instead of in parameter order.
  • Breaking: a stratification category may be named with a qualified id (sex:female). A bare name that more than one stratification declares is rejected as ambiguous, in calibration and in update_stratification_fractions, and the report qualifies its rows. Category pairs come from the engine's compartment labels instead of parsing compartment names.
  • Breaking: get_category_fraction, subgroup_population and get_conditioning_categories resolve category ids like calibration: a qualified id (sex:female) selects its stratification and a bare name that more than one stratification declares raises instead of silently using the first one. get_conditioning_categories returns qualified ids for shared names.
  • Bin and bin-prefix initial-condition ids, and the remainder, resolve from the engine's compartment labels instead of name prefixes, so a bin A no longer covers the compartments of a bin A_x.
  • The Rust engine expands bins and accumulators in one function; the equation printer and unit checker use it (expanded_outputs) instead of their own Python expansion. The Rust ModelTypes gains DifferentialEquations, so any model definition can be expanded; the difference engine rejects it.
  • Breaking: update_bin_fractions / update_initial_conditions apply the same rule as construction: the bin fractions must sum to 1.0 after the update.

  • Breaking (Rust): SimulationEngine requires compartment_labels(). CalibrationProblem::fix_auto_calculated_parameters and get_parameter_fix_info are removed; applied_parameter_values returns the clamped values the objective scored, which is what results now report.

  • Breaking: transitions are planned by the Rust engine from compartment labels (bin and categories) instead of compartment names, in one planner shared by the simulation and print_equations. The printed equations are therefore the simulated ones: a per-capita rate is shown multiplied by its source (gamma * I), a transition without flows shows (no flows), and the compact form lists the flows of each transition.

  • Breaking: building a model rejects a stratified rate whose category conditions match no source compartment (use to to route into a stratification the source does not carry), a transition with several sources and a per-capita rate, a category transition without exactly one source and one target, and a flow that ends in categories no compartment has. These used to be skipped without notice.
  • Constraint aggregates (a bin or bin prefix in a constraint expression) are built from output labels, so a bin A no longer sums the outputs of a bin A_x.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• A transition between bins no longer moves bins whose id starts with the source bin id: A -> B moved AB -> BB as well.
  • Transitions between the categories of a stratification (young -> old) are now simulated; the engine used to ignore them while print_equations showed them.

  • A transition with several sources or targets (A + B -> 2 C) now applies its flow to every source and target, as documented; the engine used to move only the first source to the first target.

  • The applied-parameters report now shows the effective head count for bin, stratification-category, and subgroup rows — the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment_fractions overrides — and reports each fraction as that head count over the declared population_size, so every row shares one denominator with N. An aggregate row written back as overrides no longer reports the stale pre-calibration value as calibrated, and a bin left uncalibrated keeps its null marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

  • A conditional-stratification category is calibrated as a fraction of its conditioning subgroup but reported as a fraction of the whole population, so the report rescales its interval by the subgroup's share of the population; the interval now brackets the reported fraction.
  • apply_calibration_parameters writes initial-condition values back so the model rebuilds the initial population the engine scored for them. Bin and category values update the fractions they declare, as the engine applied them; every compartment those fractions do not reproduce is pinned as a per-compartment override. The call computes the result before it changes the model, so a rejected value leaves the model unchanged.
  • population_size must be greater than zero, reported as a domain ValueError rather than a later ZeroDivisionError. update_bin_fractions re-applies the sum-to-1/conservation rule.
  • Calibrating a bare category name that two stratifications declare no longer builds an initial population larger than population_size: the engine used to split the overlapping pairs of both stratifications from one snapshot.
  • The PyO3 InitialConditions binding exposes population_size, bin_fractions, stratification_fractions and compartment_fractions with getters, and the _commol_rs stub declares only those real attributes (correcting the bin_fractions field name).
  • An initial-condition override that names an unknown compartment raises a ValueError when the model is built or updated, and a RuntimeError from the DifferenceEquations engine constructor.
  • The greedy ensemble search of probabilistic calibration takes its random starts from the shuffled part of the sample (argmin fork). The starts were biased towards low indices, so the same seed can now select a different ensemble.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial release of Commol
  • ModelBuilder fluent API for constructing compartment models

docs.title: Model Structure
docs.text:
Back to API Reference

A Model is a tree of Pydantic models. ModelBuilder creates it, Model.to_json writes it, and the Rust engine reads the same tree from JSON (crates/commol-core/src/types/). Most users never build these types by hand; read this page to understand model files or to work on Commol.

A model has a header, a process written once, a structure that lays the process out, and an engine that runs it. The process (bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is the same for every kind of model; the structure changes between kinds and is tagged in JSON by kind, and by variant for a narrower form of a structure. The kind today is aggregate: amounts per compartment.

Model                      name, description, version, step_unit
├── parameters: [Parameter]                (a value may be a SeriesValue)
├── engine: ModelEngine
│   ├── type: "DifferenceEquations", "DifferentialEquations",
│   │         "StochasticEvents" or "StochasticSteps"
│   └── settings: OdeSolver | StochasticEventsSettings | StochasticStepsSettings | None
│                                           (settings of that engine; None: its defaults)
├── process: Process
│   ├── bins: [Bin]
│   ├── accumulators: [Accumulator]
│   ├── stratifications: [Stratification]
│   │   └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
│   └── transitions: [Transition]          (impulse_at, impulse_every for impulses)
│       └── stratified_rates: [StratifiedRate]
│           └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
└── structure: Aggregate                   (kind: "aggregate", variant: None)
    ├── bin_amounts: {bin: amount | None}          (in the unit of the bin)
    ├── stratification_fractions: {stratification: {category: fraction}}
    ├── compartment_amounts: {compartment: amount}
    └── neighbors: Complete | Groups | None

In JSON the structure is an object with its kind, its variant and the fields of its class:

{
  "name": "Model",
  "parameters": [],
  "engine": {"type": "DifferenceEquations", "settings": null},
  "process": {"bins": [], "accumulators": [], "stratifications": [], "transitions": []},
  "structure": {
    "kind": "aggregate",
    "variant": null,
    "bin_amounts": {"A": 990.0, "B": 10.0},
    "stratification_fractions": {},
    "compartment_amounts": {},
    "neighbors": null
  },
  "step_unit": null
}

Model, Process, ModelStructure, Aggregate, Complete and Groups are documented in Model API. The engine must run the kind of the structure: a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine, both kinds and the engines of the kind of the model. A variant keeps the kind, the fields and the engines of its structure, and loads back as its own class (Design decisions).

class Stratification(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        List of the different stratification groups identifiers.
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied stratification categories satisfy ALL conditions.
        Compartments that do not satisfy the conditions are kept without
        appending this stratification's categories.

        May only reference stratifications declared before this one.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the stratification.")
    categories: list[str] = Field(
        default=...,
        description="List of the different stratification groups identifiers.",
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the stratification."
    )
    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Conditions on previously-declared stratifications that must be "
            "satisfied for this stratification to expand a compartment."
        ),
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Stratification) and self.id == other.id

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_length(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not empty.
        """
        if not self.categories:
            raise ValueError(
                (f"Stratification '{self.id}' must have at least one category.")
            )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_uniqueness(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not repeated.
        """
        categories_set = set(self.categories)

        if len(categories_set) != len(self.categories):
            duplicates = [
                item for item in categories_set if self.categories.count(item) > 1
            ]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Categories for stratification '{self.id}' must not be repeated. "
                    f"Found duplicates: {list(set(duplicates))}."
                )
            )

        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_conditions_have_categories(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that stratification expansion conditions filter by category.
        """
        if self.conditions is None:
            return self

        for condition in self.conditions:
            if condition.category is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    (
                        f"Condition for stratification '{self.id}' referencing "
                        f"'{condition.stratification}' must include a category. "
                        "Category-less conditions are only valid for transition "
                        "target overrides."
                    )
                )

        return self

class StratificationCondition(BaseModel):
    """
    Specifies a category within a stratification for rate matching.

    When ``to`` is set, the matched category in the source compartment is
    replaced with the ``to`` category in the target compartment name. This
    enables cross-category transitions within the same bin (e.g., from ``g1``
    to ``g2``).

    Attributes
    ----------
    stratification : str
        The ID of the stratification (e.g., "group", "type")
    category : str
        The category within that stratification (e.g., "g1", "t1")
    to : str | None
        Target category override. When set, the target compartment will use
        this category instead of the source compartment's category for this
        stratification.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    stratification: str = Field(default=..., description="ID of the stratification")
    category: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Category within the stratification. When None, the condition acts as a "
            "target-only override: it does not filter source compartments but still "
            "contributes a 'to' category to the computed target compartment name."
        ),
    )
    to: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Target category override. When set, the target compartment uses "
            "this category instead of the source's for this stratification."
        ),
    )

class Parameter(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a global model parameter.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        The identifier of the parameter.
    value : float | str | SeriesValue | None
        Value of the parameter. Can be:
        - float: A numerical constant value
        - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
               special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e), or contain
               mathematical expressions
        - SeriesValue: An empirical series evaluated via binary search
        - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the parameter.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "item").
        If None, the parameter has no unit specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the parameter.")
    value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = Field(
        default=...,
        description=(
            "Value of the parameter. Can be a float (constant), "
            "str (formula), SeriesValue (empirical series), "
            "or None (requires calibration)."
        ),
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the parameter."
    )
    unit: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Unit of the parameter (e.g., '1/day', 'dimensionless', 'item').",
    )

    @field_validator("value")
    @classmethod
    def validate_value(
        cls, value: float | str | SeriesValue | None
    ) -> float | str | SeriesValue | None:
        """Validate the parameter value."""
        if value is None or isinstance(value, SeriesValue):
            return value
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            return float(value)
        if not value.strip():
            raise ValueError("Formula cannot be empty")
        return value.strip()

    def is_calibrated(self) -> bool:
        """
        Check if the parameter has a value (is calibrated).

        Returns
        -------
        bool
            True if the parameter has a value, False if it needs calibration.
        """
        return self.value is not None

An empirical series for a parameter value.

Attributes:

Name Type Description data list[tuple[float, float]]

(position, value) points on the axis. Need not be pre-sorted; the engine sorts them.

mode str

How the series is read between its points: "pulse" (the value on the step of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only), "step_function" (the value of the last point at or before t), or "linear" (linear interpolation in t). class SeriesValue(BaseModel):
    """
    An empirical series for a parameter value.

    Attributes
    ----------
    data : list[tuple[float, float]]
        (position, value) points on the axis. Need not be pre-sorted; the
        engine sorts them.
    mode : str
        How the series is read between its points: ``"pulse"`` (the value on
        the step of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only),
        ``"step_function"`` (the value of the last point at or before ``t``),
        or ``"linear"`` (linear interpolation in ``t``). The engine decides
        which positions its model type accepts: a DifferenceEquations model
        only integer steps.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    data: list[tuple[float, float]]
    mode: str = Field(default="pulse", pattern="^(pulse|step_function|linear)$")

    @field_validator("data")
    @classmethod
    def validate_data(
        cls, value: list[tuple[float, float]]
    ) -> list[tuple[float, float]]:
        """Validate series points before they reach the Rust engine."""
        if not value:
            raise ValueError("Series data must contain at least one point")

        positions: list[float] = []
        for position, point_value in value:
            if not (math.isfinite(position) and position >= 0):
                raise ValueError("Series positions must be finite and non-negative")
            if not math.isfinite(point_value):
                raise ValueError("Series values must be finite")
            positions.append(position)

        if len(positions) != len(set(positions)):
            raise ValueError("Series positions must be unique")

        return value

Bases: BaseModel

Defines a rule for system evolution.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Id of the transition.

source list[str]

The origin compartments.

target list[str]

The destination compartments.

rate str | None

Default mathematical formula, parameter name, or constant value for the flow. Used when no stratified rate matches. Numeric values are automatically converted to strings during validation.

Operators: +, -, *, /, % (modulo), ^ or ** (power) Functions: sin, cos, tan, exp, ln, sqrt, abs, min, max, if, etc. Constants: pi, e

Note: Both ^ and ** are supported for exponentiation (** is converted to ^).

Examples: - "k1" (parameter reference) - "0.5" (constant, can also be passed as float 0.5) - "k1 * A * B / total" (mathematical formula) - "0.3 * sin(2 * pi * t / 365)" (formula that changes along the axis) - "2^10" or "2**10" (power: both syntaxes work)

stratified_rates list[StratifiedRate] | None

Stratification-specific rates. Each rate applies to compartments that match all specified stratification conditions.
