class CalibrationProblem(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a complete calibration problem.

    This class encapsulates all the information needed to calibrate model
    parameters against observed data. It provides validation of the calibration
    setup but delegates the actual optimization to the Rust backend.

    Attributes
    ----------
    observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
        List of observed data points to fit against
    parameters : list[CalibrationParameter]
        List of parameters to calibrate with their bounds
    constraints : list[CalibrationConstraint]
        List of constraints on calibration parameters (optional, default: empty list)
    loss_function : {"sse", "rmse", "mae"} | None
        The loss that measures the fit, with the observation weights. A
        problem has a loss or ``observation_models``, exactly one, with no
        default: what to fit is a modelling choice.
    observation_models : dict[str, ObservationModel] | None
        One observation model per series label (`NormalObservations`,
        `LogNormalObservations`, `StudentTObservations`,
        `PoissonObservations`, `NegativeBinomialObservations`,
        `BinomialObservations`): the problem fits by maximum likelihood, and
        its loss is the negative log-likelihood. Every observed series needs
        one, and every parameter of type ``"noise"`` must be an argument of
        one. It needs a deterministic engine.
    normalize_observations : bool
        When True, divide each residual by the RMS of its observation series
        before applying the loss metric (default: False). It needs a loss:
        observation models set the scale of each series with their noise.
    optimization_config : OptimizationConfig
        Configuration for the optimization algorithm
    initial_condition_remainder : str | None
        Expanded compartment or bin that absorbs the difference to the
        total once the calibrated initial conditions are applied
        (default: None). It is not calibrated itself. With a remainder, the
        sum of the initial amounts always equals ``total``; without one,
        calibrated initial conditions are applied as given and only a sum
        above ``total`` is penalized.
    replicates : int | None
        For a stochastic engine: how many replicates each evaluation runs,
        with common random numbers (the same seeds, derived from ``seed``, at
        every evaluation), so the loss is a deterministic function of the
        parameters. Required with a stochastic engine; a deterministic engine
        does not use it.
    replicate_summary : {"mean", "median", "crps"} | Quantile | None
        For a stochastic engine: what each observation is compared with. The
        mean, the median or a `Quantile` of the replicates, with
        ``loss_function``; or ``"crps"``, the continuous ranked probability
        score of their distribution, whose loss is the weighted mean score.
        Required with a stochastic engine, with no default: what to fit is a
        modelling choice.
    seed : int | None
        Seed of every random number of a calibration (default: None, a seed
        drawn from the operating system, which `Calibrator.run` logs):
        the replicates of a stochastic engine, the starts of
        ``Calibrator.run(starts=n)``, a particle swarm, and the uncertainty
        methods. Required with a stochastic engine.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint] = Field(
        default=..., min_length=1, description="Observed data points"
    )
    parameters: list[CalibrationParameter] = Field(
        default=..., min_length=1, description="Parameters to calibrate"
    )
    constraints: list[CalibrationConstraint] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Constraints on calibration parameters",
    )
    loss_function: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Loss function to use for measuring fit quality",
    )
    observation_models: dict[str, ObservationModel] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="One observation model per series label",
    )
    normalize_observations: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description=(
            "Normalize each residual by the RMS of its observation series before "
            "applying the loss metric. Keeps series measured on very different "
            "scales comparable in the loss."
        ),
    )
    optimization_config: NelderMeadConfig | ParticleSwarmConfig = Field(
        default=..., description="Optimization algorithm configuration"
    )
    initial_condition_remainder: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Expanded compartment or bin that absorbs the difference to the "
            "total once the calibrated initial conditions are applied."
        ),
    )
    replicates: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=1,
        description="Replicates per evaluation of a stochastic engine.",
    )
    replicate_summary: ReplicateSummary | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="What the observations are compared with, for a stochastic engine.",
    )
    seed: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=0,
        description=(
            "Seed of every random number of a calibration: the replicates of a "
            "stochastic engine, the starts, a particle swarm and the methods"
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("loss_function")
    @classmethod
    def validate_loss_function(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        if v is not None and v not in LossFunction:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid loss_function: {v}. Must be one of {list(LossFunction)}"
            )
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_loss_or_models(self) -> Self:
        """Require a loss or observation models, exactly one."""
        if self.loss_function is not None and self.observation_models is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "A problem has a loss_function or observation_models, not both: "
                "the fit and the posterior would answer different questions."
            )
        if self.loss_function is None and self.observation_models is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "A problem needs a loss_function (one of "
                f"{', '.join(LossFunction)}) or observation_models. There is no "
                "default: what to fit is a modelling choice."
            )
        if self.observation_models is not None and self.normalize_observations:
            raise ValueError(
                "normalize_observations needs a loss_function: the observation "
                "models set the scale of each series with their noise."
            )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_unique_parameter_ids(self) -> Self:
        """Ensure parameter IDs are unique."""
        param_ids = [p.id for p in self.parameters]
        if len(param_ids) != len(set(param_ids)):
            duplicates = [id for id in set(param_ids) if param_ids.count(id) > 1]
            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate parameter IDs found: {duplicates}")
        return self

Represents a single observed data point for calibration.

An observation compares one output, or the sum of several outputs, with an observed value at a position on the axis.

Attributes:

Name Type Description at float

Position of the observation on the axis. The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferentialEquations model any non-negative position, a DifferenceEquations model only an integer step.

output str | None

The output being observed. Give either output or outputs.

outputs list[str] | None

Outputs summed before comparing with this observation. Needs a label.

label str

Name of the observed series, used by reports, plots and the per-series normalization. Defaults to output.

value float

Observed value

weight float

How much this observation counts in the loss (default: 1.0). Every loss multiplies the squared or absolute residual by it: sse is Σ w·r², rmse is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w), mae is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. With observation models it is a power of the observation's likelihood, w·log p: a weight of 2 counts the observation twice.

factor_id str | None

Optional factor parameter ID that multiplies the model output before comparison

window float | None

Optional window length for a cumulative output: the prediction is the output at at minus the output at at - window.

trials int | None

The trials of this observation, for a BinomialObservations model with no trials of its own (default: None).

class ObservedDataPoint(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a single observed data point for calibration.

    An observation compares one output, or the sum of several outputs, with an
    observed value at a position on the axis.

    Attributes
    ----------
    at : float
        Position of the observation on the axis. The engine decides which
        positions its model type accepts: a DifferentialEquations model any
        non-negative position, a DifferenceEquations model only an integer
        step.
    output : str | None
        The output being observed. Give either `output` or `outputs`.
    outputs : list[str] | None
        Outputs summed before comparing with this observation. Needs a
        `label`.
    label : str
        Name of the observed series, used by reports, plots and the
        per-series normalization. Defaults to `output`.
    value : float
        Observed value
    weight : float
        How much this observation counts in the loss (default: 1.0). Every
        loss multiplies the squared or absolute residual by it: ``sse`` is
        ``Σ w·r²``, ``rmse`` is ``√(Σ w·r² / Σ w)``, ``mae`` is
        ``Σ w·|r| / Σ w``. With observation models it is a power of the
        observation's likelihood, ``w·log p``: a weight of 2 counts the
        observation twice.
    factor_id : str | None
        Optional factor parameter ID that multiplies the model output before
        comparison
    window : float | None
        Optional window length for a cumulative output: the prediction is the
        output at `at` minus the output at ``at - window``.
    trials : int | None
        The trials of this observation, for a `BinomialObservations` model
        with no ``trials`` of its own (default: None).
    """

    at: float = Field(
        default=..., ge=0, allow_inf_nan=False, description="Position on the axis"

    output: str | None = Field(

    )
    value: float = Field(default=..., ge=0.0, description="Observed value")
    weight: float = Field(
        default=1.0,
        gt=0.0,
        description="Weight for this observation in the loss function",
    )
    factor_id: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Optional factor parameter ID that multiplies the model output",
    )
    window: float | None = Field(
        default=None,
        gt=0,
        allow_inf_nan=False,
        description=(
            "Optional window length for cumulative-output observations. "
            "When set, prediction is value(at) - value(at - window)."

    )
    trials: int | None = Field(
        default=None,
        ge=0,
        description="Trials of a binomial observation model that reads them here",

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_observed_outputs(self) -> Self:
        """Require one of `output` and `outputs`; name the series."""
        if (self.output is None) == (self.outputs is None):
            raise ValueError("Give exactly one of 'output' and 'outputs'.")
        if self.outputs is not None:
            if not self.outputs:
                raise ValueError("outputs must be non-empty when provided")
            if not self.label:
                raise ValueError(
                    "An observation of several outputs needs a 'label' that names "
                    "their sum."
                )
        elif not self.label:
            self.label = self.output or ""
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_window(self) -> Self:
        """A window must not start before position 0."""
        if self.window is not None and self.window > self.at:
            raise ValueError(f"window ({self.window}) must be <= at ({self.at})")
        return self

    @property
    def observed_outputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """The outputs whose sum is compared: `outputs`, or `output` alone."""
        return list(self.outputs) if self.outputs is not None else [self.output or ""]

class CalibrationParameter(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a parameter or initial condition to be calibrated with its bounds.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier (parameter ID for parameters, bin ID for initial conditions)
    parameter_type : str
        Type of value being calibrated
    min_bound : float
        Minimum allowed value for this parameter
    max_bound : float
        Maximum allowed value for this parameter
    initial_guess : float | None
        Optional starting value for optimization (if None, midpoint is used)
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(
        default=..., min_length=1, description="Parameter or bin identifier"
    )
    parameter_type: str = Field(
        default=...,
        description="Type of value being calibrated",
    )
    min_bound: float = Field(default=..., description="Minimum allowed value")
    max_bound: float = Field(default=..., description="Maximum allowed value")
    initial_guess: float | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Optional starting value for optimization"
    )

    @field_validator("parameter_type")
    @classmethod
    def validate_parameter_type(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if v not in CalibrationParameterType:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid parameter_type: {v}. "
                f"Must be one of {list(CalibrationParameterType)}"
            )
        return v

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_bounds(self) -> Self:
        """Validate that max_bound > min_bound and initial_guess is within bounds."""
        if self.max_bound <= self.min_bound:
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"max_bound ({self.max_bound}) must be greater than "
                    f"min_bound ({self.min_bound}) for parameter '{self.id}'"
                )
            )
        if self.initial_guess is not None:
            if not (self.min_bound <= self.initial_guess <= self.max_bound):
                raise ValueError(
                    (
                        f"initial_guess ({self.initial_guess}) must be between "
                        f"min_bound ({self.min_bound}) and max_bound "
                        f"({self.max_bound}) for parameter '{self.id}'"
                    )
                )

        return self

docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

A constraint on calibration parameters defined as a mathematical expression.

Constraints are mathematical expressions that must evaluate to >= 0 for the constraint to be satisfied. When the expression evaluates to < 0, the constraint is violated and a penalty is applied during optimization.

Attributes:

Name Type Description id str

Unique identifier for this constraint

expression str

Mathematical expression that must evaluate >= 0 for constraint satisfaction. Can reference calibration parameters by their IDs. When at is specified, can also reference output values (A, B, C, etc.) at those positions.

description str | None

Human-readable description of the constraint (optional)

weight float

Penalty weight multiplier (default: 1.0). Higher values make this constraint more important relative to others. The penalty for violating this constraint is: weight * violation^2

at list[float] | None

Optional positions on the axis at which to evaluate this constraint. The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferenceEquations model only integer steps. If None, the constraint is evaluated once before simulation using parameter values only. If given, it is evaluated at each position and can reference output values.

Examples:

>>> # k1/k2 must be <= 5
>>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
...     id="ratio_bound",
...     expression="5.0 - k1/k2",
...     description="Ratio k1/k2 <= 5",
... )

>>> # k1 must be >= k2
>>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
...     id="ordering",
...     expression="k1 - k2",
...     description="k1 >= k2",
... )

>>> # Sum of parameters <= 1.0
>>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
...     id="sum_bound",
...     expression="1.0 - (param1 + param2 + param3)",
...     description="Sum of rates <= 1.0",
... )

>>> # At positions: bin B stays at or below 500 at specific positions
>>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
...     id="peak_b",
...     expression="500.0 - B",
...     description="Peak B never exceeds 500",
...     at=[10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
... )

class CalibrationConstraint(BaseModel):
    """
    A constraint on calibration parameters defined as a mathematical expression.

    Constraints are mathematical expressions that must evaluate to >= 0 for the
    constraint to be satisfied. When the expression evaluates to < 0, the constraint
    is violated and a penalty is applied during optimization.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for this constraint
    expression : str
        Mathematical expression that must evaluate >= 0 for constraint satisfaction.
        Can reference calibration parameters by their IDs. When `at` is specified,
        can also reference output values (A, B, C, etc.) at those positions.
    description : str | None
        Human-readable description of the constraint (optional)
    weight : float
        Penalty weight multiplier (default: 1.0). Higher values make this constraint
        more important relative to others. The penalty for violating this constraint
        is: weight * violation^2
    at : list[float] | None
        Optional positions on the axis at which to evaluate this constraint.
        The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a
        DifferenceEquations model only integer steps. If None, the constraint
        is evaluated once before simulation using parameter values only. If
        given, it is evaluated at each position and can reference output values.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # k1/k2 must be <= 5
    >>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
    ...     id="ratio_bound",
    ...     expression="5.0 - k1/k2",
    ...     description="Ratio k1/k2 <= 5",
    ... )

    >>> # k1 must be >= k2
    >>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
    ...     id="ordering",
    ...     expression="k1 - k2",
    ...     description="k1 >= k2",
    ... )

    >>> # Sum of parameters <= 1.0
    >>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
    ...     id="sum_bound",
    ...     expression="1.0 - (param1 + param2 + param3)",
    ...     description="Sum of rates <= 1.0",
    ... )

    >>> # At positions: bin B stays at or below 500 at specific positions
    >>> constraint = CalibrationConstraint(
    ...     id="peak_b",
    ...     expression="500.0 - B",
    ...     description="Peak B never exceeds 500",
    ...     at=[10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
    ... )
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(
        default=..., min_length=1, description="Unique identifier for this constraint"
    )
    expression: str = Field(
        default=...,
        min_length=1,
        description="Mathematical expression that must evaluate >= 0",
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the constraint"
    )
    weight: float = Field(
        default=1.0,
        gt=0.0,
        description="Penalty weight multiplier for violations",
    )
    at: list[float] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Optional positions on the axis at which to evaluate the constraint; "
            "it can then reference output values."
        ),
    )

    @field_validator("expression", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def validate_expression(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Perform security validation on the constraint expression."""
        try:
            validate_expression_security(value)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Security validation failed for expression '{value}': {e}"
            )
        return value

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_positions(self) -> Self:
        """Validate that the positions are finite and non-negative."""
        if self.at is not None:
            if len(self.at) == 0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"at for constraint '{self.id}' must not be empty if specified"
                )
            if any(position < 0 or not math.isfinite(position) for position in self.at):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"at for constraint '{self.id}' must all be finite and non-negative"
                )
        return self

class ParticleSwarmConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    Configuration for the Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm.

    Attributes
    ----------
    num_particles : int
        Number of particles in the swarm (default: 20)
    max_iterations : int
        Maximum number of iterations (default: 1000)
    verbose : bool
        Enable verbose output (default: False)
    initialization : str
        Particle initialization strategy (default: "uniform")

    Methods
    -------
    inertia(type, **kwargs)
        Set inertia weight strategy ("constant" or "chaotic")
    acceleration(type, **kwargs)
        Set acceleration coefficients ("constant" or "time_varying")
    mutation(strategy, scale, probability, application)
        Enable mutation to escape local optima
    velocity(clamp_factor, mutation_threshold)
        Configure velocity control
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    # Core parameters
    num_particles: int = Field(
        default=20, gt=0, description="Number of particles in the swarm"
    )
    max_iterations: int = Field(
        default=1000, gt=0, description="Maximum number of iterations"
    )
    verbose: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Enable verbose output during optimization",
    )
    initialization: str = Field(
        default=PSOInitializationStrategy.UNIFORM,
        description=(
            "Particle initialization strategy: 'uniform' (default), 'latin_hypercube',"
            "or 'opposition_based'"
        ),
    )

    # Private attributes for optional configurations (set via fluent methods)
    _inertia: PSOConstantInertia | PSOChaoticInertia | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)
    _acceleration: PSOConstantAcceleration | PSOTimeVaryingAcceleration | None = (
        PrivateAttr(default=None)
    )
    _mutation: PSOMutationConfig | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)
    _velocity: PSOVelocityConfig | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)

    @field_validator("initialization")
    @classmethod
    def validate_initialization(cls, v: str) -> str:
        if v not in PSOInitializationStrategy:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid initialization: {v}. "
                f"Must be one of {list(PSOInitializationStrategy)}"
            )
        return v

    @overload
    def inertia(self, type: str, *, factor: float = 0.721) -> Self: ...

    @overload
    def inertia(self, type: str, *, w_min: float, w_max: float) -> Self: ...

    def inertia(self, type: str, **kwargs: float) -> Self:
        """
        Set inertia weight strategy.

        Parameters
        ----------
        type : str
            Inertia strategy type: "constant" or "chaotic"
        **kwargs : float
            The settings of the strategy, listed under Other Parameters.

        Other Parameters
        ----------------
        factor : float, default=0.721
            Fixed inertia weight (canonical PSO: 1/(2*ln(2)) ≈ 0.721).
            Only used when type="constant".
        w_min : float
            Minimum inertia weight. Only used when type="chaotic".
        w_max : float
            Maximum inertia weight (must be > w_min). Only used when type="chaotic".

        Returns
        -------
        Self
            The config instance for method chaining
        """
        if type not in PSOInertiaType:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid inertia type: {type}. Must be one of {list(PSOInertiaType)}"
            )
        if type == PSOInertiaType.CONSTANT:
            self._inertia = PSOConstantInertia(factor=kwargs.get("factor", 0.721))
        else:
            self._inertia = PSOChaoticInertia(
                w_min=kwargs["w_min"], w_max=kwargs["w_max"]
            )
        return self

    @overload
    def acceleration(
        self,
        type: str,
        *,
        cognitive: float = 1.193,
        social: float = 1.193,
    ) -> Self: ...

    @overload
    def acceleration(
        self,
        type: str,
        *,
        c1_initial: float,
        c1_final: float,
        c2_initial: float,
        c2_final: float,
    ) -> Self: ...

    def acceleration(self, type: str, **kwargs: float) -> Self:
        """
        Set acceleration coefficient strategy.

        Parameters
        ----------
        type : str
            Acceleration strategy type: "constant" or "time_varying"
        **kwargs : float
            The settings of the strategy, listed under Other Parameters.

        Other Parameters
        ----------------
        cognitive : float, default=1.193
            Cognitive coefficient (c1) - attraction to personal best.
            Only used when type="constant".
        social : float, default=1.193
            Social coefficient (c2) - attraction to swarm best.
            Only used when type="constant".
        c1_initial : float
            Initial cognitive factor (typically high, e.g., 2.5).
            Only used when type="time_varying".
        c1_final : float
            Final cognitive factor (typically low, e.g., 0.5).
            Only used when type="time_varying".
        c2_initial : float
            Initial social factor (typically low, e.g., 0.5).
            Only used when type="time_varying".
        c2_final : float
            Final social factor (typically high, e.g., 2.5).
            Only used when type="time_varying".

        Returns
        -------
        Self
            The config instance for method chaining
        """
        if type not in PSOAccelerationType:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid acceleration type: {type}. "
                f"Must be one of {list(PSOAccelerationType)}"
            )
        if type == PSOAccelerationType.CONSTANT:
            self._acceleration = PSOConstantAcceleration(
                cognitive=kwargs.get("cognitive", 1.193),
                social=kwargs.get("social", 1.193),
            )
        else:
            self._acceleration = PSOTimeVaryingAcceleration(
                c1_initial=kwargs["c1_initial"],
                c1_final=kwargs["c1_final"],
                c2_initial=kwargs["c2_initial"],
                c2_final=kwargs["c2_final"],
            )
        return self

    def mutation(
        self,
        strategy: str,
        *,
        scale: float,
        probability: float,
        application: str,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Enable mutation to help escape local optima.

        Parameters
        ----------
        strategy : str
            Mutation distribution: "gaussian" or "cauchy".
            Cauchy has heavier tails for larger jumps.
        scale : float
            Standard deviation (gaussian) or scale parameter (cauchy)
        probability : float
            Mutation probability per iteration (0.0 to 1.0)
        application : str
            Which particles to mutate:
            "global_best", "all_particles", or "below_average"

        Returns
        -------
        Self
            The config instance for method chaining
        """
        if strategy not in PSOMutationStrategy:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid mutation strategy: {strategy}. "
                f"Must be one of {list(PSOMutationStrategy)}"
            )
        if application not in PSOMutationApplication:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid mutation application: {application}. "
                f"Must be one of {list(PSOMutationApplication)}"
            )

        self._mutation = PSOMutationConfig(
            strategy=PSOMutationStrategy(strategy),
            scale=scale,
            probability=probability,
            application=PSOMutationApplication(application),
        )
        return self

    def velocity(
        self,
        *,
        clamp_factor: float | None = None,
        mutation_threshold: float | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Configure velocity control.

        Parameters
        ----------
        clamp_factor : float, optional
            Velocity clamping as fraction of search space (0.0-1.0).
            Typically 0.1-0.2. Prevents explosive velocities.
        mutation_threshold : float, optional
            Reinitialize velocities below this threshold.
            Typically 0.001-0.01. Prevents stagnation.

        Returns
        -------
        Self
            The config instance for method chaining
        """
        self._velocity = PSOVelocityConfig(
            clamp_factor=clamp_factor,
            mutation_threshold=mutation_threshold,
        )
        return self

    @property
    def inertia_config(self) -> PSOConstantInertia | PSOChaoticInertia | None:
        """Get the inertia configuration (for internal use)."""
        return self._inertia

    @property
    def acceleration_config(
        self,
    ) -> PSOConstantAcceleration | PSOTimeVaryingAcceleration | None:
        """Get the acceleration configuration (for internal use)."""
        return self._acceleration

    @property
    def mutation_config(self) -> PSOMutationConfig | None:
        """Get the mutation configuration (for internal use)."""
        return self._mutation

    @property
    def velocity_config(self) -> PSOVelocityConfig | None:
        """Get the velocity configuration (for internal use)."""
        return self._velocity

def mutation(
    self,
    strategy: str,
    *,
    scale: float,
    probability: float,
    application: str,
) -> Self:
    """
    Enable mutation to help escape local optima.

    Parameters
    ----------
    strategy : str
        Mutation distribution: "gaussian" or "cauchy".
        Cauchy has heavier tails for larger jumps.
    scale : float
        Standard deviation (gaussian) or scale parameter (cauchy)
    probability : float
        Mutation probability per iteration (0.0 to 1.0)
    application : str
        Which particles to mutate:
        "global_best", "all_particles", or "below_average"

    Returns
    -------
    Self
        The config instance for method chaining
    """
    if strategy not in PSOMutationStrategy:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid mutation strategy: {strategy}. "
            f"Must be one of {list(PSOMutationStrategy)}"
        )
    if application not in PSOMutationApplication:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid mutation application: {application}. "
            f"Must be one of {list(PSOMutationApplication)}"
        )

    self._mutation = PSOMutationConfig(
        strategy=PSOMutationStrategy(strategy),
        scale=scale,
        probability=probability,
        application=PSOMutationApplication(application),
    )
    return self

class CalibrationResult(BaseModel):
    """
    Result of a calibration: the best of its starts.

    Attributes
    ----------
    best_parameters : dict[str, float]
        The calibrated value of each parameter, in the order of the problem's
        parameters.
    final_loss : float
        Loss at the best parameters.
    iterations : int
        Iterations of the best start.
    converged : bool
        Whether the best start converged.
    termination_reason : str
        Why the best start stopped.
    starts : list[StartSummary]
        Every start that finished, in order; the first is the initial guess.
    failed_runs : list[str]
        Why each start that failed did, with its number.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    best_parameters: dict[str, float] = Field(
        default=..., description="Calibrated parameter values"
    )
    final_loss: float = Field(default=..., description="Final loss value")
    iterations: int = Field(
        default=..., ge=0, description="Number of iterations performed"
    )
    converged: bool = Field(default=..., description="Whether optimization converged")
    termination_reason: str = Field(
        default=..., description="Reason for optimization termination"
    )
    starts: list[StartSummary] = Field(
        default_factory=list, description="Every start that finished"
    )
    failed_runs: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list, description="Why each failed start failed"
    )

    @override
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        """String representation of calibration result."""
        return (
            f"CalibrationResult(\n"
            f"  converged={self.converged},\n"
            f"  final_loss={self.final_loss:.6f},\n"
            f"  iterations={self.iterations},\n"
            f"  best_parameters={self.best_parameters},\n"
            f"  termination_reason='{self.termination_reason}',\n"
            f"  starts={len(self.starts)},\n"
            f"  failed_runs={len(self.failed_runs)}\n"
            f")"
        )

class SampleIdentifiability(IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport]):
    """
    Practical identifiability from any parameter sample: how much it contracts
    each parameter, which parameters move together, and which marginals have
    several modes.

    Attributes
    ----------
    sample : ParameterSample
        The sample, such as the draws of an uncertainty method.
    reference : {"bounds", "prior"}
        The distribution the contraction compares with: ``"bounds"``, the
        uniform distribution on the bounds, or ``"prior"``, the prior of each
        parameter in `priors`, such as the priors the sample was drawn with.
    correlation_threshold : float
        The absolute correlation above which a pair is listed and its
        parameters are poorly determined, strictly between 0 and 1. No
        default: it is a modelling judgment.
    priors : Priors | dict[str, Distribution] | None
        The prior of each parameter, with ``reference="prior"`` only.
    """

    sample: ParameterSample
    reference: Literal["bounds", "prior"]
    correlation_threshold: float = Field(gt=0.0, lt=1.0)
    priors: Priors | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def read_priors(cls, data: object) -> object:
        """Read a mapping of parameter to distribution as `Priors`."""
        if isinstance(data, Mapping) and data.get("priors") is not None:
            return {**data, "priors": coerce_priors(data["priors"])}
        return data

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_priors(self) -> Self:
        """The priors go with ``reference="prior"``, and only with it."""
        if self.reference == "prior" and self.priors is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "reference='prior' needs priors: the prior of each parameter."
            )
        if self.reference == "bounds" and self.priors is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "priors are read only with reference='prior'; with "
                "reference='bounds' leave them out."
            )
        return self

    structural: list[StructuralSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    collinearity: list[CollinearitySection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    sample: list[SampleSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    starts: list[StartsSection] = Field(default_factory=list)
    profile: list[ProfileSection] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_parameters(self) -> Self:
        """Check that the verdicts hold the parameters, in order."""
        if list(self.verdicts) != self.parameters:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The verdicts must hold the parameters {self.parameters} in "
                f"order, got {list(self.verdicts)}."
            )
        return self

    def merge(self, *others: "IdentifiabilityReport") -> "IdentifiabilityReport":
        """
        Join this report with others of the same parameters.

        The sections are kept side by side. A verdict that the reports agree
        on stays, with the reasons of each; one they disagree on is
        ``conflicting``, with every reason.

        Parameters
        ----------
        *others : IdentifiabilityReport
            The reports to join.

        Returns
        -------
        IdentifiabilityReport
            The joined report.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a report has other parameters.
        """
        reports = [self, *others]
        for other in others:
            if other.parameters != self.parameters:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Reports of different parameters cannot merge: "
                    f"{self.parameters} and {other.parameters}."
                )
        verdicts = {
            name: ParameterVerdicts(
                structural=_merge_structural(
                    [
                        v
                        for r in reports
                        if (v := r.verdicts[name].structural) is not None
                    ]
                ),
                practical=_merge_practical(
                    [
                        v
                        for r in reports
                        if (v := r.verdicts[name].practical) is not None
                    ]
                ),
            )
            for name in self.parameters
        }
        return IdentifiabilityReport(
            parameters=self.parameters,
            verdicts=verdicts,
            structural=[s for r in reports for s in r.structural],
            collinearity=[s for r in reports for s in r.collinearity],
            sample=[s for r in reports for s in r.sample],
            starts=[s for r in reports for s in r.starts],
            profile=[s for r in reports for s in r.profile],
        )

class ModelBuilder:
    """
    A fluent interface that writes the process of a model, once.

    The builder adds bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions and
    parameters: the process, which is the same for every kind of model.
    `build` joins it with a structure, which lays the process out (such as
    `Aggregate`, amounts per compartment), and an engine, which runs it.

    Attributes
    ----------
    _name : str
        The model name.
    _description : str | None
        The model description.
    _version : str | None
        The model version.
    _bins : list[Bin]
        List of bins (compartments) in the model.
    _stratifications : list[Stratification]
        List of stratifications.
    _transitions : list[Transition]
        List of transitions between states.
    _parameters : list[Parameter]
        List of model parameters.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str,
        description: str | None = None,
        version: str | None = None,
        bin_unit: str | None = None,
        step_unit: str | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the ModelBuilder.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name : str
            The unique name that identifies the model.
        description : str | None, default=None
            A human-readable description of the model's purpose and function.
        version : str | None, default=None
            The version number of the model.
        bin_unit : str | None, default=None
            The default unit for all bins.
            Individual bins can override this with their own unit parameter.
            Units are optional but required for model.check_unit_consistency().
        step_unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of one step on the axis, of any single dimension (for example
            ``"day"`` or ``"meter"``). The unit check requires every flow to be
            ``<bin unit>/<step_unit>``, and ``Model.axis_units()`` converts
            values to steps of it. None means ``step``, the default increment
            of any axis.
        """
        self._name: str = name
        self._description: str | None = description
        self._version: str | None = version
        self._bin_unit: str | None = bin_unit
        self._step_unit: str | None = step_unit

        self._bins: list[Bin] = []
        self._accumulators: list[Accumulator] = []
        self._stratifications: list[Stratification] = []
        self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
        self._parameters: list[Parameter] = []
        self._series_counter: int = 0

        logger.info(
            (
                f"Initialized ModelBuilder: name='{self._name}', "
                f"version='{self._version or 'N/A'}'"
            )
        )

    def add_bin(self, id: str, name: str, unit: str | None = None) -> Self:
        """
        Add a bin to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the bin.
        name : str
            Human-readable name for the bin.
        unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of measurement for this bin. If None, uses the model-level bin_unit.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.
        """
        # Use bin-specific unit, or fall back to model-level bin_unit
        final_unit = unit if unit is not None else self._bin_unit
        self._bins.append(Bin(id=id, name=name, unit=final_unit))
        logger.info(f"Added bin: id='{id}', name='{name}', unit='{final_unit}'")
        return self

    def add_accumulator(self, id: str, name: str) -> Self:
        """Add a cumulative event counter to the model outputs."""
        self._accumulators.append(Accumulator(id=id, name=name))
        logger.info(f"Added accumulator: id='{id}', name='{name}'")
        return self

    def add_stratification(
        self,
        id: str,
        categories: list[str],
        description: str | None = None,
        conditions: list[StratificationConditionDict] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a stratification to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the stratification.
        categories : list[str]
            list of category identifiers within this stratification.
        description : str | None, default=None
            Human-readable description of the stratification.
        conditions : list[dict] | None, default=None
            When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
            already-applied categories satisfy ALL conditions. Each dict must
            contain "stratification" and "category" keys referencing a
            stratification declared before this one.

            Example: only apply the `sub` stratification to `group1`::

                conditions = [{"stratification": "group", "category": "group1"}]

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any condition references a stratification not yet declared.
        """
        if conditions:
            declared_ids = {s.id for s in self._stratifications}
            for cond in conditions:
                if cond["stratification"] not in declared_ids:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Stratification '{id}': condition references "
                        f"'{cond['stratification']}' which has not been declared yet. "
                        "Conditions may only reference stratifications declared before "
                        "this one."
                    )

        condition_objects = (
            [StratificationCondition(**c) for c in conditions] if conditions else None
        )
        self._stratifications.append(
            Stratification(
                id=id,
                categories=categories,
                description=description,
                conditions=condition_objects,
            )
        )
        logger.info(f"Added stratification: id='{id}', categories={categories}")
        return self

    def add_parameter(
        self,
        id: str,
        value: float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None,
        description: str | None = None,
        unit: str | None = None,
        mode: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a global parameter to the model.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the parameter.
        value : float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None
            Value of the parameter. Can be:
            - float: A numerical constant value
            - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
                   special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e),
                   or contain mathematical expressions (e.g., "k1 * 2",
                   "total_g1 / total")
            - list[tuple[float, float]]: Empirical series as (position, value)
                   points; requires ``mode`` to be set.
            - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use

        description : str | None, default=None
            Human-readable description of the parameter.
        unit : str | None, default=None
            Unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "item").
            Used for unit consistency checking in equations.
        mode : str | None, default=None
            Required when ``value`` is a list of (position, value) points.
            Selects how the series is read: ``"pulse"`` (the value on the step
            of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only),
            ``"step_function"`` (the value of the last point at or before
            ``t``), or ``"linear"`` (linear interpolation in ``t``).

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``value`` is a list but ``mode`` is not provided, or if
            ``mode`` is provided without a list ``value``.
        """
        if isinstance(value, list):
            if mode is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is required when 'value' is a "
                    "series list. Use mode='pulse', 'step_function', or 'linear'."
                )
            param_value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = SeriesValue(
                data=value, mode=mode
            )
        else:
            if mode is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is only valid when 'value' is a "
                    "series list."
                )
            param_value = value
        self._ensure_parameter_id_available(id)
        self._parameters.append(
            Parameter(id=id, value=param_value, description=description, unit=unit)
        )
        logger.info(f"Added parameter: id='{id}', value={value}, unit='{unit}'")
        return self

    def _ensure_parameter_id_available(self, id: str) -> None:
        if any(parameter.id == id for parameter in self._parameters):
            raise ValueError(f"Parameter id '{id}' already exists")

    def _register_series_pattern(
        self,
        pattern: AxisPattern,
        *,
        transition_id: str,
        source_bin: str,
        target_bin: str,
    ) -> AxisPattern:
        """Auto-register a series parameter for pulse-type patterns.

        If ``pattern`` has numeric pulse data, registers a ``"pulse"`` series
        parameter and returns a ``_ComputedAxisPattern`` whose formula is the
        generated parameter name. Otherwise returns ``pattern`` unchanged.
        """
        data = pattern._as_series_data()
        if data is None:
            return pattern
        conditions = pattern.conditions
        if transition_id and conditions:
            src_cats = "_".join(c["category"] for c in conditions if "category" in c)
            tgt_cats = "_".join(
                c["to"] if "to" in c else c["category"]
                for c in conditions
                if "to" in c or "category" in c
            )
            src = f"{source_bin}_{src_cats}" if source_bin else src_cats
            tgt = f"{target_bin}_{tgt_cats}" if target_bin else tgt_cats
            param_name = f"{transition_id}_{src}_to_{tgt}"
        else:
            param_name = f"_series_{self._series_counter}"
            self._series_counter += 1
        self._ensure_parameter_id_available(param_name)
        self._parameters.append(
            Parameter(
                id=param_name,
                value=SeriesValue(data=data, mode="pulse"),
            )
        )
        return _ComputedAxisPattern(
            computed_formula=param_name,
            conditions=conditions,
            source_compartment=pattern.source_compartment,
        )

    def add_transition(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
        rate: "str | float | AxisPattern | None" = None,
        stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRateDict] | None = None,
        per_compartment: bool | None = None,
        accumulators: list[str] | None = None,
        impulse_at: list[float] | None = None,
        impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Add a transition between states to the model.

        This method supports two distinct behaviors:

        When you specify multiple sources without the $compartment placeholder,
        a single transition is created that affects all sources simultaneously.
        The rate is evaluated once, at each position the engine reads it, and
        that value applies to all source compartments at once. What the value
        means (an amount moved in one step or an instantaneous rate) is the
        engine's; see "What a rate means" in the Core Concepts guide.

        When you use the $compartment placeholder in the rate formula with multiple
        sources, the system automatically expands this into multiple independent
        transitions - one for each source compartment. Each transition has its own
        rate calculation where $compartment is replaced with the actual compartment
        name.

        Each transition's rate is evaluated independently, giving per-compartment
        dynamics. This suits an outflow such as ``k1 * $compartment``, where the
        flow of each compartment is proportional to its own amount.

        **$compartment Usage Rules**:
        - Only valid when len(source) > 1
        - Target must be empty [] or have exactly one element
        - Can be used with stratified_rates - the placeholder will be expanded in
          both the base rate and all stratified rate expressions
        - The placeholder $compartment will be replaced with each source compartment
          name

        **$compartment Restrictions**:
        - Using $compartment with a single source will raise an error (use the
          compartment name directly instead)
        - Using $compartment with multiple targets will raise an error (ambiguous
          which target corresponds to which source)

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Unique identifier for the transition. When using $compartment expansion,
            the system will append "__<compartment_name>" to create unique IDs for
            each expanded transition (e.g., "out__A", "out__B").
        source : list[str]
            List of source state/category identifiers. When using $compartment in
            the rate, each source will generate a separate transition.
        target : list[str]
            List of target state/category identifiers. When using $compartment,
            target must be empty [] or have exactly one element.
        rate : str | float | None, default=None
            Default mathematical formula, parameter reference, or constant value for
            the transition rate. Used when no stratified rate matches.
            Can be:
            - A parameter reference
            - A constant value
            - A mathematical formula
            - A formula with $compartment placeholder

            Special variables available in formulas:
            - total: The sum of every compartment, accumulators excluded
            - total_<category>…: The sum of the compartments with these
              categories, in the declaration order of the stratifications
            - t: The current position on the axis
            - step: The step that holds it, ``floor(t)``; in a
              DifferenceEquations model ``t`` and ``step`` are equal
            - pi, e: Mathematical constants
            - $compartment: Expands to each source compartment name (only with
              multiple sources)

        stratified_rates : list[dict] | None, default=None
            List of stratification-specific rates. Each dict must contain:
            - "conditions": List of dicts with "stratification" and "category" keys
            - "rate": Rate expression string

        per_compartment : bool | None, default=None
            When True, base compartment names in the rate
            expression are automatically replaced with the specific stratified
            compartment name for each expanded transition flow. This ensures
            each subgroup transitions based on its own compartment value
            rather than the total across all subgroups.

        accumulators : list[str] | None, default=None
            Ids of accumulators that add up the flow of this transition.

        impulse_at : list[float] | None, default=None
            Make the transition an impulse at these positions on the axis. At
            each one, ``rate`` is the fraction of the source (proportional) or the
            amount (absolute) moved at once, before the flows of that step. A
            DifferenceEquations model needs integer positions.

        impulse_every : tuple[float, float] | None, default=None
            ``(period, offset)``: make the transition an impulse at ``offset``,
            ``offset + period``, ``offset + 2 * period``, ...

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            - If $compartment is used with only one source compartment
            - If $compartment is used with multiple targets
            - If rate is None when using $compartment
        """
        # If `rate` is a AxisPattern, extract its rate string and stratified
        # rates and route them into the existing pipeline. A AxisPattern fully
        # specifies how the rate changes along the axis, so passing `stratified_rates=`
        # alongside it is a conflict.
        if isinstance(rate, AxisPattern):
            if impulse_at is not None or impulse_every is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{id}': an impulse moves its rate at once; pass "
                    "a fraction or an amount as `rate=`, not a AxisPattern."
                )
            if stratified_rates is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Transition '{id}': pass either a AxisPattern as `rate=` "
                    "or `stratified_rates=`, not both."
                )
            src_bin = source[0] if source else ""
            tgt_bin = target[0] if target else ""
            if isinstance(rate, _ScheduleAxisPattern):
                resolved = rate.model_copy(
                    update={
                        "patterns": [
                            _GroupEntry(
                                pattern=self._register_series_pattern(
                                    entry.pattern,
                                    transition_id=id,
                                    source_bin=src_bin,
                                    target_bin=tgt_bin,
                                ),
                                absolute=entry.absolute,
                            )
                            for entry in rate.patterns
                        ]
                    }
                )
                rate = resolved
            else:
                rate = self._register_series_pattern(
                    rate, transition_id=id, source_bin=src_bin, target_bin=tgt_bin
                )
            stratified_rates = rate._builder_stratified_rates()
            rate = rate._builder_rate()

        # Convert rate to string if numeric
        if isinstance(rate, int) or isinstance(rate, float):
            rate = str(rate)

        # Check for $compartment placeholder and handle expansion
        if rate and "$compartment" in rate:
            self._validate_compartment_placeholder(id, source, target)
            self._expand_compartment_transition(
                id, source, target, rate, stratified_rates, impulse_at, impulse_every
            )
            return self

        # Convert stratified rates dicts to Pydantic objects
        stratified_rates_objects: list[StratifiedRate] | None = None
        if stratified_rates:
            stratified_rates_objects = []
            for rate_dict in stratified_rates:
                conditions = [
                    StratificationCondition(**cond) for cond in rate_dict["conditions"]
                ]
                stratified_rates_objects.append(
                    StratifiedRate(
                        conditions=conditions,
                        rate=str(rate_dict["rate"]),
                        absolute=rate_dict.get("absolute"),
                    )
                )

        self._transitions.append(
            Transition(
                id=id,
                source=source,
                target=target,
                accumulators=accumulators or [],
                rate=rate,
                stratified_rates=stratified_rates_objects,
                per_compartment=per_compartment,
                impulse_at=impulse_at,
                impulse_every=impulse_every,
            )
        )
        logger.info(
            (
                f"Added transition: id='{id}', source={source}, target={target}, "
                f"rate='{rate}', stratified_rates={
                    len(stratified_rates_objects) if stratified_rates_objects else 0
                }"
            )
        )
        return self

    def _validate_compartment_placeholder(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Validate that $compartment placeholder is used correctly.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Transition identifier (for error messages)
        source : list[str]
            Source compartments
        target : list[str]
            Target compartments
        rate : str
            Rate formula
        stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRateDict] | None
            Stratified rates

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If $compartment usage violates any rules
        """
        # Check that we have either multiple sources OR multiple targets, but not both
        has_multiple_sources = len(source) > 1
        has_multiple_targets = len(target) > 1

        if not has_multiple_sources and not has_multiple_targets:
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Transition '{id}': $compartment placeholder requires either "
                    f"multiple source compartments or multiple target compartments "
                    f"(found {len(source)} source(s) and {len(target)} target(s)). "
                    f"If you have a single source/target, use the compartment name "
                    f"directly in the rate formula instead of $compartment."
                )
            )

        if has_multiple_sources and has_multiple_targets:
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Transition '{id}': $compartment placeholder cannot be used "
                    f"with both multiple sources and multiple targets "
                    f"(found {len(source)} sources and {len(target)} targets). "
                    f"This would create ambiguous mappings. Use either multiple "
                    f"sources with single/empty target, or single/empty source with "
                    f"multiple targets."
                )
            )

    def _expand_compartment_transition(
        self,
        id: str,
        source: list[str],
        target: list[str],
        rate: str,
        stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRateDict] | None,
        impulse_at: list[float] | None = None,
        impulse_every: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Expand a transition with $compartment placeholder into multiple transitions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            Base transition identifier
        source : list[str]
            Source compartments
            (will create one transition per source if multiple sources)
        target : list[str]
            Target compartments
            (will create one transition per target if multiple targets)
        rate : str
            Rate formula containing $compartment
        stratified_rates : list[StratifiedRateDict] | None
            Stratified rates (can contain $compartment which will be expanded)
        impulse_at, impulse_every : optional
            Impulse schedule of every expanded transition
        """
        # Determine if we're expanding over sources or targets
        has_multiple_sources = len(source) > 1

        if has_multiple_sources:
            compartments = source
            expand_type = "source"
        else:
            compartments = target
            expand_type = "target"

        logger.info(
            (
                f"Expanding transition '{id}' with $compartment placeholder: "
                f"{len(compartments)} {expand_type} compartments will create "
                f"{len(compartments)} separate transitions"
            )
        )

        for compartment in compartments:
            # Replace $compartment with actual compartment name in base rate
            expanded_rate = rate.replace("$compartment", compartment)

            # Expand stratified rates if present
            expanded_stratified_rates: list[StratifiedRate] | None = None
            if stratified_rates:
                expanded_stratified_rates = []
                for rate_dict in stratified_rates:
                    # Replace $compartment in stratified rate expression
                    strat_rate_value = rate_dict["rate"]
                    # Convert to string if it's a number
                    if isinstance(strat_rate_value, (int, float)):
                        strat_rate_str = str(strat_rate_value)
                    else:
                        strat_rate_str = strat_rate_value

                    expanded_strat_rate = strat_rate_str.replace(
                        "$compartment", compartment
                    )

                    # Convert conditions to Pydantic objects
                    conditions = [
                        StratificationCondition(**cond)
                        for cond in rate_dict["conditions"]
                    ]

                    expanded_stratified_rates.append(
                        StratifiedRate(conditions=conditions, rate=expanded_strat_rate)
                    )

            # Generate unique ID for this expanded transition
            expanded_id = f"{id}__{compartment}"

            # add_transition accepts several sources or several targets.
            if has_multiple_sources:
                expanded_source = [compartment]
                expanded_target = target
            else:
                expanded_source = source
                expanded_target = [compartment]

            self._transitions.append(
                Transition(
                    id=expanded_id,
                    source=expanded_source,
                    target=expanded_target,
                    rate=expanded_rate,
                    stratified_rates=expanded_stratified_rates,
                    impulse_at=impulse_at,
                    impulse_every=impulse_every,
                )
            )

            strat_info = (
                f", {len(expanded_stratified_rates)} stratified rates"
                if expanded_stratified_rates
                else ""
            )
            logger.info(
                (
                    f"  Created expanded transition: id='{expanded_id}', "
                    f"source=['{compartment}'], target={target}, "
                    f"rate='{expanded_rate}'{strat_info}"
                )
            )

        logger.info(
            f"Successfully expanded transition '{id}' into {len(compartments)} "
            "transitions"
        )

    def get_summary(self) -> dict[str, str | int | list[str] | None]:
        """
        Get a summary of the current model builder state.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, dict[str, str | int | list[str] | None]]
            Dictionary containing summary information about the model being built.
        """
        return {
            "name": self._name,
            "description": self._description,
            "version": self._version,
            "bins_count": len(self._bins),
            "bin_ids": [state.id for state in self._bins],
            "stratifications_count": len(self._stratifications),
            "stratification_ids": [strat.id for strat in self._stratifications],
            "transitions_count": len(self._transitions),
            "transition_ids": [trans.id for trans in self._transitions],
            "parameters_count": len(self._parameters),
            "parameter_ids": [param.id for param in self._parameters],
        }

    def clone(self) -> Self:
        """
        Create a deep copy of this ModelBuilder.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            A new ModelBuilder instance with the same configuration: every
            bin, accumulator, stratification, transition and parameter.
            Changes to one builder do not affect the other.
        """
        return copy.deepcopy(self)

    def reset(self) -> Self:
        """
        Reset the builder to empty state.

        The name, description, version and ``bin_unit`` are kept. Every bin,
        accumulator, stratification, transition and parameter is removed.

        Returns
        -------
        ModelBuilder
            Self for method chaining.
        """
        self._bins.clear()
        self._accumulators.clear()
        self._stratifications.clear()
        self._transitions.clear()
        self._parameters.clear()
        self._series_counter = 0
        return self

    def process(self) -> Process:
        """
        The process the builder has written so far.

        Returns
        -------
        Process
            The bins, accumulators, stratifications and transitions.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ids repeat, or a transition or a stratified rate names an id
            the process does not have.
        """
        return Process(
            bins=self._bins,
            accumulators=self._accumulators,
            stratifications=self._stratifications,
            transitions=self._transitions,
        )

    def build(
        self,
        structure: StructureT,
        engine: EngineName,
        settings: EngineSettings | None = None,
    ) -> Model[StructureT]:
        """
        Join the process with a structure and an engine into a model.

        The process is written once; the structure lays it out and sets the
        kind of the model, so one builder builds every kind its process fits:

        ``builder.build(Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}),
        engine="DifferentialEquations")``

        Parameters
        ----------
        structure : ModelStructure
            How the process is laid out, such as `Aggregate` (amounts per
            compartment). The model is a ``Model`` of its class.
        engine : EngineName
            The engine that runs the model, which must run the kind of the
            structure: ``"DifferenceEquations"`` (discrete time) or
            ``"DifferentialEquations"`` (continuous time).
        settings : EngineSettings | None, default=None
            Settings of that engine; None uses its defaults. Only
            ``"DifferentialEquations"`` takes settings (`OdeSolver`).

        Returns
        -------
        Model[StructureT]
            The model, of the class of ``structure``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If validation fails, the structure does not fit the process (for
            example a fraction names no bin, or a rate reads ``neighbors_<bin>``
            and the structure has no ``neighbors``), the engine is unknown or
            does not run the kind of the structure, the settings are not
            settings of that engine, or a per-compartment override names an
            unknown compartment or makes the initial amounts exceed the total.
        """
        model: Model[StructureT] = Model(
            name=self._name,
            description=self._description,
            version=self._version,
            parameters=self._parameters,
            engine=ModelEngine(type=engine, settings=settings),
            process=self.process(),
            structure=structure,
            step_unit=self._step_unit,
        )

        logger.info(f"Model '{self._name}' successfully built for the {engine} engine.")

        return model

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str,
    description: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    bin_unit: str | None = None,
    step_unit: str | None = None,
):
    """
    Initialize the ModelBuilder.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        The unique name that identifies the model.
    description : str | None, default=None
        A human-readable description of the model's purpose and function.
    version : str | None, default=None
        The version number of the model.
    bin_unit : str | None, default=None
        The default unit for all bins.
        Individual bins can override this with their own unit parameter.
        Units are optional but required for model.check_unit_consistency().
    step_unit : str | None, default=None
        Unit of one step on the axis, of any single dimension (for example
        ``"day"`` or ``"meter"``). The unit check requires every flow to be
        ``<bin unit>/<step_unit>``, and ``Model.axis_units()`` converts
        values to steps of it. None means ``step``, the default increment
        of any axis.
    """
    self._name: str = name
    self._description: str | None = description
    self._version: str | None = version
    self._bin_unit: str | None = bin_unit
    self._step_unit: str | None = step_unit

    self._bins: list[Bin] = []
    self._accumulators: list[Accumulator] = []
    self._stratifications: list[Stratification] = []
    self._transitions: list[Transition] = []
    self._parameters: list[Parameter] = []
    self._series_counter: int = 0

    logger.info(
        (
            f"Initialized ModelBuilder: name='{self._name}', "
            f"version='{self._version or 'N/A'}'"
        )
    )

def add_bin(self, id: str, name: str, unit: str | None = None) -> Self:
    """
    Add a bin to the model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for the bin.
    name : str
        Human-readable name for the bin.
    unit : str | None, default=None
        Unit of measurement for this bin. If None, uses the model-level bin_unit.

    Returns
    -------
    ModelBuilder
        Self for method chaining.
    """
    # Use bin-specific unit, or fall back to model-level bin_unit
    final_unit = unit if unit is not None else self._bin_unit
    self._bins.append(Bin(id=id, name=name, unit=final_unit))
    logger.info(f"Added bin: id='{id}', name='{name}', unit='{final_unit}'")
    return self

def add_stratification(
    self,
    id: str,
    categories: list[str],
    description: str | None = None,
    conditions: list[StratificationConditionDict] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a stratification to the model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        list of category identifiers within this stratification.
    description : str | None, default=None
        Human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[dict] | None, default=None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied categories satisfy ALL conditions. Each dict must
        contain "stratification" and "category" keys referencing a
        stratification declared before this one.

        Example: only apply the `sub` stratification to `group1`::

            conditions = [{"stratification": "group", "category": "group1"}]

    Returns
    -------
    ModelBuilder
        Self for method chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any condition references a stratification not yet declared.
    """
    if conditions:
        declared_ids = {s.id for s in self._stratifications}
        for cond in conditions:
            if cond["stratification"] not in declared_ids:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Stratification '{id}': condition references "
                    f"'{cond['stratification']}' which has not been declared yet. "
                    "Conditions may only reference stratifications declared before "
                    "this one."
                )

    condition_objects = (
        [StratificationCondition(**c) for c in conditions] if conditions else None
    )
    self._stratifications.append(
        Stratification(
            id=id,
            categories=categories,
            description=description,
            conditions=condition_objects,
        )
    )
    logger.info(f"Added stratification: id='{id}', categories={categories}")
    return self

def add_parameter(
    self,
    id: str,
    value: float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None,
    description: str | None = None,
    unit: str | None = None,
    mode: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a global parameter to the model.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        Unique identifier for the parameter.
    value : float | str | list[tuple[float, float]] | None
        Value of the parameter. Can be:
        - float: A numerical constant value
        - str: A mathematical formula that can reference other parameters,
               special variables (total, total_<category>, step, t, pi, e),
               or contain mathematical expressions (e.g., "k1 * 2",
               "total_g1 / total")
        - list[tuple[float, float]]: Empirical series as (position, value)
               points; requires ``mode`` to be set.
        - None: Indicates that the parameter needs to be calibrated before use

    description : str | None, default=None
        Human-readable description of the parameter.
    unit : str | None, default=None
        Unit of the parameter (e.g., "1/day", "dimensionless", "item").
        Used for unit consistency checking in equations.
    mode : str | None, default=None
        Required when ``value`` is a list of (position, value) points.
        Selects how the series is read: ``"pulse"`` (the value on the step
        of a point, 0 on every other step; integer positions only),
        ``"step_function"`` (the value of the last point at or before
        ``t``), or ``"linear"`` (linear interpolation in ``t``).

    Returns
    -------
    ModelBuilder
        Self for method chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``value`` is a list but ``mode`` is not provided, or if
        ``mode`` is provided without a list ``value``.
    """
    if isinstance(value, list):
        if mode is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is required when 'value' is a "
                "series list. Use mode='pulse', 'step_function', or 'linear'."
            )
        param_value: float | str | SeriesValue | None = SeriesValue(
            data=value, mode=mode
        )
    else:
        if mode is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Parameter '{id}': 'mode' is only valid when 'value' is a "
                "series list."
            )
        param_value = value
    self._ensure_parameter_id_available(id)
    self._parameters.append(
        Parameter(id=id, value=param_value, description=description, unit=unit)
    )
    logger.info(f"Added parameter: id='{id}', value={value}, unit='{unit}'")
    return self
