class SensitivityAnalysis:
    """
    The forward questions of a model: how uncertainty in its inputs moves its
    outputs, and which inputs matter most.

    A calibration asks which inputs fit the data; an analysis needs no data.
    It holds the simulation, what varies (`InputSpace`), the replicates of a
    stochastic engine and the seed of every random number, and every method
    of one analysis reads the same inputs. The forward model is built in Rust
    once, when the analysis is created: the values of the inputs reach the
    engine as a calibration writes them.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        simulation: Simulation,
        inputs: InputSpace,
        *,
        replicates: int | None = None,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Build the analysis of `inputs` on `simulation`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulation : Simulation
            The model to analyse.
        inputs : InputSpace
            What varies.
        replicates : int | None, optional
            For a stochastic engine, required, at least 1: how many replicates
            each point runs. A point of the design of PRCC, Morris, Sobol or
            polynomial chaos holds the mean of its replicates, on the same
            seeds at every point; a propagation keeps every replicate, each
            with a seed of its own. A deterministic engine does not use it, so
            the same analysis runs on either engine.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the designs and the replicates. Required with a
            stochastic engine; otherwise None draws one from the operating
            system, which the analysis logs.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an input is not a value of the model, the replicates or the
            seed do not fit the engine, `replicates` is below 1, or the seed
            is not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
        """
        engine_type = simulation.model_definition.engine.type
        stochastic = commol_rs.engine.EngineType(engine_type).is_stochastic
        if replicates is not None and replicates < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"replicates is at least 1, got {replicates}")
        if stochastic and replicates is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set replicates, how many "
                "replicates each point of a design runs."
            )
        if stochastic and seed is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set seed, so the "
                "replicates and the analysis are reproducible."
            )
        self.simulation: Simulation = simulation
        self.inputs: InputSpace = inputs
        self.replicates: int | None = replicates
        if seed is not None:
            check_seed(seed)
        self._seed: int | None = seed
        check_values(
            simulation.model_definition,
            simulation.engine,
            inputs.parameters,
            inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
        )
        self._rust: "ForwardAnalysisProtocol" = commol_rs.inference.ForwardAnalysis(
            simulation.engine,
            engine_state.rust_parameters(inputs.parameters),
            distributions=inputs.rust_distributions(),
            sample=None if inputs.sample is None else inputs.sample.rust_sample,
            initial_condition_remainder=inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
            replicates=replicates if stochastic else None,
            seed=self.seed,
        )

    @property
    def rust_analysis(self) -> "ForwardAnalysisProtocol":
        """
        The forward analysis built in Rust, for the runners of methods.

        Returns
        -------
        ForwardAnalysisProtocol
            The forward model and the inputs every method reads.
        """
        return self._rust

    def rust_predictive(
        self, sample: ParameterSample, positions: list[float]
    ) -> "PredictiveProtocol":
        """
        The run of every draw of `sample` at `positions`, for a `Predictive`:
        each replicate of a stochastic engine has a seed of its own, derived
        from the seed of the analysis, as in a propagation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws, in the order of the inputs.
        positions : list[float]
            Positions to report at, ascending.

        Returns
        -------
        PredictiveProtocol
            The runs, computed in Rust.
        """
        return self._rust.predictive(sample.rust_sample, positions)

    def rust_observation_draws(
        self,
        sample: ParameterSample,
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint],
        noise: ObservationNoise,
    ) -> "ObservationDrawsProtocol":
        """
        Every draw's value of `observed_data`, for a `Predictive`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws, in the order of the inputs.
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.
        noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
            The observation noise; only ``NoNoise()``.

        Returns
        -------
        ObservationDrawsProtocol
            The draws, computed in Rust.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the noise is not ``NoNoise()``: residual noise needs the
            residuals of a fit, distribution noise the observation models of a
            problem, and an analysis has neither.

        if not isinstance(noise, NoNoise):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(noise).__name__} needs a calibration: residual noise reads "
                "the residuals of a fit and distribution noise the observation "
                "models of a problem, and a sensitivity analysis has no data. Read "
                "the observations with NoNoise()."
            )
        return self._rust.observation_draws(
            sample.rust_sample, engine_state.rust_observed_data(observed_data)
        )

    def rust_log_score(
        self,
        sample: ParameterSample,  # noqa: ARG002
        observed_data: list[ObservedDataPoint],  # noqa: ARG002
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Refuse the log score, which `commol.scores.log_score` asks for.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws.
        observed_data : list[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            Always: the log score reads the observation models of a problem,
            and an analysis has no data.
        """
        raise ValueError(
            "The log score needs the observation models of a calibration problem, "
            "and a sensitivity analysis has no data."
        )

    @property
    def seed(self) -> int:
        """
        The seed of the analysis' random numbers.

        Returns
        -------
        int
            The seed given, or a seed drawn from the operating system once
            per analysis and logged.
        """
        if self._seed is not None:
            return self._seed
        if not hasattr(self, "_drawn_seed"):
            self._drawn_seed = draw_seed()
            logger.info(
                "No seed set; drew the seed %d, which repeats this analysis.",
                self._drawn_seed,
            )
        return self._drawn_seed

    def run(self, method: SensitivityMethod[ResultT]) -> ResultT:
        """
        Run a sensitivity method on the inputs of this analysis.

        Parameters
        ----------
        method : SensitivityMethod[ResultT]
            The configuration of the method; its type sets the result type.

        Returns
        -------
        ResultT
            The method's result.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `method` is not a sensitivity method; the message names its
            entry point.
        ValueError
            If the method does not take these inputs, such as a method of
            independent inputs on inputs from a sample.
        """
        return run_method(self, method, SensitivityMethod)

def __init__(
    self,
    simulation: Simulation,
    inputs: InputSpace,
    *,
    replicates: int | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
):
    """
    Build the analysis of `inputs` on `simulation`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The model to analyse.
    inputs : InputSpace
        What varies.
    replicates : int | None, optional
        For a stochastic engine, required, at least 1: how many replicates
        each point runs. A point of the design of PRCC, Morris, Sobol or
        polynomial chaos holds the mean of its replicates, on the same
        seeds at every point; a propagation keeps every replicate, each
        with a seed of its own. A deterministic engine does not use it, so
        the same analysis runs on either engine.
    seed : int | None, optional
        The seed of the designs and the replicates. Required with a
        stochastic engine; otherwise None draws one from the operating
        system, which the analysis logs.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an input is not a value of the model, the replicates or the
        seed do not fit the engine, `replicates` is below 1, or the seed
        is not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
    """
    engine_type = simulation.model_definition.engine.type
    stochastic = commol_rs.engine.EngineType(engine_type).is_stochastic
    if replicates is not None and replicates < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"replicates is at least 1, got {replicates}")
    if stochastic and replicates is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set replicates, how many "
            "replicates each point of a design runs."
        )
    if stochastic and seed is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The {engine_type} engine is stochastic: set seed, so the "
            "replicates and the analysis are reproducible."
        )
    self.simulation: Simulation = simulation
    self.inputs: InputSpace = inputs
    self.replicates: int | None = replicates
    if seed is not None:
        check_seed(seed)
    self._seed: int | None = seed
    check_values(
        simulation.model_definition,
        simulation.engine,
        inputs.parameters,
        inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
    )
    self._rust: "ForwardAnalysisProtocol" = commol_rs.inference.ForwardAnalysis(
        simulation.engine,
        engine_state.rust_parameters(inputs.parameters),
        distributions=inputs.rust_distributions(),
        sample=None if inputs.sample is None else inputs.sample.rust_sample,
        initial_condition_remainder=inputs.initial_condition_remainder,
        replicates=replicates if stochastic else None,
        seed=self.seed,
    )

class InputSpace(BaseModel):
    """
    What a sensitivity analysis varies.

    Each input is a `CalibrationParameter`, a model parameter or an initial
    condition with its bounds, as a calibration sets it. The inputs follow
    independent distributions, one per input, truncated to its bounds, or
    are the draws of a sample, with their weights; the inputs of a sample may
    depend on each other, so only the methods that allow it take one. Build
    it with `independent`, `uniform_on_bounds` or `from_sample`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    parameters : list[CalibrationParameter]
        The inputs, in order. A factor or a noise parameter is not an input:
        both belong to observations, and an analysis has none.
    distributions : dict[str, Distribution] | None
        The distribution of each input, for independent inputs.
    sample : ParameterSample | None
        The draws of the inputs, for inputs from a sample.
    initial_condition_remainder : str | None
        The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions leave
        of the sum the model states, as in a calibration problem.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    parameters: list[CalibrationParameter] = Field(
        min_length=1, description="The inputs, in order."
    )
    distributions: dict[str, Distribution] | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The distribution of each independent input."
    )
    sample: ParameterSample | None = Field(
        default=None, description="The draws of inputs from a sample."
    )
    initial_condition_remainder: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions leave.",
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def check_inputs(self) -> Self:
        """Check the inputs against the distributions or the sample."""
        ids = [parameter.id for parameter in self.parameters]
        repeated = sorted({i for i in ids if ids.count(i) > 1})
        if repeated:
            raise ValueError(f"Inputs repeat the ids {repeated}.")
        observed = {
            CalibrationParameterType.FACTOR: (
                "a factor, which multiplies an observation"
            ),
            CalibrationParameterType.NOISE: (
                "a noise parameter, which belongs to an observation model"
            ),
        }
        for parameter in self.parameters:
            what = observed.get(CalibrationParameterType(parameter.parameter_type))
            if what is not None:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"'{parameter.id}' is {what}; a sensitivity analysis has no "
                    "observations."
                )
        if (self.distributions is None) == (self.sample is None):
            raise ValueError("Give distributions or a sample, not both.")
        if self.distributions is not None:
            missing = [i for i in ids if i not in self.distributions]
            extra = sorted(set(self.distributions) - set(ids))
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"The inputs {missing} have no distribution: give one per "
                    "input, or InputSpace.uniform_on_bounds(parameters)."
                )
            if extra:
                raise ValueError(f"The distributions of {extra} name no input.")
        if self.sample is not None:
            bounds = [(p.min_bound, p.max_bound) for p in self.parameters]
            if self.sample.names != ids or list(self.sample.bounds) != bounds:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"The sample has the inputs {self.sample.names} with the bounds "
                    f"{list(self.sample.bounds)}; the parameters are {ids} with the "
                    f"bounds {bounds}, in this order."
                )
        return self

    @classmethod
    def independent(
        cls,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        distributions: Mapping[str, Distribution],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Independent inputs, each with its distribution.

        Parameters
        ----------
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in order.
        distributions : Mapping[str, Distribution]
            The distribution of each input, truncated to its bounds.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an input has no distribution or is a factor, a distribution
            names no input, or an id repeats.
        """
        return cls(
            parameters=list(parameters),
            distributions=dict(distributions),
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @classmethod
    def uniform_on_bounds(
        cls,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Independent inputs, each uniform on its bounds; they must be finite.

        Parameters
        ----------
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in order.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.
        """
        return cls.independent(
            parameters,
            {parameter.id: Uniform() for parameter in parameters},
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_sample(
        cls,
        sample: ParameterSample,
        parameters: Sequence[CalibrationParameter],
        *,
        initial_condition_remainder: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        The draws of a sample, with their weights, such as a posterior.

        Its inputs may depend on each other, so only PRCC and propagation
        take it. The parameters give the type of each value, which a sample
        does not hold.

        Parameters
        ----------
        sample : ParameterSample
            The draws.
        parameters : Sequence[CalibrationParameter]
            The inputs, in the order and with the bounds of the sample.
        initial_condition_remainder : str | None, optional
            The bin or compartment that takes what the initial conditions
            leave.

        Returns
        -------
        InputSpace
            The input space.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the sample's names or bounds are not the parameters'.
        """
        return cls(
            parameters=list(parameters),
            sample=sample,
            initial_condition_remainder=initial_condition_remainder,
        )

    @property
    def names(self) -> list[str]:
        """The ids of the inputs, in order."""
        return [parameter.id for parameter in self.parameters]

    def rust_distributions(self) -> list[tuple[str, str, list[float]]] | None:
        """The distributions as the Rust runners read them, or None."""
        if self.distributions is None:
            return None
        return [self.distributions[name].rust_prior(name) for name in self.names]

class PropagationResult(BaseModel):
    """
    The draws of the inputs and what each run gives.

    Its `sample` is a `ParameterSample`, so `Predictive(analysis,
    result.sample, positions)` gives the bands, plots and reports of the
    propagation, as for a calibration.

    Attributes
    ----------
    sample : ParameterSample
        The draws of the inputs: a Latin hypercube of their distributions, or
        the sample of the input space itself.
    labels : list[str]
        The label of each quantity.
    values : list[list[float]]
        The quantities of each run, ``[run][quantity]``: one run per draw, or
        with a stochastic engine one per replicate of each draw.
    weights : list[float]
        The weight of each run; with a stochastic engine each replicate has
        an equal share of its draw's weight. They sum to 1.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    sample: ParameterSample
    labels: list[str]
    values: list[list[float]]
    weights: list[float]

    def summary(self, confidence_level: float) -> list[QuantitySummary]:
        """
        The weighted distribution of each quantity across the runs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        list[QuantitySummary]
            One summary per quantity, in the order of `labels`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The confidence level is strictly between 0 and 1, got "
                f"{confidence_level}"
            )
        levels = [0.5, (1 - confidence_level) / 2, (1 + confidence_level) / 2]
        summaries = []
        for index, label in enumerate(self.labels):
            column = [row[index] for row in self.values]
            median, lower, upper = commol_rs.inference.weighted_quantiles(
                column, self.weights, levels
            )
            summaries.append(
                QuantitySummary(
                    label=label,
                    confidence_level=confidence_level,
                    mean=commol_rs.inference.weighted_mean(column, self.weights),
                    median=median,
                    lower=lower,
                    upper=upper,
                )
            )
        return summaries

Bases: SensitivityMethod[ChaosResult]

A polynomial chaos expansion (Sudret 2008): a polynomial surrogate of each quantity, and the Sobol indices of its coefficients, in far fewer runs than Sobol when the quantity is smooth.

Every input goes to u = F(x), uniform on [0, 1] through its distribution, so one basis of orthonormal Legendre polynomials fits every distribution, truncated ones included. The coefficients come from least squares on a Latin hypercube; the leave-one-out error says how well the expansion predicts the model. It needs independent inputs.

    def predict(self, values: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The quantities the expansion gives at each set of input values.

        Parameters
        ----------
        values : Sequence[Sequence[float]]
            One value per input, in the order of `inputs`, for each point,
            each inside the bounds of its input.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            The value of each quantity at each point, ``[point][quantity]``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a point has not one value per input or a value outside the
            bounds of its input, or the coefficients do not fit the degree.
        """
        return commol_rs.inference.chaos_evaluate(
            engine_state.rust_parameters(self.input_space.parameters),
            self.input_space.rust_distributions() or [],
            self.degree,
            self.coefficients,
            [list(point) for point in values],
        )

        bounds of its input, or the coefficients do not fit the degree.
    """
    return commol_rs.inference.chaos_evaluate(
        engine_state.rust_parameters(self.input_space.parameters),
        self.input_space.rust_distributions() or [],
        self.degree,
        self.coefficients,
        [list(point) for point in values],
    )

    The value at `end` minus the value at `start`: what entered a cumulative

    ``end - start`` reads it.

    end: Position = Field(description="The end of the window.")

docs.text:
A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

The engine follows the model: run and engine rebuild it when model_definition no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built from, for example after Model.update_parameters.

Source code in commol/api/simulation.py 
class Simulation:
    """
    A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

    The engine follows the model: ``run`` and ``engine`` rebuild it when
    ``model_definition`` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built
    from, for example after ``Model.update_parameters``.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: Model):
        """
        Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind.
            None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

        """
        if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
            raise TypeError(
                f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
                f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
                "holds the structure of its kind, such as an Aggregate."
            )
        logger.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
        self.model_definition: Model = model
        self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())

    def _build_engine(self, model_json: str) -> None:
        """Build the engine and its output names from a model JSON."""
        self._model_json: str = model_json
        self._engine: "EngineProtocol" = build_engine(model_json)
        self._simulation_outputs: list[str] = self._engine.output_names
        logger.info(
            f"Simulation engine ready. Outputs: {len(self._simulation_outputs)}"
        )

    def _sync_engine(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild the engine when the model changed since it was built."""
        model_json = self.model_definition.model_dump_json()
        if model_json != self._model_json:
            logger.info("Model changed since the engine was built; rebuilding it.")
            self._build_engine(model_json)

    def _validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self, model: Model) -> None:
        """
        Validates that every parameter, and every value of the model kind, has
        a value (is calibrated).

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model to validate.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any parameter, or any value of the model kind such as an
            initial condition, has a None value.
        """
        uncalibrated_params = model.get_uncalibrated_parameters()
        uncalibrated_ics = model.structure.uncalibrated_values()

        errors = []
        if uncalibrated_params:
            errors.append(
                f"Parameters requiring calibration: {', '.join(uncalibrated_params)}"
            )
        if uncalibrated_ics:
            errors.append(
                f"Initial conditions requiring calibration: "
                f"{', '.join(uncalibrated_ics)}"
            )

        if errors:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot run Simulation: {'; '.join(errors)}. "
                f"Please calibrate these values before running a simulation."
            )

    @property
    def is_stochastic(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the engine of the model draws random numbers."""
        return commol_rs.engine.EngineType(
            self.model_definition.engine.type
        ).is_stochastic

    def _seed_run(self, seed: int | None) -> int | None:
        """Seed the engine of a stochastic model; None for a deterministic one."""
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            return None
        seed = draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed)
        self._engine.set_seed(seed)
        return seed

    def run(self, num_steps: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state on its default grid.

        Every call starts at position 0 with the current ``model_definition``,
        so two calls with the same model, and the same seed for a stochastic
        engine, give the same result. To continue a run, call
        ``simulation.engine.step()``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: the results hold the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which ``results.seed`` keeps, so
            every run can be repeated. A deterministic engine ignores it.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, or the seed is
            not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
        RuntimeError
            If a rate cannot be evaluated or is not a number; the message
            names the flow and the position.
        """
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        logger.info(f"Running simulation for {num_steps} steps.")
        start = time.time()
        positions, rows = self._engine.run(num_steps)
        logger.info(f"Simulation complete. It took {time.time() - start} seconds.")
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def run_at(
        self, at: Sequence[float], *, seed: int | None = None
    ) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state and reports at given positions.

        The positions are on the axis, the independent variable of the model.
        The engine decides which positions its model type reports at: a
        DifferentialEquations model at any finite, non-negative position, from
        the dense output of its solver; a DifferenceEquations model only at
        integer steps.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine; see `run`.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, the positions are
            not sorted and unique, or the engine does not report at one of them;
            the message is the engine's.
        RuntimeError
            If a rate cannot be evaluated or is not a number; the message
            names the flow and the position.
        """
        positions = [float(position) for position in at]
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        rows = self._engine.run_at(positions)
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def replicates(self, n: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> "ReplicateRuns":
        """
        Replicates of the runs of a stochastic engine.

        The returned object has ``run`` and ``run_at``, as `Simulation`, and
        they return `SimulationReplicates`: ``n`` runs, each with its own seed,
        run in parallel in the engine. Replicate ``i`` takes the seed derived
        from ``seed`` and ``i`` (the SplitMix64 of ``seed + i``), so it gives
        the same run however many replicates run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        n : int
            How many replicates, at least 1.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which the replicates keep.

        Returns
        -------
        ReplicateRuns
            The runner of the replicates.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the engine is deterministic (every replicate would be equal),
            ``n`` is below 1, or the seed is not valid.
        """
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {self.model_definition.engine.type} engine is deterministic: "
                "every replicate would be equal. Replicates need a stochastic engine."
            )
        if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"The number of replicates is at least 1, got {n!r}.")
        return ReplicateRuns(self, n, draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed))

    @property
    def engine(self) -> "EngineProtocol":
        """
        The engine for the current ``model_definition``.

        It is rebuilt, at step 0, when the model changed since it was built.
        Otherwise it is the same object, in the state the last ``run`` or
        ``step`` left it.
        """
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._engine

    @property
    def simulation_outputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of the columns returned by simulation runs."""
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._simulation_outputs

    def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
        """
        Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

        The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
        (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for an aggregate model, by
        bin and accumulator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            A source id, such as a bin id or an accumulator id.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Output names for that id, in the order the engine reports them.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If `id` is not a source of the model.
        """
        model = self.model_definition
        outputs = model.structure.outputs_by_source(model)
        if id not in outputs:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{id}' is not a bin or accumulator of model "
                f"'{self.model_definition.name}'. Available: {sorted(outputs)}"
            )
        return outputs[id]

    def group_outputs(self, ids: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        Group output names by the bin or accumulator they belong to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Each id mapped to its output names, keeping the order given.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model.
        """
        return {id: self.outputs_for(id) for id in ids}

    def total_series(
        self,
        results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        ids: Iterable[str],
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
            Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One value per position of `results`.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        """
        names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
        missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
        if not names:
            return []
        return [
            sum(values)
            for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
        ]

    def windowed_totals(
        self,
        results: SimulationResults,
        ids: Iterable[str],
        window: float,
        at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : SimulationResults
            Simulation results, with their positions.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Accumulator ids whose outputs are summed before windowing.
        window : float
            Length of one window on the axis.
        at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
            Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete
            window of the results (:func:`commol.window_ends`). Pass the
            observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a
            calibration used.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One increment per window.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        ValueError
            If `window` is not positive, or the results have no value at the
            end or the start of a requested window.
        """
        return windowed_totals(
            self.total_series(results, ids), results.positions, window, at
        )

def run_at(
    self, at: Sequence[float], *, seed: int | None = None
) -> SimulationResults:
    """
    Runs the simulation from the initial state and reports at given positions.

    The positions are on the axis, the independent variable of the model.
    The engine decides which positions its model type reports at: a
    DifferentialEquations model at any finite, non-negative position, from
    the dense output of its solver; a DifferenceEquations model only at
    integer steps.

    Parameters
    ----------
    at : Sequence[float]
        Sorted, unique positions to report at.
    seed : int | None, optional
        The seed of a stochastic engine; see `run`.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulationResults
        One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
        seed of a stochastic run.

    Raises
    ------
    InfeasibleStateError
        If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
        compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
    ValueError
        If a parameter or initial condition has no value, the positions are
        not sorted and unique, or the engine does not report at one of them;
        the message is the engine's.
    RuntimeError
        If a rate cannot be evaluated or is not a number; the message
        names the flow and the position.
    """
    positions = [float(position) for position in at]
    self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
    self._sync_engine()
    used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
    self._engine.reset()
    rows = self._engine.run_at(positions)
    return SimulationResults.from_rows(
        positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
    )

def replicates(self, n: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> "ReplicateRuns":
    """
    Replicates of the runs of a stochastic engine.

    The returned object has ``run`` and ``run_at``, as `Simulation`, and
    they return `SimulationReplicates`: ``n`` runs, each with its own seed,
    run in parallel in the engine. Replicate ``i`` takes the seed derived
    from ``seed`` and ``i`` (the SplitMix64 of ``seed + i``), so it gives
    the same run however many replicates run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        How many replicates, at least 1.
    seed : int | None, optional
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from, a whole number from 0 to
        ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which the replicates keep.

    Returns
    -------
    ReplicateRuns
        The runner of the replicates.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the engine is deterministic (every replicate would be equal),
        ``n`` is below 1, or the seed is not valid.
    """
    if not self.is_stochastic:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The {self.model_definition.engine.type} engine is deterministic: "
            "every replicate would be equal. Replicates need a stochastic engine."
        )
    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"The number of replicates is at least 1, got {n!r}.")
    return ReplicateRuns(self, n, draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed))

def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
    """
    Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

    The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
    (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for an aggregate model, by
    bin and accumulator.

    Parameters
    ----------
    id : str
        A source id, such as a bin id or an accumulator id.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        Output names for that id, in the order the engine reports them.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If `id` is not a source of the model.
    """
    model = self.model_definition
    outputs = model.structure.outputs_by_source(model)
    if id not in outputs:
        raise KeyError(
            f"'{id}' is not a bin or accumulator of model "
            f"'{self.model_definition.name}'. Available: {sorted(outputs)}"
        )
    return outputs[id]

def total_series(
    self,
    results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
    ids: Iterable[str],
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
        Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
    ids : Iterable[str]
        Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One value per position of `results`.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
        output is missing from `results`.
    """
    names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
    missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
    if not names:
        return []
    return [
        sum(values)
        for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
    ]

class SimulationResults(dict[str, list[float]]):
    """
    Values of every output at each position on the axis.

    A ``dict`` from output name to one value per position, so
    ``results["A"]``, ``json.dumps(results)`` and
    ``pandas.DataFrame(results)`` work as for any mapping. The positions the
    values were read at are in :attr:`positions`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, ascending. ``results[name][i]`` is the value of
        ``name`` at ``positions[i]``.
    seed : int | None
        The seed of the run of a stochastic engine, which repeats it; None for
        a deterministic engine, whose runs depend on no seed.
    """

    positions: list[float]
    seed: int | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        positions: Iterable[float],
        values: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None = None,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Results at the given positions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Iterable[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        values : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None, optional
            One value per position for each output.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the run, or None when it depends on no seed.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an output does not have one value per position.
        """
        super().__init__(
            {name: list(series) for name, series in (values or {}).items()}
        )
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        self.seed = seed
        for name, series in self.items():
            if len(series) != len(self.positions):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Output '{name}' has {len(series)} values for "
                    f"{len(self.positions)} positions."
                )

    @classmethod
    def from_rows(
        cls,
        positions: Sequence[float],
        names: Sequence[str],
        rows: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
        seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> "SimulationResults":
        """
        Results from one row of output values per position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        names : Sequence[str]
            Output names, in the order of each row.
        rows : Sequence[Sequence[float]]
            One row per position.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the run, or None when it depends on no seed.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series per output name.
        """
        columns = list(zip(*rows)) if rows else [() for _ in names]
        return cls(positions, dict(zip(names, columns, strict=True)), seed=seed)

    def rows(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        Every output at each position, one row per position.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            ``rows()[i][j]`` is the value of the ``j``-th output, in key order
            (the order of ``Simulation.simulation_outputs``), at
            ``positions[i]``.
        """
        return [list(row) for row in zip(*self.values())] if self else []

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The positions, the seed and the values."""
        seed = "" if self.seed is None else f"seed={self.seed!r}, "
        return (
            f"SimulationResults(positions={self.positions!r}, {seed}"
            f"{dict.__repr__(self)})"
        )

class ReplicateRuns:
    """
    Runs replicates of a stochastic model; `Simulation.replicates` makes it.

    Attributes
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The simulation whose model the replicates run.
    n : int
        How many replicates.
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    """

    def __init__(self, simulation: Simulation, n: int, seed: int):
        """
        The replicates of a simulation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulation : Simulation
            The simulation whose model the replicates run.
        n : int
            How many replicates.
        seed : int
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
        """
        self.simulation = simulation
        self.n = n
        self.seed = seed

    def _replicates(self, grid: int | list[float]) -> SimulationReplicates:
        """The replicates on ``grid``: a number of steps or the positions."""
        simulation = self.simulation
        simulation._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(simulation.model_definition)
        engine = simulation.engine
        positions, seeds, runs = engine.run_replicates(self.seed, self.n, grid)
        outputs = simulation.simulation_outputs
        return SimulationReplicates(
            (
                SimulationResults.from_rows(
                    positions, outputs, rows, seed=replicate_seed
                )
                for replicate_seed, rows in zip(seeds, runs, strict=True)
            ),
            seed=self.seed,
            positions=positions,
        )

    def run(self, num_steps: int) -> SimulationReplicates:
        """
        Every replicate from the initial state, on the default grid.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: each replicate holds the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationReplicates
            One `SimulationResults` per replicate, each with its seed.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a replicate leaves the values the model allows.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or a value of the model has no value.
        """
        return self._replicates(num_steps)

    def run_at(self, at: Sequence[float]) -> SimulationReplicates:
        """
        Every replicate from the initial state, reported at given positions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationReplicates
            One `SimulationResults` per replicate, each with its seed.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a replicate leaves the values the model allows.
        ValueError
            If a parameter has no value, the positions are not sorted and
            unique, or the engine does not report at one of them.
        """
        return self._replicates([float(position) for position in at])

class SimulationReplicates(list[SimulationResults]):
    """
    Replicates of a run of a stochastic engine, one `SimulationResults` each.

    A ``list`` of runs at the same positions, each with its own seed:
    ``replicates[i].seed`` repeats replicate ``i``. The statistics reduce the
    replicates position by position, and `member_statistics` reduces them as
    ``ci_percentiles`` requires.

    Attributes
    ----------
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, shared by every replicate.
    """

    seed: int
    positions: list[float]

    def __init__(
        self, runs: Iterable[SimulationResults], seed: int, positions: Sequence[float]
    ):
        """
        Replicates of one run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        runs : Iterable[SimulationResults]
            One run per replicate, at `positions`.
        seed : int
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a run is not at `positions`.
        """
        super().__init__(runs)
        self.seed = seed
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        for index, run in enumerate(self):
            if run.positions != self.positions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Replicate {index} is at other positions than the replicates."
                )

    @property
    def seeds(self) -> list[int]:
        """The seed of each replicate, in order."""
        return [run.seed for run in self if run.seed is not None]

    def _values(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.asarray([run[name] for run in self], dtype=float)

    def mean(self) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        The mean of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series of means per output, with no seed.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If there are no replicates.
        """
        names = list(self[0]) if self else []
        if not names:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        return SimulationResults(
            self.positions,
            {name: self._values(name).mean(axis=0).tolist() for name in names},
        )

    def quantiles(self, levels: Sequence[float]) -> dict[float, SimulationResults]:
        """
        Quantiles of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        The quantile is the one convention of commol (`weighted_quantiles`
        with equal weights, NumPy's ``method="hazen"``).

        Parameters
        ----------
        levels : Sequence[float]
            Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1, such as ``[0.05, 0.5,
            0.95]``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[float, SimulationResults]
            The results of each level.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a level is outside ``[0, 1]`` or there are no replicates.
        """
        for level in levels:
            if not 0.0 <= level <= 1.0:
                raise ValueError(f"A quantile level is between 0 and 1, got {level}.")
        if not self:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        from commol.api.inference.intervals import weighted_quantiles

        names = list(self[0])
        per_name = {
            name: [
                weighted_quantiles(column.tolist(), levels)
                for column in self._values(name).T
            ]
            for name in names
        }
        return {
            level: SimulationResults(
                self.positions,
                {
                    name: [at_position[index] for at_position in per_name[name]]
                    for name in names
                },
            )
            for index, level in enumerate(levels)
        }

    def member_statistics(
        self, output: str, confidence_level: float
    ) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        The spread of one output across the replicates, at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output : str
            An output name.
        confidence_level : float
            Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[float]]
            Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
            ``max``, one value per position (`member_statistics`).

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If no replicate has the output.
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is out of range or there are no
            replicates.
        """
        from commol.api.inference.intervals import member_statistics

        if self and output not in self[0]:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{output}' is not an output of the replicates. "
                f"Outputs: {sorted(self[0])}"
            )
        return member_statistics([run[output] for run in self], confidence_level)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The number of replicates, their seed and their positions."""
        return (
            f"SimulationReplicates({len(self)} replicates, seed={self.seed!r}, "
            f"positions={self.positions!r})"
        )

def __init__(
    self, runs: Iterable[SimulationResults], seed: int, positions: Sequence[float]
):
    """
    Replicates of one run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runs : Iterable[SimulationResults]
        One run per replicate, at `positions`.
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions on the axis, ascending.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a run is not at `positions`.
    """
    super().__init__(runs)
    self.seed = seed
    self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
    for index, run in enumerate(self):
        if run.positions != self.positions:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Replicate {index} is at other positions than the replicates."
            )

def window_index(at: float, window: float) -> int:
    """
    Window a position belongs to.

    The exact inverse of :func:`window_end`, and the containing window for
    any position in between: ``max(ceil(at / window) - 1, 0)``. Position 0
    belongs to window 0. :func:`commol.api.reporting.observed_report` places
    each observation with this rule.

    Parameters
    ----------
    at : float
        A position on the axis.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Zero-based window index.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive or `at` is negative.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    if not at >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"at must not be negative, got {at}.")
    return max(math.ceil(_windows_in(at, window)) - 1, 0)

def window_ends(window: float, end: float) -> list[float]:
    """
    Positions closing each complete window up to a position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    end : float
        Last position covered, such as the last position of a run.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        ``window``, ``2 * window``, ... up to `end`. A trailing partial window
        is not included.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    # A non-positive end has no window: range() of a count below 1 is empty.
    count = math.floor(_windows_in(end, window))
    return [window_end(index, window) for index in range(count)]

def windowed_totals(
    series: Sequence[float],
    positions: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Amount a cumulative series gained over each window.

    Each value is the series at the end of the window minus the series at its
    start, ``at - window``: the same quantity a calibration compares an
    observation against when that observation sets ``window``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : Sequence[float]
        A cumulative series, one value per position.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions of the series, ascending, such as
        ``SimulationResults.positions``.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
        Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete window of
        the series (:func:`window_ends`). Pass the observation positions to
        reproduce exactly the values a calibration used.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One increment per requested position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive, a window starts before position 0, or the
        series has no value at the end or the start of a requested window.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    ends = (
        window_ends(window, positions[-1] if positions else 0.0)
        if at is None
        else list(at)
    )

    totals = []
    for end in ends:
        start = end - window
        if start < -POSITION_TOLERANCE * max(abs(end), 1.0):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Position {end} has no complete window of {window} before it."
            )
        totals.append(
            series[index_at(positions, end)]
            - series[index_at(positions, max(start, 0.0))]
        )
    return totals

Bases: BaseModel

Draws of the parameters of a calibration problem, each with a weight.

A method that has draws returns them in a sample: a bootstrap, a sequential Monte Carlo run, a Markov chain. Plots, reports, the predictive and the scores read a sample, never the result of one method. Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust; with equal weights it is the unweighted statistic.

A sample has no single set of parameters: to run one draw, take it from draws.

The natural logarithm of each draw's weight, normalized so that the weights sum to 1. A draw of weight zero has -inf.

class ParameterSample(BaseModel):
    """
    Draws of the parameters of a calibration problem, each with a weight.

    A method that has draws returns them in a sample: a bootstrap, a
    sequential Monte Carlo run, a Markov chain. Plots, reports, the
    predictive and the scores read a sample, never the result of one method.
    Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust; with equal weights it
    is the unweighted statistic.

    A sample has no single set of parameters: to run one draw, take it from
    `draws`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    names : list[str]
        One name per column, in the order of the problem's parameters.
    bounds : list[tuple[float, float]]
        The bounds of each parameter; every value lies inside them.
    values : list[list[float]]
        One row per draw, one column per name.
    log_weights : list[float]
        The natural logarithm of each draw's weight, normalized so that the
        weights sum to 1. A draw of weight zero has ``-inf``.
    groups : list[int] | None
        The group of each draw (a chain, a replicate or a wave), or None.
    method : SampleMethod
        What made the sample.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a value is not finite or outside its bounds, a log weight is NaN or
        ``+inf``, every log weight is ``-inf``, a name repeats, or the shapes
        differ.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, ser_json_inf_nan="constants")

    names: list[str] = Field(description="One name per column.")
    bounds: list[tuple[float, float]] = Field(description="Bounds of each parameter.")
    values: list[list[float]] = Field(description="One row per draw.")
    log_weights: list[float] = Field(description="Normalized log weight of each draw.")
    groups: list[int] | None = Field(default=None, description="Group of each draw.")
    method: SampleMethod = Field(description="What made the sample.")

    _rust: "ParameterSampleProtocol" = PrivateAttr()

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def normalize_log_weights(cls, data: object) -> object:
        """Check the invariants in Rust and normalize the log weights."""
        if not isinstance(data, Mapping):
            return data
        rust = commol_rs.inference.ParameterSample(
            list(data.get("names", [])),
            [tuple(bound) for bound in data.get("bounds", [])],
            [list(row) for row in data.get("values", [])],
            [float(w) for w in data.get("log_weights", [])],
            data.get("groups"),
        )
        return {**data, "log_weights": rust.log_weights}

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def build_rust_sample(self) -> Self:
        """Keep the Rust sample that computes the statistics."""
        self._rust = commol_rs.inference.ParameterSample(
            self.names, self.bounds, self.values, self.log_weights, self.groups
        )
        return self

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        """Two samples are equal when their fields are."""
        if not isinstance(other, ParameterSample):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.model_dump() == other.model_dump()

    __hash__ = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    @classmethod
    def equally_weighted(
        cls,
        names: list[str],
        bounds: list[tuple[float, float]],
        values: list[list[float]],
        method: SampleMethod,
        groups: list[int] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        A sample whose draws have equal weights.

        Parameters
        ----------
        names : list[str]
            One name per column.
        bounds : list[tuple[float, float]]
            The bounds of each parameter.
        values : list[list[float]]
            One row per draw.
        method : SampleMethod
            What made the sample.
        groups : list[int] | None, optional
            The group of each draw.

        Returns
        -------
        ParameterSample
            The sample.
        """
        return cls(
            names=names,
            bounds=bounds,
            values=values,
            log_weights=[0.0] * len(values),
            groups=groups,
            method=method,
        )

    @property
    def rust_sample(self) -> "ParameterSampleProtocol":
        """The sample in Rust, for the runners of methods and the predictive."""
        return self._rust

    @property
    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """The weight of each draw; they sum to 1."""
        return self._rust.weights

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """The number of draws."""
        return len(self.values)

    def draws(self) -> Iterator[dict[str, float]]:
        """
        Every draw, as a mapping of parameter name to value.

        Yields
        ------
        dict[str, float]
            One draw, in the order of `values`.
        """
        for row in self.values:
            yield dict(zip(self.names, row, strict=True))

    def mean(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        """
        The weighted mean of each parameter.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, float]
            One mean per name.
        """
        return dict(zip(self.names, self._rust.mean(), strict=True))

    def covariance(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted covariance matrix, in the order of `names`.

        With weights ``w`` that sum to 1 it is
        ``Σ wᵢ(xᵢ − x̄)(yᵢ − ȳ) / (1 − Σ wᵢ²)``: with equal weights, the
        sample covariance. It is NaN for a sample of one effective draw.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            One row per name.
        """
        return self._rust.covariance()

    def correlation(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted correlation matrix, in the order of `names`.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            One row per name; NaN for a parameter with no spread.
        """
        return self._rust.correlation()

    def quantiles(self, levels: list[float]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted quantiles of each parameter.

        The quantile is the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution,
        interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights; with
        equal weights it is NumPy's ``method="hazen"``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        levels : list[float]
            Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[float]]
            One quantile per level for each name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a level is not between 0 and 1.
        """
        rows = self._rust.quantiles([float(level) for level in levels])
        return {
            name: [row[column] for row in rows]
            for column, name in enumerate(self.names)
        }

    def interval(self, confidence_level: float) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
        """
        The central interval of each parameter.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1, such as 0.95.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, tuple[float, float]]
            ``(lower, upper)`` for each name: the quantiles
            ``(1 − c)/2`` and ``(1 + c)/2``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        lower, upper = self._rust.interval(confidence_level)
        return {
            name: (low, high)
            for name, low, high in zip(self.names, lower, upper, strict=True)
        }

    def effective_size(self) -> float:
        """
        Kish's effective sample size: ``1 / Σ wᵢ²``.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Between 1 and the number of draws; equal weights give the number
            of draws.
        """
        return self._rust.effective_size()

    def resample(self, count: int, seed: int) -> "ParameterSample":
        """
        Draw `count` draws with replacement, each with probability its weight.

        Parameters
        ----------
        count : int
            Number of draws.
        seed : int
            Seed of the generator.

        Returns
        -------
        ParameterSample
            A sample of equal weights.
        """
        indices = self._rust.resample(count, seed)
        return ParameterSample.equally_weighted(
            self.names,
            self.bounds,
            [self.values[i] for i in indices],
            SampleMethod(
                name="resample",
                settings={"of": self.method.name, "count": count, "seed": seed},
            ),
        )

    def summary(self, confidence_level: float) -> dict[str, ParameterSummary]:
        """
        Weighted statistics of each parameter, for a report.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, ParameterSummary]
            One summary per name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        lower, upper = self._rust.interval(confidence_level)
        quantiles = self.quantiles([0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
        mean = self.mean()
        covariance = self.covariance()
        return {
            name: ParameterSummary(
                mean=mean[name],
                median=quantiles[name][1],
                std=covariance[index][index] ** 0.5,
                lower=lower[index],
                upper=upper[index],
                min=quantiles[name][0],
                max=quantiles[name][2],
            )
            for index, name in enumerate(self.names)
        }

The draws run in parallel in Rust, through the forward model of a calibration problem or of a sensitivity analysis: with a stochastic engine every replicate of a draw is a draw of the predictive, with an equal share of its weight. class Predictive:
    """
    The run of every draw of a parameter sample.

    The draws run in parallel in Rust, through the forward model of a
    calibration problem or of a sensitivity analysis: with a stochastic engine
    every replicate of a draw is a draw of the predictive, with an equal share
    of its weight. A band
    reduces the draws position by position with their weights; without
    observation noise it is a band of the model, not a prediction interval.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: PredictiveSource,
        sample: ParameterSample,
        positions: Sequence[float],
    ):
        """
        Run every draw of `sample` at `positions`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        source : PredictiveSource
            The calibration problem the sample is a sample of (`Calibrator`),
            or the sensitivity analysis of its inputs (`SensitivityAnalysis`).
        sample : ParameterSample
            Its parameters, in the order of the problem or the analysis.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions to report at, ascending.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the sample's parameters are not the source's.
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a draw leaves the values its model allows.
        """
        self.source: PredictiveSource = source
        self.sample: ParameterSample = sample
        self.positions: list[float] = [float(position) for position in positions]
        self.output_names: list[str] = list(source.simulation.engine.output_names)
        self._rust = source.rust_predictive(sample, self.positions)

    @property
    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """The weight of each draw of the predictive; they sum to 1."""
        return self._rust.weights

    def runs(self) -> list[SimulationResults]:
        """
        The trajectory of every draw, in the order of `weights`.

        Returns
        -------
        list[SimulationResults]
            One run per draw, at `positions`.
        """
        return [
            SimulationResults.from_rows(self.positions, self.output_names, rows)
            for rows in self._rust.trajectories
        ]

    def band(self, confidence_level: float) -> PredictiveBand:
        """
        The band of every output.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        PredictiveBand
            The weighted mean, median and central interval of each output at
            each position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.band(confidence_level)

        def by_output(table: list[list[float]]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
            return {
                name: [row[index] for row in table]
                for index, name in enumerate(self.output_names)
            }

        return PredictiveBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=self.positions,
            mean=by_output(mean),
            median=by_output(median),
            lower=by_output(lower),
            upper=by_output(upper),
        )

    def series_band(
        self,
        outputs: Sequence[str],
        confidence_level: float,
        cumulative: bool = False,
    ) -> SeriesBand:
        """
        The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total.

        Each draw is reduced to the series first, then the series are reduced
        across the draws.

        Parameters
        ----------
        outputs : Sequence[str]
            The outputs summed.
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.
        cumulative : bool, optional
            Whether the series is the running total along the positions.

        Returns
        -------
        SeriesBand
            One value per position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an output is unknown or the confidence level is out of range.
        """
        unknown = [name for name in outputs if name not in self.output_names]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown outputs {unknown}. Outputs: {self.output_names}."
            )
        indices = [self.output_names.index(name) for name in outputs]
        mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.series_band(
            indices, cumulative, confidence_level
        )
        return SeriesBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=self.positions,
            mean=mean,
            median=median,
            lower=lower,
            upper=upper,
        )

    def at_observations(
        self,
        observed_data: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
        noise: ObservationNoise,
    ) -> ObservationDraws:
        """
        Every draw's value of each observation, with observation noise.

        The observations need not be the ones the problem was fitted to: held
        out data are read the same way, through the observation operator,
        and so are the observations of the model of an analysis. The noise
        is drawn from the calibrator's seed.

        Parameters
        ----------
        observed_data : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.
        noise : NoNoise | ResidualNoise | DistributionNoise
            What an observation shows around a draw's prediction, with no
            default: ``NoNoise()`` gives a band of the model,
            ``ResidualNoise(...)`` and ``DistributionNoise()`` a prediction
            interval. Both need a calibrator: residuals come from a fit, and
            observation models from a problem.

        ObservationDraws

        Raises

        ValueError
            If an observation names an unknown output or factor, a series the
            residual noise has no residuals of, or a series with no
            observation model; `DistributionNoise` comes with a problem that
            has a loss; or the noise is not `NoNoise()` and the source is an
            analysis.
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a draw leaves the values its model allows.
        """
        draws = self.source.rust_observation_draws(
            self.sample, list(observed_data), noise

def __init__(
    self,
    source: PredictiveSource,
    sample: ParameterSample,
    positions: Sequence[float],
):
    """
    Run every draw of `sample` at `positions`.

def band(self, confidence_level: float) -> PredictiveBand:
    """
    The band of every output.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    PredictiveBand
        The weighted mean, median and central interval of each output at
        each position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.band(confidence_level)

    def by_output(table: list[list[float]]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        return {
            name: [row[index] for row in table]
            for index, name in enumerate(self.output_names)
        }

    return PredictiveBand(
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        positions=self.positions,
        mean=by_output(mean),
        median=by_output(median),
        lower=by_output(lower),
        upper=by_output(upper),
    )

def series_band(
    self,
    outputs: Sequence[str],
    confidence_level: float,
    cumulative: bool = False,
) -> SeriesBand:
    """
    The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total.

    Each draw is reduced to the series first, then the series are reduced
    across the draws.

    Parameters
    ----------
    outputs : Sequence[str]
        The outputs summed.
    confidence_level : float
        Strictly between 0 and 1.
    cumulative : bool, optional
        Whether the series is the running total along the positions.

    Returns
    -------
    SeriesBand
        One value per position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an output is unknown or the confidence level is out of range.
    """
    unknown = [name for name in outputs if name not in self.output_names]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown outputs {unknown}. Outputs: {self.output_names}."
        )
    indices = [self.output_names.index(name) for name in outputs]
    mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.series_band(
        indices, cumulative, confidence_level
    )
    return SeriesBand(
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        positions=self.positions,
        mean=mean,
        median=median,
        lower=lower,
        upper=upper,
    )
