docs.title: Repository Map
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Use this page when you know what to change but not where it belongs.

docs.title: Rust crates
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here crates/commol-core/src/types/ The model data types shared by all crates and serialized from Python: Model (header, engine, process, structure), Process (process.rs: bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions; the names NEIGHBORS and NEIGHBORS_PREFIX), ModelStructure (one variant per kind, tagged by kind), Aggregate (aggregate.rs: InitialConditions, Neighbors and their checks, AggregateVariant), Transition (transitions.rs), …; types/test_kind.rs only with the test-kind feature. Engine behavior. crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs EngineType, the one list of engines (model types): per entry, the model kinds it runs (kinds, engines_of; ModelKind, with the value types it accepts, ModelValueType), the form of its dynamics (DynamicsForm: its schedule and the left-hand side of its equations), its settings and their validation, and the meaning of a rate. ModelEngine, the engine and settings of a model. The engines themselves. crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/ Parsing, preprocessing and evaluation of rate expressions; the Cranelift JIT and its global cache (jit/). Model-specific variables. crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs The SimulationEngine trait, for an engine of any kind: runs at positions (check_position), outputs (output_names, state_outputs, output_sums), parameters, reset, the seed of a stochastic engine (set_seed), and the values of its kind (plan_values, apply_values, ValuePlan); Trajectory, check_positions, run_replicates (one run per seed, in parallel). What calibration needs from any engine. Code for one engine or one kind. crates/commol-random/ What every stochastic engine shares and no model: the generator (Generator, Xoshiro256PlusPlus seeded by SplitMix64), replicate_seed, the samplers (sample: exponential, Poisson, binomial, multinomial), SumTree, the rates of a set of events, and latin_hypercube on the unit cube. Anything of a model or an engine. crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs Expansion of the bins and accumulators of a process over its stratifications (expand, expand_compartments, expand_accumulators), the initial state (initial_state), the checks of an aggregate model (check_model: variant, neighbors, names, whole units for a stochastic engine; as_whole), the subgroup total names (subgroup_total_names), impulse schedules and the compilation into CompiledModel (try_from_model). Flow planning; stepping. crates/commol-model/src/layout.rs CompartmentLayout: compartments in engine order with their labels, and lookups by bin and categories. Name parsing. crates/commol-model/src/labels.rs OutputLabels (bin and categories of an output) and output_sums (bin totals and partial totals). Name parsing. crates/commol-model/src/engine.rs CompartmentalEngine: what a compartmental engine gives besides SimulationEngine (compartments, labels, state, total, set_initial_condition). Code for one engine. crates/commol-model/src/initial_conditions.rs How initial-condition values reach a compartmental engine (InitialConditionPlan: resolution, layers, remainder); both engines' plan_values and apply_values use it. Parameter values. crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs Transition flow planning (plan_transition_flows), the sums the neighbors of a unit are (resolve_neighbors), and the description of the flows for Python (describe_flows). Rate evaluation at run time. crates/commol-model/src/helpers.rs Stratified-rate resolution and rate rewriting helpers. New public API. crates/commol-model/src/rates.rs Evaluation of a compiled rate: fast path, JIT with resolved slots, evalexpr fallback. Flow logic. crates/commol-model/src/system.rs The flows every engine reads: flow_rates (the value of each flow), transition_rates (its rate), flow_changes (the change of one event of each flow), the right-hand side derivatives built on them; impulses (apply_impulses, impulse_rates, impulse_changes, impulse_positions); the positions where a rate can jump (breakpoints, reads_time); the accessors the engines use. Stepping along the axis. crates/commol-model/src/types.rs CompiledModel, compiled flows, FlowChange (one event of a flow), impulse schedules, series lookup (SeriesParameter). Python types. crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs DifferenceEquations: the discrete step (state += derivatives), impulses at integer steps, the positions it accepts (integers), and its SimulationEngine and CompartmentalEngine implementations. Model compilation. crates/commol-differential/src/lib.rs DifferentialEquations: state, output positions, impulses, and its SimulationEngine and CompartmentalEngine implementations. Numerical methods. crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs The integration with diffsol: pieces between the breakpoints of the model, the finite-difference J·v, dense or sparse matrices (SPARSE_THRESHOLD). Model compilation. crates/commol-stochastic/src/events.rs StochasticEvents: whole units one event at a time (the direct method, with a time change when a rate reads t) or in leaps (tau-leaping, fixed or chosen as Cao, Gillespie and Petzold 2006 do), stopping at the breakpoints; its SimulationEngine and CompartmentalEngine implementations. Samplers; flows. crates/commol-stochastic/src/steps.rs StochasticSteps: the chain binomial (one multinomial per source, capped Poisson draws for absolute flows) and the check of its per-step probabilities. Samplers; flows. crates/commol-stochastic/src/units.rs What both stochastic engines share: the generator, the whole start of a run (largest_remainder, random_rounding) and impulses that move whole units. Anything of one engine. crates/commol-calibration/src/calibration_problem.rs CalibrationProblem: the layers below, built once (new, with_replicates, with_observation_normalization, with_initial_condition_remainder), a copy with other observed values and weights (with_data), a copy whose runs also report at the positions of other observations (observing), the one evaluation of a point (evaluate), the predictions of one seeded run (predict_once), and the position check that names an observation or constraint (check_positions). It uses only SimulationEngine. Penalties; optimizer setup; anything of one model kind. crates/commol-calibration/src/forward.rs ForwardModel: every clone, reset, write of values and run of the engine (run_schedule, run_observed, run_at), one run per replicate of a stochastic engine, or one run seeded by its caller (run_once); the same model on other observations (with_observations), or with none (unobserved); Workspace. Loss, penalties, history. crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs ObservationOperator: one prediction per observation from the rows of a run (rows, sums of outputs, windows, factors). Comparison with data. crates/commol-calibration/src/feasibility.rs Feasibility (bounds, constraints), Violation and EvaluationError. Penalties. crates/commol-calibration/src/discrepancy.rs Discrepancy and DiscrepancyConfig: the loss, or the negative log-likelihood of observation models, of predictions against the data, with weights, per-series normalization of a loss and the summary of the replicates; the discrepancy of one run (of_run); the base of the penalty (penalty_base). Running engines. crates/commol-calibration/src/likelihood/ The observation models: ObservationModel and Argument (likelihood/mod.rs), Likelihood (the model and trials of each observation, the checks of models, noise parameters and observed values, the pointwise log-likelihood), Noise (density.rs: a model with numbers for its noise, its log density, the means it allows, its scores and Fisher information), TermDerivatives (the gradient and the expected curvature of each observation's term, also of a loss through Discrepancy::term_derivatives). Draws; running engines. crates/commol-calibration/src/objective.rs OptimizationObjective: the argmin cost function, the only place that turns a violation into a penalty; the history decorator. Recording history inside the objective. crates/commol-calibration/src/starts.rs The starts of a multi-start optimization (start_points: the guess, then a Latin hypercube) and optimize_starts, in parallel. Statistics. crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs LossConfig (every loss, and replicate_loss), ReplicateSummary, crps and weighted_crps, Replicates, the observation, parameter, constraint and result types. Optimizer setup. crates/commol-calibration/src/values.rs How calibrated values reach any engine: parameters by id, values of the model kind through the engine (ValueWriter, check_model_values, configured_engine). How a kind resolves its values. crates/commol-calibration/src/optimization.rs Nelder-Mead and particle swarm setup on the argmin fork, from a start point (optimize, optimize_from, optimize_with_history, optimize_with_observer), and on a subproblem (optimize_subproblem: a smaller search space, or the augmented Lagrangian of the fork around the problem's optimizer); no output to the process streams. Loss definitions; numerical methods that know no model, such as the sine transform of the bounds or the handling of a NaN cost by the swarm (the argmin fork). crates/commol-calibration/src/subproblem.rs Subproblem: the problem with one parameter held (left out of the search) or one prediction held (an equality constraint, ConstraintSettings); predict, the value of a prediction; SubproblemResult. Stepping along a profile; thresholds. crates/commol-inference/src/statistics.rs The one quantile (weighted, midpoints of the cumulative weights; Hazen with equal weights), weighted mean and covariance, Kish's effective size. Quantiles anywhere else. crates/commol-inference/src/sample.rs ParameterSample: weighted draws, their invariants and statistics, resampling. What a method does. crates/commol-inference/src/predictive.rs Predictive (the run of every draw, its bands), observation_draws through the observation operator, the ObservationNoise port (one draw's whole vector), NoNoise, and DistributionNoise with the draw of each observation model. Noise models of one method. crates/commol-inference/src/resampling/ Fits to reweighted or resampled data: blocks.rs (BlockScheme, the automatic block length), residuals.rs (Residuals on a scale, residuals by series and position), resamplers.rs (the Resampler port, Perturbation, the Bayesian, residual and wild bootstraps, ParametricResampler), runner.rs (ReplicateRunner, bootstrap), jackknife.rs (block_jackknife), noise.rs (ResidualNoise). Changes to the problem other than through with_data. crates/commol-inference/src/conformal/ Conformal prediction intervals: score.rs (NonconformityScore, Pooling, ConformalSettings, the scale of a score), quantile.rs (the conformal quantile, the order statistics of jackknife+), intervals.rs (PredictionIntervals, ConformalRun), predict.rs (predictions and spread at any observations, the target points), and one file per variant: split.rs, rolling.rs, jackknife_plus.rs (with cv_plus_bound), enbpi.rs, adaptive.rs (AdaptiveLevel). A second quantile or score of one variant. crates/commol-inference/src/scores.rs Coverage, interval score, weighted interval score, sample CRPS, PIT, the log score of observation models, and their means per series. — crates/commol-inference/src/sensitivity/ SensitivitySource, the port of derivatives of the predicted observations; FiniteDifferences on the design of the observations or a dense one; the scaled sensitivities and observation_scales. Ranks, verdicts. crates/commol-inference/src/design.rs, quantity.rs, batch.rs What a design-based method shares: InputSpace (independent distributions or a sample) and its designs (Latin hypercube, Morris trajectories, the Saltelli matrices, the scale F(x)); Quantity and Quantities, read through the observation operator; BatchRunner, every point through a forward model in parallel, replicate by replicate or as their mean. Estimators. crates/commol-inference/src/global_sensitivity/ analysis.rs (ForwardAnalysis: the forward model, the inputs and the seed streams, and each method in one call), and the estimators: prcc.rs (weighted PRCC and its test), morris.rs, sobol.rs (with the bootstrap of rows), chaos.rs (ChaosExpansion, a surrogate). Designs; code of one engine. crates/commol-inference/src/identifiability/ The analyses: structural_rank (ranks, null space, combinations), collinearity (Brun's indices), sample_identifiability (contraction, correlations, modes), starts_identifiability. Derivatives; reports. crates/commol-inference/src/profiles/ Profile likelihood: tracer.rs (ProfileTracer, the adaptive step and the secant start, Profile and its interval), threshold.rs (chi_square, beale, bootstrap_thresholds), verdict.rs (ProfileVerdict), resets.rs (read_structure: the resets of a flat profile, StructuralReading). Holding a quantity (a Subproblem's); optimizers. crates/commol-inference/src/target.rs Target (a log density, −∞ outside the support) and discrepancy_in_support. Penalties. crates/commol-inference/src/distribution.rs, special.rs Family and Distribution, one family truncated to the bounds of a parameter (density, distribution function, quantile, closed-form moments, draws by inversion); the special functions on libm. The quantile sets the bracket of the root and takes the root finder from the argmin fork (NewtonRoot). Distributions from a dependency, whose draws change with it; a root finder of its own. crates/commol-inference/src/priors.rs Priors: one distribution per parameter, the check of their bounds, the joint density and draws. Defaults of a prior. crates/commol-inference/src/transform.rs Transform: the unbounded scale a move proposes on (logit, log or identity by the bounds) and its log Jacobian. Kernels. crates/commol-inference/src/local/ Local approximations at a fit: Curvature (Gauss–Newton or the stepped Hessian of the finitediff crate of the argmin fork, on the unbounded scale, with the term gradients), CurvatureKind and laplace_approximation (approximation.rs), Gaussian and laplace (gaussian.rs), delta_band (band.rs), sandwich, block_meat and sandwich_approximation (sandwich.rs), laplace_mixture (mixture.rs). Finite-difference formulas of their own; samplers. crates/commol-inference/src/psis.rs, importance.rs Pareto-smoothed importance sampling (smooth, k̂); importance_sample of a Target from a Proposal on the unbounded scale, and TemperedPosterior, the last level of a TemperedTarget as a Target. Proposals of one method. crates/commol-inference/src/smc/ Sequential Monte Carlo: the TemperedTarget port (smc/mod.rs), SmcSampler, next_level and abc_rejection (sampler.rs), the Kernel port and RandomWalk (kernel.rs), GibbsTarget with the calibrations of η (gibbs.rs), AbcTarget with its distances (abc.rs), LikelihoodTarget and bayesian_posterior (likelihood.rs). Anything of one target in the sampler.

docs.title: PyO3 bindings
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here py-commol/src/core.rs Bindings of the model types (Model, Process, Aggregate, …). Logic. py-commol/src/model.rs The queries of commol_rs.model on a process and its aggregate structure: initial_state, expanded_outputs, transition_flows, subgroup_total_names; check_model on a model; the names NEIGHBORS and NEIGHBORS_PREFIX. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/engine.rs commol_rs.engine: Engine::build (the four engines of the aggregate kind and those of the test kind), which checks the kind and builds the implementation of the pair of an EngineType entry and the kind of the structure, and the Python classes Engine (any engine, built from a model), EngineType (the list, for Python to ask) and ModelKind. Engine logic. py-commol/src/test_kind.rs TestEngine and TestStochasticEngine, the engines of the test model kind; only with the test-kind feature. Anything a release needs. py-commol/src/calibration.rs The calibration types (observations, parameters, constraints, loss, optimizers, results) and the checks that take an Engine. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/identifiability.rs commol_rs.inference: structural_rank, collinearity, sample_identifiability, starts_identifiability and their result classes. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/smc.rs commol_rs.inference: Distribution, the priors as Python passes them, the runners of the sequential Monte Carlo methods (gibbs_posterior, bayesian_posterior, information_matching_eta, bootstrap_coverage_eta, abc_smc, abc_rejection) and SmcRun, EtaCoverage. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/local.rs commol_rs.inference: the runners of the local approximations (laplace, sandwich, delta_band, laplace_mixture) and LocalRun, MixtureRun. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/conformal.rs commol_rs.inference: check_conformal_settings, the runners of the conformal methods (split_conformal, rolling_conformal, jackknife_plus, enbpi, adaptive_conformal) and ConformalRun. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/sensitivity.rs commol_rs.inference: ForwardAnalysis, the wrapper of the Rust type (one call per method, the predictive, the observation draws with no noise), chaos_evaluate, SobolRun, ChaosRun. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/inference.rs commol_rs.inference: CalibrationProblem (built once from a Calibrator, with a loss or observation models: starts, history, predictions, the predictive, the log score, the pointwise log-likelihood), ParameterSample, Predictive, ObservationDraws, BootstrapRun, JackknifeRun, weighted_quantiles, weighted_mean, by_series, quantile_error; the runners of methods (the bootstraps, parametric_bootstrap, jackknife). Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/profiles.rs commol_rs.inference: trace_profiles, BootstrapSettings, Profile, ProfileRun. Logic beyond type conversion. py-commol/src/python_observer.rs The progress table of a verbose optimization, written to Python's sys.stdout. Writes to the standard error. py-commol/commol/commol_rs/_commol_rs.pyi The type stub of the extension. Update it with every binding change. —

docs.title: Python package (py-commol/commol/)
docs.text: Path Owns Do not put here api/model_builder.py The fluent ModelBuilder, which writes the process; build(structure, engine) joins it with a structure. Validation rules that belong to the model; anything of one structure. api/simulation.py Simulation: runs (run, run_at, with the seed of a stochastic engine), replicates (replicates, ReplicateRuns), output grouping through ModelStructure.outputs_by_source. Expansion rules; which positions a model type accepts; anything of one model kind. api/results.py SimulationResults (values with their positions and seed), SimulationReplicates (runs with one seed each, and their statistics), index_at, sample. Engine rules. api/calibrator.py Calibrator: the one conversion of a problem to Rust types, run(starts=n), run_with_history, and the entry point uncertainty; check_values, the check of the values a calibration or an analysis sets. Loss or optimizer logic. api/sensitivity.py SensitivityAnalysis: the inputs, the replicates and the seed of an analysis, its forward model in Rust, and the entry point run. Estimators. api/inference/ What reads a sample: Predictive (predictive.py), the scores (api/inference/scores.py, exposed as commol.scores), the one interval convention (intervals.py: weighted_quantiles, member_statistics, ci_percentiles), the registry of method runners (registry.py), the runners of the identifiability methods (api/inference/identifiability.py), which build the report, the runners of the resampling methods (api/inference/resampling.py), of the sequential Monte Carlo methods (api/inference/smc.py), of the local approximations (api/inference/local.py), of the conformal methods (api/inference/conformal.py), which build ConformalResult, of the sensitivity methods (api/inference/global_sensitivity.py), and of the profiles (api/inference/profiles.py), which build ProfileResult. Transforms of predictions; quantile formulas. api/reporting.py simulation_report and applied_parameters_report, with the sections the structure adds (ModelStructure.report_sections). Domain vocabulary; sections of one model kind. api/patterns.py, api/windows.py Rates that change along the axis (AxisPattern), the window grid and windowed totals. Physical units inside the model. api/plotter.py Plots of results, of the bands of a Predictive, of sensitivity results (plot_prcc, plot_morris, plot_sobol) and of profiles (plot_profiles). Computation of results. context/inference/ InferenceMethod and its kinds UncertaintyMethod, IdentifiabilityMethod and SensitivityMethod (method.py), ParameterSample, SampleMethod, ParameterSummary, the identifiability methods and IdentifiabilityReport (context/inference/identifiability.py), the observation noise (noise.py: NoNoise, ResidualNoise, DistributionNoise), the distributions and Priors (distributions.py), and the settings and results of the resampling methods (context/inference/resampling.py), of the sequential Monte Carlo methods (context/inference/smc.py: GibbsPosterior, BayesianPosterior, EtaCalibration, AbcSmc, AbcRejection, the distances, SmcResult, GibbsResult), of the local approximations (context/inference/local.py: Laplace, Sandwich, LaplaceMixture, its targets, LaplaceResult, SandwichResult, DeltaBand, ImportanceResult), of the conformal methods (context/inference/conformal.py), of the sensitivity methods with InputSpace and the quantities of interest (context/inference/global_sensitivity.py), and of the profiles (context/inference/profiles.py: ProfileLikelihood, PredictionProfile, PredictionSpec, Threshold, ProfileResult). Runners. api/description.py The renderers of a ModelDescription: text, Markdown (Mermaid), LaTeX, JSON and Graphviz DOT, and save. Anything of one model kind: a renderer reads only blocks. context/ The Pydantic model: fields, validation, JSON I/O, update methods. Engine rules. context/model.py Model: the header, the engine, the process and the structure of any kind, generic in its structure class (Model[Aggregate]). Anything of one model kind. context/process.py Process: bins, accumulators, stratifications and transitions, and the checks of the process by itself. Checks that depend on a structure. context/structure.py ModelStructure, the interface every model kind gives the generic layers, and its registry of kinds and variants. Code of one kind. context/aggregate.py Aggregate: the initial amounts and the neighbors, their checks against the process, and the aggregate side of the interface. Generic code. context/initial_conditions.py InitialConditions, the fields and the fraction logic Aggregate holds. Checks against the process. context/neighbors.py Complete and Groups, who the neighbors of a unit are. How the terms resolve (the engine's). context/description.py ModelDescription and its blocks (Text, Table, Equations, StateGraph, Matrix): a description as data. Rendering; code of one kind. context/transition.py Transition and StratifiedRate. — context/observation_models.py The observation models of a calibration problem (NormalObservations, …, BinomialObservations, the union ObservationModel), as settings. Densities and checks (the engine's). context/axis_units.py AxisUnits: values in units to steps of the axis, and rates asked from the engine (Model.axis_units). Formulas of a rate per engine (they are in RateMeaning). context/engine.py ModelEngine (Model.engine: the engine type and its settings, read with the class of that engine), the settings classes OdeSolver, StochasticEventsSettings and StochasticStepsSettings, Rounding, and the names of the engines as the Literal EngineName. Settings validation or engine meanings: ask commol_rs.engine.EngineType. context/_model/engine_state.py The only Python access to the engine queries, and build_engine, which builds the engine the model names. Python re-implementations of them. context/_model/describe.py The sections every kind shares and the layouts of a description ("default", "odd"). Sections of one kind. context/_model/ (other files) Internals of an aggregate model: the sections of its description (aggregate_description.py, and the equations, event table and state graphs of _model/equations.py), unit checker, calibration write-back, the initial_conditions report section (report.py); JSON rendering of any model. Public API. context/report_entry.py The spread of a report entry from the summary of a sample (Interval, entry_interval), for every kind. — utils/security.py Validation of every user expression (SecurityConfig limits). Expression evaluation. utils/equations.py Dimensional analysis with pint. —

docs.title: Other paths
docs.text: Path Owns py-commol/tests/ Python tests: one package per page of the user guide (building/, transitions/, rates/, axis_patterns/, initial_conditions/, simulation/, stochastic/, units/, calibration/, uncertainty/, reporting/, plotting/, docs/); reference_models/, published models checked against their stated results; model_kinds/, the test model kind through every generic layer; suite/, the checks of the rules of the tests; and support/ with the shared model factories, the test kind (kinds.py), the test uncertainty method (methods.py), the coverage harness (coverage.py), the flow models, the reference solver, the oracles and the assertions. See Tests. crates/*/tests/, #[cfg(test)] modules Rust tests. docs/ This site. docs/codebase/ is for maintainers; the rest is for users. .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ The templates of a proposal, a bug or small change, and a release (Planning). .github/scripts/start.sh Start an issue: write the links of the releases (parallel.py --releases), check the issue, take it, set it to In Progress, and create its branch and worktree, linked to the issue; then refresh the precedence levels (parallel.py --levels). .github/scripts/next.sh The next proposals and changes to implement: open, not blocked, not taken, not touching an issue in progress, by priority, milestone and number, after it writes the links of the releases and refreshes the precedence levels (parallel.py --releases --levels --next). .github/scripts/parallel.py The proposals and changes that can run in parallel, from their Touches or Where and the links of the open issues; --next gives the next ones, --releases writes the links of the releases (Milestones), and --levels writes the precedence level of each open issue into the field Level of the project. .github/scripts/github.py The REST calls of parallel.py: every page, and one line that says why GitHub refused a request. .github/scripts/affected.py The open issues that the changes of a branch affect: those whose body names a changed path. .github/scripts/release_notes.py The notes of a GitHub release, from its section of the changelog. .github/workflows/ CI: code quality, build, docs, release, and the coverage studies (coverage.yaml), which Build and the release call.

docs.title: Placement rule
docs.text:
Place code at the narrowest owner that can hold it:

  1. A rule about how a model becomes numbers → a Rust crate.
  2. Type conversion between Python and Rust → py-commol/src/.
  3. Validation of user input → the Pydantic model in context/.
  4. User-facing workflow → api/.
  5. Presentation (reports, plots) → api/reporting.py, api/plotter.py.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Where a Python test goes, how it builds its model, what it must check, and how long it may take. The Python tests live in py-commol/tests/; the Rust tests are #[cfg(test)] modules and the tests/ folder of each crate.

docs.title: Layout: one package per guide page
docs.text:
A test goes in the package of the guide page that documents the behavior it checks, so "where is the test of X" has the same answer as "where is the guide of X". A pure-Python helper (utils/security.py, context/axis_units.py, api/inference/intervals.py) goes in the package of its feature. The exceptions are reference_models/, which checks published models across features (see Reference models), and model_kinds/, which runs a model kind that is not aggregate through every generic layer.

Package Tests of Guide page building/ The builder, parameters, stratifications, reserved names, save and load Building Models transitions/ Flows, $compartment, stratified rates, impulses Transitions rates/ Formulas, functions, variables, expression security Mathematical Expressions axis_patterns/ AxisPattern formulas, runs and schedules Axis Patterns initial_conditions/ Bin, stratification and compartment fractions; the initial state Building Models simulation/ Runs, run_at, results and their positions, differential models, outputs, the window grid and windowed totals, AxisUnits Running Simulations stochastic/ The stochastic engines of an aggregate model through the layers: their means against the deterministic engines, whole units, calibration with replicates (the closed forms are in crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs) Stochastic Simulation units/ Unit checks Units description/ Model.describe, its sections and blocks, the renderers and their snapshots (description/snapshots/), the equations of the dynamics (equation_forms in support/description.py) Describing a Model calibration/ One file per calibration page: test_problem.py, test_optimizers.py, test_starts.py, test_constraints.py, test_observations.py, test_initial_conditions.py, test_write_back.py Model Calibration and its sub-pages uncertainty/ The parameter sample, the one quantile, the predictive, the scores, the entry points Calibrator.uncertainty and SensitivityAnalysis.run, and the coverage harness (test_coverage.py, marker coverage_study) Uncertainty reporting/ Reports Reports plotting/ SimulationPlotter Running Simulations docs/ The documentation examples and the API coverage (marker docs) — reference_models/ Published models against their stated results, one module per model family — (across features) model_kinds/ The test model kind (support/kinds.py) through a simulation, a calibration, a report and a plot; the check that an engine runs its kind; the variants of a structure (UnstratifiedVariant). It needs the extension built with --features test-kind. — (across features; Design decisions) suite/ The rules of this page that a program can check (test_rules.py), and the plugin that records how long each test takes (durations.py) — support/ No tests: the code the tests share —

Keep a test module under about 600 lines. When it grows past that, split it by topic inside its package.

docs.title: Models: use the factories
docs.text:
• Build models with the factories of tests/support/models.py: abc_builder (A → B → C), abcd_builder (A → B → C → D) and a_to_b_builder, and the special models override_builder, shared_category_builder and conditional_pathway_builder. A factory returns a FactoryBuilder: a ModelBuilder of the process and the Aggregate that lays it out (builder.structure, which set_structure replaces). A keyword overrides one part of the default model, so a test names only what it changes. build builds for difference equations; build_ode builds for differential equations, with the tight solver settings TIGHT by default; build_stochastic builds for a stochastic engine (STOCHASTIC_ENGINES, and MEAN_FIELD, the deterministic engine of each); run builds and simulates.
  • Build a model by hand only when one test needs it and no factory keyword expresses it. A model that a second file needs goes to support/.
  • Test models use abstract names, as examples do: bins A, B, C, parameters k1, k2, categories g1, t1. Only tests/reference_models/ and the support code that only it uses (support/oracles.py, support/flows.py) keep the names of their published source.
  • Fixtures: abc_model and abc_simulation (tests/conftest.py); truth and truth_run (tests/calibration/conftest.py). A fixture is function-scoped unless its cost is measured; a wider scope never holds an object a test can change. A class-scoped fixture is never an instance method (removed in pytest 10).

docs.title: Every test checks a result
docs.text:
A test compares a result with an oracle:

Oracle Example A value computed by hand in the test reference_run (tests/support/reference.py) evaluates the flows in plain Python, as the engine does: every flow from the state at the start of the step, no clamping. tests/rates/test_formulas.py compares whole trajectories with it. An analytic value An outflow rate d on every bin gives total(t) = total(0) (1 - d)^t (tests/transitions/test_compartment_placeholder.py). An invariant A total that the model keeps (assert_total_conserved); two paths that must agree, such as a bin id and the explicit sum of its compartments. What a stated result predicts about a run tests/support/oracles.py, for the reference models: final_size solves the final size relation, assert_threshold checks that a model grows at a reproduction number of 1.05 and decays at 0.95, settled reads a limit once doubling the horizon no longer moves it.

"It runs" is not a result. A test whose only check is that no exception occurs is allowed only when the exception is its subject, such as a validator that accepts a valid input; it calls assert_accepted(check, *args) (tests/support/assertions.py), which fails with the message of the rejection.

A test checks the behavior of commol. It does not check:

  • the behavior of Python, pydantic, NumPy or another library, such as a str path that pathlib accepts, or an unknown keyword that Python rejects;
  • a default of a pydantic model or of a binding;
  • an attribute read back as the test set it;
  • the absence of an API that was removed: that is history, not behavior.

tests/suite/test_rules.py checks the part of this that a program can read: every Python test has an assert, a pytest.raises, pytest.warns or pytest.fail, a call of np.testing.assert_*, or a call of a helper of tests/ that has one; every Rust test has an assert*!, panic! or unreachable!, calls a function of its crate that has one, is #[should_panic], or returns a Result. Review checks the rest.

docs.title: Duplicates
docs.text:
Two tests do not check the same behavior with the same inputs. Candidates come from the coverage of each test:

COVERAGE_CORE=ctrace pytest --cov=commol --cov-context=test --cov-report=

The sysmon core, the default of coverage on Python 3.14, records a line only for the first test that runs it, so it gives most tests no context. Two tests of one module whose covered lines are equal, or one inside the other, are a candidate. Coverage does not decide: two tests can run the same lines and check different results. Read both, and keep one only when the other checks nothing that it does not: the same output for the same input, or a weaker check of the same output ("+" in formula against the exact formula).

docs.title: Tolerances
docs.text:
• assert_close(actual, expected, rel=…, abs=…) (tests/support/assertions.py) needs a stated tolerance, and reports the key and the index of the first difference.
  • ENGINE_REL = 1e-9 compares the engine with a hand computation of the same arithmetic: only the order of the floating-point operations differs.
  • ODE_REL = 1e-6 compares a differential model with a closed form, a final size or an equilibrium. flow_model solves with FINE (TIGHT with atol = 1e-12), so the error of a value near zero stays below its own size.
  • pytest.approx with its default (relative 1e-6) suits a single value computed by hand.
  • An optimizer result states the tolerance its convergence allows, for example abs=1e-5 for Nelder-Mead on noise-free data.
  • np.testing.assert_allclose skips masked values. Read the points of a matplotlib collection as floats (np.asarray(offsets, dtype=float), as _scatter in tests/plotting/test_plotter.py does), so a point at None is NaN and fails.

docs.title: Reference models
docs.text:
tests/reference_models/ shows that commol can state published models and computes their stated results. A module holds one model family and is named after the published model (test_pulse_vaccination.py); a test checks one stated result (test_the_fixed_point_starts_the_periodic_orbit).

  • Attribution. The module docstring has a References section in the NumPy format with the original papers of the model and of its parameter values (authors, year, title, journal, DOI). A value or a result taken from a paper cites it in a comment next to the value. A model with no primary source is not added.
  • Independent oracle. The expected value comes from the stated result, computed with math or numpy: a closed form, a root of the final size relation, a spectral radius. A test never compares commol with commol. A quantity that commol does not output, such as a reproduction number, is checked through what it predicts about a run (tests/support/oracles.py).
  • Equations. To check that a model has the stated equations, increments reads its right-hand side at one state: a difference-equation step adds the flows of the state it starts from, and both engines compile the same flows.
  • Tolerances. ENGINE_REL for a discrete model, ODE_REL for a differential one; an asymptotic result is read with settled, and the test states its horizon.
  • Gaps. A model that commol cannot state, or computes wrong, gets a test marked as Skips, expected failures and ignored tests says, with the open issue of the finding.

To add a test, write the model with Flow and flow_model (tests/support/flows.py) from the initial value of each bin, compute the stated result in the test, and cite the papers.

docs.title: Skips, expected failures and ignored tests
docs.text:
• An xfail is strict=True and its reason starts with the open issue that fixes it (reason="#196: …"): the fix makes the test pass, and the strict marker then fails the run until the fix removes it.
  • A test that skips when an optional dependency is missing runs in at least one CI job: the dev extra installs pydot, and Python Coverage and the job Test of Build on Ubuntu install latexmk.
  • A Rust #[ignore] gives a reason with the cargo test command that runs it, such as the benchmarks of crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs. A benchmark also asserts that the methods it times give the same result.

tests/suite/test_rules.py checks the xfail markers and the reasons of #[ignore].

docs.title: Time budget
docs.text:
A test takes at most 1 s, setup and teardown included, in the job Test of Build on Ubuntu, which runs every test without coverage. Coverage slows a test that runs much Python up to ten times, so the run under coverage (Python Coverage) skips the check, and so does a run off Linux. A test over 0.5 s stays only if it checks what no faster test checks, with the smallest inputs that still check it: a shorter horizon, fewer steps, fewer replicates. tests/suite/durations.py records the time of each test, and test_slow_tests_are_listed runs last and fails on a test over the budget that the table below does not list.

The coverage studies (coverage_study) are the one exception. A study counts how often an interval covers the truth over hundreds of synthetic data sets; fewer data sets widen its tolerance until it checks nothing, so it cannot shrink to the budget. They do not run less often than the code they check: Build runs them for every pull request that changes what they run, and the release runs them before it publishes (CI pipelines). test_every_coverage_study_runs_in_a_group_of_the_workflow checks that coverage.yaml runs each of them, and test_the_studies_run_for_a_change_of_any_crate_they_use that a change of commol-inference, of a crate it depends on or of the engines of their models (difference and stochastic) runs them.

The check reads the wall time of the run, so a machine that runs other work at the same time can exceed the budget. pytest --durations=20 shows the slowest tests; Python Coverage prints them, slowed by coverage. A row names a test, or one case of a parametrized test with its parameter in brackets.

Test Why it takes longer tests/description/test_rendering.py::TestLatex::test_the_latex_document_compiles It compiles the LaTeX description with latexmk; the first TeX run of the job loads its formats. No other test checks that the document compiles. tests/docs/test_examples.py::test_page_examples_run[docs/guide/simulations.md] It runs every example of the page, which draws and saves four figures with matplotlib, one label per plotted position; the figures are what the page documents.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
Back to Design decisions

What weights, bounds, the observation operator and constraints mean in a calibration.

docs.title: One meaning of an observation weight
docs.text:
LossConfig::term and LossConfig::finish in crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs compute every loss: sse is Σ w·r², rmse is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w), mae is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. The likelihood of observation models (Likelihood::pointwise in crates/commol-calibration/src/likelihood/mod.rs) is Σ w·log p: a weight is a power of its term, so a weight of 2 counts the observation twice in a likelihood as in every loss. The discrepancy (discrepancy.rs) calls them for the optimizer and for every method that reads the loss.

Rule: never write a loss formula or a log density of an observation elsewhere.

Guards: commol-calibration/src/types.rs loss_tests; discrepancy::tests; crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_likelihood.rs::a_weight_of_two_is_the_observation_twice.

docs.title: A problem has a loss or observation models
docs.text:
A Discrepancy measures predictions by a loss or by the negative log-likelihood of one observation model per series label (DiscrepancyConfig), never both: the fit and the posterior would answer different questions about one problem. Neither has a default, because what to fit is a modelling choice. A model takes the prediction of the observation operator as its mean and only adds the scatter; its noise arguments are numbers or parameters of type Noise, which the value writer skips, as it skips factors. What only makes sense for a loss refuses observation models: normalize_observations, the replicate summaries of a stochastic engine (the likelihood of a summary ignores the noise of the process), LossDistance of ABC and information matching of η.

Alternative Why not Both, the loss for the optimizer and the likelihood for samplers The fit and the posterior would answer different questions. Keep "sse" by default and refuse only a loss written next to models The rule would depend on whether a field was written, and the library would choose what to fit. A noise parameter of type parameter The value writer would send it to the engine, and reports would mix it with model parameters. Densities from a dependency Their values change with its version; SciPy reference values in a test check ours.

Guards: crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_likelihood.rs, tests/uncertainty/test_observation_models.py.

docs.title: Nelder-Mead searches inside the bounds
docs.text:
The objective clamps values to their bounds, so the loss is flat outside them, and a simplex that crosses a bound collapses there. Nelder-Mead therefore searches an unbounded u and scores x = lo + (hi − lo)·(sin u + 1)/2 (SineTransform and BoundedProblem of the argmin fork, in argmin::core::bounds; SearchSpace::transform in optimization.rs builds the transform and refuses an infinite bound). Its evaluations and its result are recorded in x. converged is true only for SolverConverged and TargetCostReached (optimization::converged). An error of the model at a vertex of the initial simplex stops the run with its message (NelderMead::init of the argmin fork returns it).

Rule: report and record values in x, never in u. Every optimizer run, the verbose one included, goes through optimization::run.

Guards: optimization::tests; tests/calibration/test_optimizers.py.

docs.title: A Simulation follows its model
docs.text:
Simulation keeps the JSON its engine was built from. run, engine and simulation_outputs compare it with model_dump_json() and rebuild the engine when it differs (Simulation._sync_engine), and run resets the engine first. Calibrator takes simulation.engine when it is created, so the check is in the property, not only in run.

Guard: tests/simulation/test_runs.py.

docs.title: One observation operator
docs.text:
ObservationOperator (crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs) is the only code that turns a run into observed quantities: the row of each observation, the sum of its outputs, its increment over its window and its factor. The loss, the predictions of PyCalibrationProblem, the predictive's at_observations and every score read it, and the plotter reads a windowed or scaled series of a predictive through it. The calibration problem is split into one layer per job, each in its own module: ForwardModel (forward.rs) is the only code that clones, resets, writes values to or runs the engine; Feasibility (feasibility.rs) checks bounds and constraints; Discrepancy (discrepancy.rs) compares predictions with data; OptimizationObjective (objective.rs) is the argmin cost function. CalibrationProblem holds them, is built once and has no interior mutability; the buffers of an evaluation are a Workspace per thread.

Rule: Python never transforms a prediction of a calibration problem or of a sample: their windows, sums, factors, normalization, quantiles and scores come from Rust. Calibrator builds the Rust problem once (commol_rs.inference.CalibrationProblem) and every call reads it. The helpers that present results already computed, such as windowed_totals (api/windows.py) for a run or its replicates, are not predictions; they must agree with the operator, which tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss checks.

Guards: observation::tests, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_predictive.rs::observation_draws_are_the_predictions_the_loss_compares, tests/uncertainty/test_predictive.py::TestObservations.

docs.title: Constraints bound the support
docs.text:
A point is feasible, or it violates the problem by an amount: a bound, a constraint, an infeasible start or run, a value that is not finite, or a predicted mean outside the means its observation model allows (Violation in feasibility.rs). Only OptimizationObjective turns a violation into a penalty, base × (1 + amount), where base (Discrepancy::penalty_base) is above the discrepancy of a poor fit: 1000 · n · max_obs² for a loss, and 1000 · Σ wᵢ tᵢ for observation models, with tᵢ the cost of observation i at the narrowest noise the bounds allow and a mean max_obs from it; at least 1e10. An inference method sees the same violation as the edge of the support: its log density is −∞ (discrepancy_in_support in crates/commol-inference/src/target.rs).

Alternative Why not The penalty for every method Its scale is arbitrary, so a sampler would give weight to infeasible points. Reject and draw again, with no value A profile or a Laplace fit needs the value at the edge. The base of a loss for a likelihood A normal model of a small sd costs more than it, so infeasible points would look better. The worst feasible cost seen so far State in the objective: the result would depend on the order of evaluations and on threads.

Guards: feasibility::tests, crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_infeasible_runs.rs, crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_likelihood.rs::the_penalty_is_above_every_feasible_cost.

docs.title: A subproblem holds one quantity fixed
docs.text:
Subproblem (crates/commol-calibration/src/subproblem.rs) holds one parameter or one prediction while optimize_subproblem (optimization.rs) fits the others with the problem's own optimizer. A held parameter leaves the search space (SearchSpace): the optimizer searches one dimension less, and the cost puts the fixed value back before it scores a point. A held prediction g(θ) = c is an equality constraint met by the augmented Lagrangian of the argmin fork, whose factory builds the problem's optimizer at each outer iteration: Nelder-Mead on the sine transform, from the point of the iteration before, or a swarm seeded by replicate_seed(seed, k). The prediction is read through the observation operator of a copy of the problem whose runs also report at its positions (CalibrationProblem::observing), so one run gives the objective and the constraint, and the cost keeps the constraint of the last point it scored. A point that is not feasible keeps its penalty and a constraint of 0. Each point starts from Algencan's scaled penalty; the multiplier is the warm start.

Alternative Why not Bounds [v, v] for a held parameter Nelder-Mead keeps a vertex for a dimension that moves nothing. A growing quadratic penalty on g − c It meets the constraint only as μ → ∞, and a large μ makes a narrow valley where Nelder-Mead stops early. A second run for the prediction Twice the model runs of each evaluation. μ = 100·|Δλ/Δc| from the two points before In the experiment of #132 (the ABC model of tests/support/ with a normal model, the problem of the_multiplier_of_a_prediction_profile_is_minus_its_slope), B at 30 took 5465 evaluations against 3179 with Algencan's μ₀, C at 24 5405 against 3175, for the same intervals and a mean error of the multipliers of 0.8e-4 against 1.2e-4; 10⁴·|Δλ/Δc| gained 4 %. The stop rule reads ‖g − c‖, which a small μ leaves large.

A swarm without stop rules runs each outer iteration to its max_iterations, so a held prediction stops at the outer limit and never reports convergence.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/tests/test_profiles.rs (fixing_a_parameter_at_the_fit_keeps_the_loss, fixing_a_prediction_at_the_fit_keeps_the_parameters, a_problem_observing_more_positions_scores_as_the_problem, a_swarm_fits_a_subproblem_and_repeats_from_its_seed).

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
Back to Design decisions

What every engine shares, and the rules of the difference, ODE and stochastic engines.

docs.title: One list of engines
docs.text:
EngineType (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs) is the one list of model types. An entry is an engine, named by its type (DifferenceEquations, DifferentialEquations, StochasticEvents, StochasticSteps): a method, not a kind. It names the model kinds it runs (EngineType::kinds; today all four run aggregate). Each entry validates its settings and says the form of its dynamics (DynamicsForm: the schedule a description shows and the left-hand side of its equations) and the meaning of a rate (per_step or continuous). Engine::build (py-commol/src/engine.rs) builds the engine of an entry. A model holds its engine and the settings of that engine, Model.engine = {type, settings}, because the engine sets what a rate means, so a saved model reproduces its runs.

Python asks the list (commol_rs.engine.EngineType): it builds the engine, writes the left-hand side of an equation and the schedule of a description, and checks settings through it, and never branches on an engine name. It keeps the names of the engines only as the Literal EngineName (context/engine.py), for static typing and completion of ModelBuilder.build; a test checks that it equals the entries of the list (test_the_python_names_equal_the_engines_of_the_list). ModelEngine.type is a str that the list checks, so a model can name an engine of any kind; its settings are read with the class of that engine (ModelEngine.settings_of_the_engine), so a model loads back with the class it was saved with. Generating the Literal from Rust would need a code-generation step for four names; the test catches the same drift. An entry names the kinds it runs, so another kind (for example an agent network) adds kinds to an entry or new entries, not a second meaning of the type; see One interface for every model kind.

The builder takes the structure, the engine and its settings where it chooses them, build(structure, engine, settings=None), so one builder builds a model for each structure and engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both.

Guards: crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs (tests), py-commol/src/engine.rs::every_entry_builds_its_engine_and_runs, tests/building/test_engine.py.

docs.title: Every engine reads one set of flows
docs.text:
A compiled model is a set of flows (crates/commol-model/src/system.rs): CompiledModel::flow_rates gives the value of each flow, its rate times its source for a proportional rate (transition_rates gives the rate alone), and CompiledModel::flow_changes gives the change of the state of one event of each flow: −1 for each source piece, +1 for each target piece and each accumulator. Every engine reads them, and none has flow logic of its own:

Engine Reads DifferenceEquations derivatives, Σ changes × flow, added once per step DifferentialEquations derivatives, integrated StochasticEvents flow_rates as propensities, and one event of flow_changes at a time StochasticSteps transition_rates as per-step probabilities, and the drawn number of events of each flow

derivatives is flow_changesᵀ · flow_rates, computed piece by piece in the order of the old right-hand side, so the deterministic runs did not change by a bit. The deterministic engines are the mean-field limits of the stochastic ones, which gives the main test oracle. The positions where a rate can jump come from the same model (CompiledModel::breakpoints), so the differential and the continuous-time stochastic engines stop at the same positions.

A rate that is not a number stops the run in every engine, with a RuntimeError that names the flow and the position: a calibration fails with the cause instead of a penalty for a run of NaN. derivatives checks the flows of both deterministic engines (check_flows); each stochastic engine checks its own rates. A flow that is not a number is not an error when a compartment of the state is not a number, because diffsol finds the sparse pattern of the Jacobian by passing NaN through J·v (The solver is diffsol).

Guards: crates/commol-model/tests/flows.rs (a_rate_that_is_not_a_number_names_its_flow_and_its_position, a_compartment_that_is_not_a_number_gives_flows_that_are_not_numbers), tests/simulation/test_runs.py::test_a_rate_that_is_not_a_number_stops_the_run, crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs::one_step_adds_the_derivatives_exactly, crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs (the_mean_of_many_runs_is_the_solution_of_the_ode, the_mean_of_many_chain_binomial_runs_is_the_difference_engine).

docs.title: A difference step never leaves an amount below zero
docs.text:
DifferenceEquations checks every compartment after the impulses of a step and after its flows (DifferenceEquations::step, settle in crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs). An amount below −10⁻¹² × total, the total at the start of the step, stops the run with SimulationError::Infeasible (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs). The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows that drain it (CompiledModel::outflows, impulse_outflows). The check reads the state and the right-hand side once, with no allocation, and the state stays as it was before the step. Accumulators are not checked: a net flow may count negative.

An error, for every cause, and not:

Alternative Why not A check only of proportional rates that sum above 1 None of the seven negative runs the test suite had broke that rule: they came from absolute rates on a bin total and from rates that turn negative. A warning A negative amount is never a correct state, and a warning inside a loop of calibrations is lost. Clamp the amount to zero The total is no longer kept, and the flows are no longer those of the model, without notice. Scale the outflows down to what the compartment holds A different model, chosen by the library; modelling choices belong to the user.

Calibration tells such a run from a failure by its type, not by its message. SimulationEngine returns SimulationError: Infeasible { position, message } for a state outside the values the model allows, and Failed(String) for every other error. The forward model turns an infeasible run into a Violation::InfeasibleRun and a failed one into EvaluationError::Failed (forward.rs); the optimization objective gives a violation a penalty and records nothing in the history; a failed run still stops the calibration, so a rate that cannot be evaluated does not hide behind a poor fit. An optimizer that explores the bounds of a rate would otherwise stop on the first infeasible point, though the fit lies elsewhere. A prediction of an infeasible draw raises InfeasibleStateError (prediction_error in py-commol/src/inference.rs). Python receives InfeasibleStateError, a ValueError (simulation_error in py-commol/src/engine.rs); a failed run stays a RuntimeError.

The differential engine is not checked: a solver may step below zero by its tolerance, and a model whose exact solution goes negative is a modelling choice there.

Guards: crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs (flows_that_move_more_than_a_compartment_holds_stop_the_first_step, a_rate_that_turns_negative_stops_the_step_where_an_amount_drops_below_zero, proportional_rates_that_sum_to_one_empty_a_compartment, an_impulse_that_moves_more_than_its_source_holds_stops_its_step, an_accumulator_may_count_a_negative_net_flow), crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_infeasible_runs.rs.

docs.title: Stochastic engines and seeds
docs.text:
A stochastic engine draws every random number from one generator seeded by SimulationEngine::set_seed (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs); reset restores it, so a run is reproducible from its seed. The default set_seed does nothing, so the deterministic engines did not change. EngineType::is_stochastic says which engines draw: StochasticEvents and StochasticSteps (crates/commol-stochastic/). A run does not depend on the positions it reports at: StochasticEvents measures each wait from the last change of the state, never from a reported position, and draws the flow of an event only when the event happens.

Part Rule Generator Xoshiro256PlusPlus of rand_xoshiro, seeded by four SplitMix64 numbers of the seed (Generator in crates/commol-random/). Its sequence is the same on every platform and version. Samplers Exponential, Poisson, binomial and multinomial written in commol-random/src/sample.rs, not taken from rand_distr, whose values may change in a minor version. A test holds the first values of each for a fixed seed. Replicates Replicate i of seed s takes replicate_seed(s, i), the SplitMix64 of s + i. run_replicates runs them in parallel (rayon); a deterministic engine has no replicates. Calibration Common random numbers: the same replicate seeds at every evaluation, so the loss is a deterministic function of the parameters (CalibrationProblem::with_replicates). The user chooses the summary (ReplicateSummary); LossConfig computes it.

Reproducibility has three levels: the same machine and commol version give the same run; another platform gives the same random numbers, but most rate functions come from the system's libm (address in math_expression/jit/libm.rs), which can differ in the last bit, so a run there is equal in distribution and rarely differs draw by draw; another commol version may change a run, and the changelog says so.

Alternative Why not A random source passed to every call The trait grows an argument that the deterministic engines ignore. The seed in the model file A model is a description; the seed belongs to a run, as CalibrationProblem.seed does. StdRng or SmallRng StdRng is slower and its security is not needed; SmallRng is documented as not portable. A pure-Rust libm for every function of the JIT pow takes 4 times as long (21 ns against 5 ns) and exp, log and sin about 40 % more, in every engine, for a difference in the last bit; the levels above are documented instead. The libm crate gives only the functions the standard library does not have (erf, erfc, tgamma, lgamma, the Bessel functions, fdim, remainder). The JIT looks each function up in the process (dlsym) A Linux binary links the system libm only for the functions Rust calls, so floor can be missing and the build fails; Windows names some functions otherwise (_j0). address gives the JIT the address of each function. One run per calibration evaluation The loss is noise, and Nelder-Mead stops anywhere. The mean as the default summary What to fit is a modelling choice; the mean of runs where half go extinct describes no run.

Guards: crates/commol-random/ (tests, with the stored first values of each sampler in tests/reference_values.txt), py-commol/src/engine.rs (a_stochastic_engine_repeats_a_run_from_its_seed, an_aggregate_stochastic_engine_repeats_a_run_from_its_seed, a_deterministic_engine_ignores_the_seed), crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs::a_run_depends_on_its_seed_and_not_on_where_it_reports, crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs (replicate_tests), tests/model_kinds/test_stochastic.py.

docs.title: Whole units in a stochastic engine
docs.text:
A stochastic engine moves whole units, so it starts from whole amounts. check_model (crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs, called by build and by every engine) rejects a bin whose amount (the sum of its compartments) is not whole, and initial amounts that are not whole unless the settings of the engine name a Rounding (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs); the message lists both. There is no default. A rounding makes the compartments of each bin whole and keeps the amount of the bin (round_bins), so a unit never moves to another bin, such as from a concentration to a count:

rounding Start of each run (Units::begin in crates/commol-stochastic/src/units.rs) "largest_remainder" The same whole amounts: in each bin, each amount rounded down, the units left over to the largest remainders, the first compartment first on a tie "random" A multinomial draw of the amount of each bin with the fractions of the model, from the generator of the run

The engine rounds at the start of a run, not when it is built, so a value that calibration writes (InitialConditionPlan) goes through the same rounding, and "random" draws after the values are written. With no rounding, a written value that is not whole is an error.

Alternative Why not Largest remainder by default With small amounts the rounding is a modelling choice: half a unit in each of ten groups starts five groups with one unit and five with none, which decides which groups can start a process at all. The library would choose it without notice. Random rounding by default The same objection, the other way. Reject every amount that is not whole Most stratified models would fail, with no way out but to compute whole amounts by hand. Round over every compartment at once It keeps only the sum of every bin: a unit left over in one bin can start in another bin, of another unit. Round each compartment on its own No bin keeps its amount, and "random" changes it from one run to the next. Round the amount of a bin that is not whole too It changes a declared amount without notice.

A per-step probability of StochasticSteps outside [0, 1], or proportional rates out of one compartment that sum to more than 1, are an error that names the compartment, the step and the flows (SimulationError::Infeasible), not a clamp: a binomial draw has no meaning outside [0, 1], and a clamp would change the model without notice.

Guards: crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs (amounts_that_are_not_whole_need_a_rounding, whole_amounts_need_no_rounding_and_each_bin_must_be_whole, the_largest_remainder_starts_every_run_from_the_same_whole_amounts, a_random_rounding_starts_on_average_from_the_amounts_of_the_model, calibrated_initial_conditions_go_through_the_rounding, a_negative_rate_or_probabilities_above_one_fail_at_their_step), crates/commol-stochastic/src/units.rs (each_bin_keeps_its_amount_when_rounded), builder.rs (a_bin_that_is_not_whole_is_a_build_error_of_a_stochastic_engine), tests/stochastic/test_whole_units.py.

docs.title: The solver is diffsol
docs.text:
The differential engine keeps no numerical method of its own: diffsol (pinned to a minor version, ~0.17.1) solves the system with tsit45 or bdf. bdf takes the Jacobian-vector product by finite differences (RightHandSide::jac_mul), one extra right-hand-side evaluation, because a symbolic derivative of every rate would be new numerical code. The matrix is dense (nalgebra) below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and sparse (faer) from there; diffsol finds the sparse pattern by passing NaN through J·v. Solver settings live in the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces a run.

Guards: crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs (bdf_solves_a_stiff_model_within_the_tolerance, a_large_stiff_model_uses_the_sparse_path).

docs.title: Initial conditions
docs.text:
Back to Design decisions

How the fractions of the categories compose, and how calibrated values reach the initial state. The initial state itself is an amount per bin (Model structure).

docs.title: Category fractions compose down the condition chain
docs.text:
The fractions of a conditional stratification are relative to the subgroup that its conditions select, not to the whole bin. The amount of a compartment therefore multiplies along the chain: bin amount × fraction(group1) × fraction(cat1) (initial_state in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs). Aggregate.subgroup_total sums the state the engine builds, overrides included, and Aggregate.get_conditioning_categories names the subgroup (context/aggregate.py).

Guard: tests/simulation/test_outputs.py::TestSubgroupTotal compares the result with the state the engine starts from.

docs.title: Calibrated initial conditions are applied in layers
docs.text: InitialConditionPlan in crates/commol-model/src/initial_conditions.rs applies calibrated values in a fixed order: bins, category splits, exact compartments, and then the remainder named by CalibrationProblem.initial_condition_remainder. A bin, prefix or compartment value is an amount in the unit of its bin; a category value is a split. Both engines of the aggregate kind resolve and write initial conditions through it (SimulationEngine::plan_values and apply_values), and the calibration writes every value through the engine (ValueWriter in crates/commol-calibration/src/values.rs), so the objective, the predictions and the write-back (configured_engine, then the binding calibrated_initial_state) agree by construction. Aggregate.with_calibrated_values (context/_model/calibration_write_back.py) writes back the amount of every bin whose every compartment a value or the remainder sets and the split of every calibrated category, and pins as per-compartment overrides every compartment that these cannot reproduce.

docs.title: The remainder keeps the sum the model declares
docs.text:
The remainder takes the sum of the amounts the model states (CompartmentalEngine::total, fixed when the engine is built), less every other compartment after the values are written. A compartment that no value covers keeps its declared amount and cancels out, so the remainder keeps the declared sum of the compartments the values and it cover, and a bin of another unit does not enter. A bin left None counts as 0, so the model states the sum on the remainder ({"A": 1000, "B": None}). Without a remainder every state is feasible, because the engine rejects a negative amount. With one, a remainder below zero is infeasible by its share of the amounts the values set, a number with no unit that is never a division by zero.

Units live only in Python (the Rust Bin has none), so Aggregate.check_calibration_values rejects a remainder whose unit is not the unit of every compartment a value sets, from the coverage the engine resolves (InitialConditionPlan::coverage, the binding initial_condition_coverage).

Alternative Why not A total in the problem that the remainder keeps It repeats a number of the model and can contradict it. The sum of the bins of the unit of the remainder The engine has no units, and the unit of a bin is optional free text. The deficit as a share of the sum the remainder keeps That sum can be 0, as when every bin starts empty.

Guards: tests/calibration/test_write_back.py::TestApplyCalibrationParameters::test_applied_model_reproduces_the_loss_the_optimizer_scored, tests/calibration/test_write_back.py::TestWriteBackReadability::test_an_amount_in_the_unit_of_its_bin_is_written_back, tests/calibration/test_initial_conditions.py::TestRemainderUnits; crates/commol-model/tests/initial_conditions.rs (the layers, the remainder and the targets of an id, and the_remainder_keeps_the_declared_sum_of_what_it_covers). See also Per-compartment initial conditions.

docs.title: Local approximations
docs.text:
Back to Design decisions

How the curvature, the Laplace approximation, the sandwich and the Laplace mixture read a fit, and where their scores, their Fisher information and PSIS live.

docs.title: The curvature lives on the unbounded scale
docs.text:
Curvature (crates/commol-inference/src/local/curvature.rs) holds H_u = D · H_θ · D, with D = dθ/du at the fit on the scale of Transform (transform.rs: a logit with two bounds, a log with one, the identity with none), centred on the fit mapped to that scale, with no curvature of the log Jacobian. Every draw maps back with from_unbounded, so it lies inside the bounds; every density on that scale, as the importance weights of the mixture, adds log_jacobian. A fit on a bound, within 1e-8 of the width of its bounds (on_bound), is refused with a message that names the parameter: its variance on that scale is infinite. The tolerance comes from the optimizer: Nelder-Mead searches on a sine (SineTransform) of the unbounded coordinate, which approaches a bound quadratically in u and ends about 1e-15 of the width from it; 1e-8 of the width is a step δu ≈ 2e-4, far below any posterior spread. The mixture skips such an end and notes it; when the end fits at least as well as the worst kept component (its objective is not above), the mixture misses an optimum the data support, and the sample is marked unreliable, since k̂ cannot see mass the proposal never reaches.

Alternative Why not The scale of the parameters A normal there puts mass outside the bounds near them. A truncated normal on the scale of the parameters It biases the mean and breaks the delta method. Centring on the mode of the density on the unbounded scale, Jacobian included It moves the centre away from the fit for no gain: importance sampling corrects the difference. A fit on a bound by exact equality An optimizer that the bound stops ends a few roundings from it, where the variance on the unbounded scale is huge but finite. Every skipped end marks the sample unreliable An end on a bound that fits worse than every component holds little mass; the note is enough.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::draws_mapped_back_stay_inside_the_bounds, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::an_end_on_a_bound_better_than_a_component_marks_the_sample_unreliable, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::an_end_on_a_bound_worse_than_every_component_is_only_noted, tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestCurvature::test_a_fit_on_a_bound_is_refused, tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestResults::test_an_end_on_a_bound_gives_no_component.

docs.title: Gauss–Newton by default, the Hessian on request
docs.text:
Curvature::gauss_newton reads the expected curvature of each observation's term over its arguments, the mean and the noise arguments of its model (Noise::information), through the Jacobian of SensitivitySource and the identity of each noise parameter: Jᵀ W J on the model parameters, with the cross terms where they do not vanish (a log-normal of a Mean center, the two arguments of a Student t). Curvature::hessian takes the central Hessian of the objective with given steps of the finitediff crate of the argmin fork, with steps δ^{1/4} · dθ/du (δ^{1/4} · max(|θ|, 1) with no bound), δ the output accuracy of the engine, so θ ± 2h stays inside the bounds. Each entry of either carries an estimated error; an entry above 1 % of √(H_jj H_kk) is a note. The threshold measures the error on the scale of a correlation, so an off-diagonal entry near 0 is judged against its row and column; a note changes no result.

Alternative Why not The Hessian always 4p² + 1 runs, and indefinite away from the optimum. Gauss–Newton always Wrong when the residuals are large or the mean is wrong, where the observed and expected curvature differ. The fixed step √(2ε) of finitediff With an ODE solved to rtol, an error of about accuracy / h². Differences written in commol The fork keeps the numerical methods; commol chooses the steps from its engine.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::curvatures_of_a_linear_model_equal_the_information, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::the_hessian_of_a_linear_model_equals_the_information, crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_likelihood.rs::fisher_information_of_each_model_has_its_closed_form.

docs.title: Scores and information live in commol-calibration
docs.text:
Discrepancy::term_derivatives (crates/commol-calibration/src/discrepancy.rs) gives each observation's gradient and expected curvature over its arguments: −2 w n² r and 2 w n² for the sum of squares, the same times c = 1 / (2 √(W · S)) for the root mean squared error (its derivative per unit of S), −w times Noise::scores and w times Noise::information for an observation model. The mean absolute error is refused: its sandwich needs a density of the residuals at 0 and a bandwidth. The sandwich, information matching and later gradient methods read them.

Alternative Why not Derivatives in each method Every method would repeat the models and their noise arguments. A kernel density for the absolute error It hides a bandwidth choice; the bootstrap needs none.

Guards: crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_likelihood.rs::scores_equal_the_differences_of_the_terms.

docs.title: The sandwich sums scores over blocks
docs.text:
sandwich (local/sandwich.rs) gives H⁻¹ B H⁻¹ with B = G/(G − 1) · Σ_b s_b s_bᵀ over the non-overlapping blocks of BlockScheme (CR1), and its draws and intervals read a Student t with G − 1 degrees of freedom. G ≤ p is refused, since the block scores of a fit sum to zero and B would have rank below p. block_length has no default; "auto" is the length of non-overlapping blocks of the residuals. Information matching (smc/gibbs.rs) reads the same H as J and the same B as I, so it takes a likelihood and holds under dependence.

Alternative Why not The independent sandwich (White) Too narrow when the residuals are autocorrelated. Newey–West It needs lags across series at irregular positions, and does not reuse the blocks. A warning below a fixed number of blocks An arbitrary threshold; the t widens the intervals by the right amount. CR2 with Bell–McCaffrey degrees of freedom Linear theory and the leverage of each block; kept for when a coverage study needs it.

Guards: tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestSandwich, tests/uncertainty/test_coverage.py::TestSandwich, tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestInformationMatching.

docs.title: The Laplace approximation needs observation models
docs.text:
laplace_approximation (local/approximation.rs) refuses a loss: a loss has no noise scale, so its curvature is no inverse variance. The message names NormalObservations(sd="sd") with a noise parameter, whose fit estimates the scale by maximum likelihood (SSE/n, narrower than SSE/(n − p) by √(n/(n − p))), and the sandwich, which needs no noise model. A result holds only data: Calibrator.delta_band(result, positions, level) reads the problem from the calibrator, so a result read back from JSON gives the same band.

Alternative Why not A variance scale SSE / (n − p) It assumes normal, independent noise of one size, which a loss does not state. LaplaceResult.delta_band with a private reference to the problem A result read back from JSON has none.

Guards: tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestLaplace::test_laplace_refuses_a_loss, tests/uncertainty/test_local.py::TestLaplace::test_a_result_read_from_json_gives_the_same_delta_band.

docs.title: PSIS lives in commol-inference
docs.text:
smooth (crates/commol-inference/src/psis.rs) follows Vehtari et al. (2024) as ArviZ does: the tail of ⌊3√S⌋ or ⌊S/5⌋ weights, the generalized Pareto fit of Zhang and Stephens (2009) with a prior on k, the quantiles at (r + ½)/M kept at most the largest weight. Its test compares k̂ and the smoothed weights with values computed once with ArviZ and stored in the test. importance_sample (importance.rs) takes any Proposal and any Target; the mixture is one proposal.

Alternative Why not ArviZ A large Python dependency for one function, and the weights would leave Rust and come back. The argmin fork PSIS is a statistical estimator, not optimization. A crate of its own Every reader is in commol-inference; no Rust crate implements it.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::psis_matches_the_reference_values, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::banana_target_gives_a_large_k_hat, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_local.rs::mixture_finds_both_modes_in_proportion.

docs.title: Model kinds
docs.text:
Back to Design decisions

How a model is composed, and what lets the generic layers run any model kind.

docs.title: One interface for every model kind
docs.text:
The layers that do not depend on how a model is built (Simulation, Calibrator, the uncertainty methods, the reports and SimulationPlotter) use only Model and the methods of ModelStructure (py-commol/commol/context/structure.py), and in Rust only the SimulationEngine trait (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs). What only an aggregate model has (compartments, initial amounts) is behind them: Aggregate (context/aggregate.py), and in Rust CompartmentalEngine and InitialConditionPlan (crates/commol-model/). A new kind, such as an agent network, is a new ModelStructure subclass with its engines in the list; nothing that exists changes.

Part Rule Why, against the alternative ModelStructure An abstract base class (Pydantic's metaclass derives from ABCMeta). A missing method fails when the object is made and names it; optional methods have a default. A typing.Protocol shows a missing method only under ty, or mid-run as an AttributeError, and gives no defaults. Engine kinds An engine names a method, not a kind: each entry of EngineType names the kinds it runs (EngineType::kinds). Model asks the list (check_kind) when it is made, and Engine::build asks it again and picks the implementation by the pair of the engine and the kind; the error names the engine, both kinds and the engines of the kind of the model (EngineType::engines_of). Without the check, a model of one kind reaches the engine of another and fails deep in its compilation. One engine per kind would multiply the names: a stochastic engine runs every structure that implements it. Values calibration sets parameter and factor are generic. Each kind declares the types of value of its own it accepts (ModelKind::value_types, which ModelStructure.calibration_value_types asks); the aggregate kind accepts initial_condition. The engine resolves and writes them (SimulationEngine::plan_values, apply_values). The calibration crate would know compartments, and a new kind could not calibrate values of its own without editing it. Report sections ModelStructure.report_sections adds the sections of a kind to applied_parameters_report (default: none); the aggregate kind adds initial_conditions. A check of the kind in reporting.py brings back a branch per kind.
