docs.title: Running Simulations
docs.text:
Back to Home

Simulation runs a built Model in the Rust engine and returns its outputs: one series per compartment and per accumulator, with the positions on the axis they were read at. This page covers running a model, reading and aggregating its outputs, running it in continuous time as differential equations, and plotting them.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total", accumulators=["cum_ab"]
    )
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 900, "B": 100, "C": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

print(simulation.simulation_outputs)  # ['A', 'B', 'C', 'cum_ab']
print(f"C at step 100: {results['C'][-1]:.0f}")

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
Member Returns What it does Simulation(model) — Builds the engine for the model. A model with uncalibrated parameters can be built, but not run. run(num_steps, *, seed=None) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state, with the model as it is now, and reports at the positions 0, 1, …, num_steps. Raises ValueError if a parameter is still None, InfeasibleStateError if a difference step leaves an amount below zero (Amounts below zero), and RuntimeError that names the flow and the position if a rate is not a number. run_at(at, *, seed=None) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state and reports at the given sorted positions only. The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferentialEquations model any non-negative position, such as 0.5; a DifferenceEquations model only integer steps. Otherwise ValueError, with the engine's message. See Differential equations. replicates(n, *, seed=None) ReplicateRuns For a stochastic engine: an object whose run and run_at return SimulationReplicates, n runs with one seed each. See Randomness, seeds and replicates. is_stochastic bool Whether the engine draws random numbers. simulation_outputs list[str] The output names, in engine order: compartments first, then accumulators. outputs_for(id) list[str] The outputs of one bin or accumulator. group_outputs(ids) dict[str, list[str]] The outputs of several bins or accumulators, keyed by id. total_series(results, ids) list[float] The sum of all outputs of the given ids, at each position of the results. windowed_totals(results, ids, window, at=None) list[float] What the given accumulators gained in each window. engine engine The underlying Rust engine, for the model as it is now: the engine model.engine.type names (engine.engine_type). engine.step() advances it one step; engine.reset() returns it to the initial state.

Every run starts again from the initial state, so two calls with the same model give the same result (Simulation.run resets the engine first). To continue a run step by step, use the engine:

first = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
again = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(again["A"] == first["A"])  # True: it started again

simulation.engine.step()  # step 11, from where the last run stopped
print(simulation.engine.state[0] < first["A"][-1])  # True: A keeps falling

The engine follows the model. When the model changed after the Simulation was created, for example with update_parameters or apply_calibration_parameters, run and engine rebuild the engine from the model as it is now (Simulation._sync_engine compares model_dump_json() with the JSON the engine was built from):

model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.0})
frozen = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(frozen["A"][10] == frozen["A"][0])  # True: k1 = 0 stops A → B
model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.3})

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
run and run_at return SimulationResults (py-commol/commol/api/results.py): a dict from output name to one value per position, so results["A"], json.dumps(results) and pandas.DataFrame(results) work as for any mapping. The positions the values were read at are in results.positions.

Member Shape Use for results[name] [value at positions[0], …] Reading one output, plotting results.positions [0.0, 1.0, …, n] for run(n); the requested positions for run_at Reading a value at a position, windows, reports results.rows() [[every output at positions[0]], …], in simulation_outputs order Matrix operations, export

run(num_steps) holds num_steps + 1 positions: position 0 is the initial state.

rows = results.rows()

print(results.positions[:3])  # [0.0, 1.0, 2.0]
print(len(rows))              # 101
print(len(rows[0]))           # 4: A, B, C and cum_ab
print([round(value) for value in rows[0]])  # [900, 100, 0, 0]

docs.title: Randomness, seeds and replicates
docs.text:
A stochastic engine draws random numbers, so its runs depend on a seed; a deterministic engine, such as DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations, gives the same run for every seed (EngineType.is_stochastic in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs).

Call Deterministic engine Stochastic engine run(n, seed=s), run_at(at, seed=s) Ignores the seed; results.seed is None One run from seed s; results.seed is s run(n) without a seed results.seed is None Draws a seed from the operating system and keeps it in results.seed, so the run can be repeated replicates(n, seed=s).run(…) Raises ValueError that names the engine: every replicate would be equal n runs, in parallel in the engine, each with its own seed 
print(simulation.is_stochastic)                # False: a difference engine
print(simulation.run(num_steps=5, seed=1).seed)  # None: the run depends on no seed
try:
    simulation.replicates(10)
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)  # The DifferenceEquations engine is deterministic: ...

Replicate i takes the seed derived from seed and i, the SplitMix64 of seed + i (replicate_seed in crates/commol-random/src/generator.rs), so a replicate gives the same run however many replicates run, and simulation.run(…, seed=replicates[i].seed) repeats it. SimulationReplicates (py-commol/commol/api/results.py) is a list of SimulationResults:

Member Returns replicates[i], len(replicates) One run, with its seed; the number of runs seed, seeds, positions The seed the replicate seeds derive from, the seed of each replicate, the positions mean() SimulationResults of the mean of every output at each position quantiles(levels) {level: SimulationResults}, at each position, by the one quantile (NumPy's method="hazen") member_statistics(output, confidence_level) mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max of one output at each position, reduced replicate by replicate with the one quantile 
from commol.api.plotter import SimulationPlotter

stochastic = Simulation(
    ModelBuilder(name="Stochastic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0}), engine="StochasticEvents")
)
replicates = stochastic.replicates(200, seed=42).run(num_steps=50)
mean = replicates.mean()
band = replicates.member_statistics("B", confidence_level=0.9)
SimulationPlotter(stochastic, replicates).plot_series()  # the mean and a 95 % band
print(replicates.seeds[:2] == [run.seed for run in replicates[:2]])  # True

The stochastic engines and what they draw are in Stochastic Simulation.

A run is reproducible from its model and its seed, on one platform and one commol version:

Where The same seed gives The same machine and commol version The same run Another platform, the same commol version The same random numbers (Xoshiro256PlusPlus and samplers written in commol, crates/commol-random/), but the rate functions (exp, sin, log, …) come from the system's math library, which can differ in the last bit between operating systems; a run there is equal in distribution and rarely differs draw by draw Another commol version A run that may change; the changelog says so

docs.title: Accumulators
docs.text:
An accumulator output starts at 0 and only grows: it is the total that its transitions have moved since step 0. Here cum_ab is everything that has moved from A to B, so A plus cum_ab stays at the initial A:

print(round(results["A"][-1] + results["cum_ab"][-1]))  # 900

docs.title: Stratified outputs
docs.text:
With stratifications, every bin and accumulator has one output per combination of categories, named {id}_{category}_{category}… in the order the stratifications were declared.

stratified = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stratified")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(id="type", categories=["t1", "t2"])
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k", accumulators=["cum_ab"])
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5},
                "type": {"t1": 0.5, "t2": 0.5},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

stratified_simulation = Simulation(stratified)
stratified_results = stratified_simulation.run(num_steps=50)

print(stratified_simulation.outputs_for("B"))
# ['B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2', 'B_g2_t1', 'B_g2_t2']
print(stratified_simulation.group_outputs(["A", "cum_ab"])["cum_ab"])
# ['cum_ab_g1_t1', 'cum_ab_g1_t2', 'cum_ab_g2_t1', 'cum_ab_g2_t2']

docs.title: Totals by bin
docs.text:
total_series sums every output of the ids you give, at each position:

total_b = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["B"])
total_ab = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["A", "B"])
print(round(total_ab[-1]))  # 1000: A and B hold the whole total

Do not select outputs by name prefix

[k for k in results if k.startswith("B_")] also matches an accumulator named B_events, and, with conditional stratifications, outputs may have fewer suffixes than their siblings. outputs_for, group_outputs and total_series use the model structure, so neither case can go wrong.

docs.title: Totals by category
docs.text:
To select compartments by category, use their labels from model.structure.initial_state(model.process): each entry has name, bin and categories.

in_g1 = [
    compartment.name
    for compartment in stratified.structure.initial_state(stratified.process)
    if compartment.categories.get("group") == "g1"
]
print(in_g1)  # ['A_g1_t1', 'A_g1_t2', 'B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2']

total_g1 = [
    sum(stratified_results[name][step] for name in in_g1)
    for step in range(len(stratified_results[in_g1[0]]))
]
print(round(total_g1[-1]))  # 500: g1 started with half of every bin

docs.title: Windowed totals
docs.text:
windowed_totals turns a cumulative output into the amount it gained in each window of length window on the axis. Window w covers (w · window, (w + 1) · window], and each value is the output at the end of the window minus the output at its start. Both must be positions of the results.

per_week = stratified_simulation.windowed_totals(
    stratified_results, ["cum_ab"], window=7
)
print(len(per_week))  # 7: the complete windows of a 50-step run
Argument Meaning ids Accumulator ids; their outputs are summed first. window The window length on the axis. Must be positive. at The positions where windows close. By default, every complete window of the results (window_ends). Pass observation positions to get the values a calibration compares against.

The window grid and the same reduction work on any series with the module-level functions of py-commol/commol/api/windows.py:

Function Returns window_start(i, window), window_end(i, window) The positions that bound window i: i · window and (i + 1) · window window_index(at, window) The window that holds a position, max(ceil(at / window) − 1, 0); the inverse of window_end. Reports place observations with it. window_ends(window, end) Every complete window end up to end windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at=None) The gain of a series over each window 
from commol import window_end, window_ends, window_index, windowed_totals

print(window_ends(window=7, end=30))                       # [7, 14, 21, 28]
print(window_end(0, 7), window_index(7, 7), window_index(7.5, 7))  # 7 0 1
print(windowed_totals([0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28], range(8), 3))  # [6, 15]

A window need not be a whole number of steps: see Reporting at any position.

docs.title: Differential equations
docs.text:
A model built with engine="DifferentialEquations" runs in continuous time. The engine (crates/commol-differential/) integrates dX/dt = Σ flows(t, X) with the ODE solver diffsol. The flows are the same as in a difference model: the same transitions, rates, accumulators, outputs, calibration, reports and plots. Only the way the engine advances changes.

import math

from commol import OdeSolver

ode_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Decay")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1", accumulators=["moved"])
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferentialEquations",
        settings=OdeSolver(method="tsit45", rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8),
    )
)

ode = Simulation(ode_model)
at = ode.run_at([0, 0.5, 2.25])
print(round(at["A"][2], 3), round(1000 * math.exp(-0.1 * 2.25), 3))  # 798.516 798.516
print(round(ode.run(num_steps=10)["moved"][10], 1))  # 632.1: the integral of the flow

docs.title: Solver settings
docs.text:
OdeSolver holds the settings of the DifferentialEquations engine. They are part of the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces its runs. Pass them where you choose the engine, build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...), so one builder can build the model for each engine with its own settings; without them the defaults apply. The DifferenceEquations engine takes no settings: the engine rejects settings of another engine with an error that names both (ValidationError).

Field Default Meaning method "tsit45" "tsit45": explicit Runge–Kutta 5(4), for non-stiff models. "bdf": backward differentiation formulas, for stiff models (rates of very different speeds). rtol 1e-6 Relative tolerance of each state component. atol 1e-6 Absolute tolerance of each state component, in the unit of the bins.

bdf builds its Jacobian from a finite-difference Jacobian-vector product. It uses a dense matrix below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and a sparse one from there (crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs).

docs.title: Time inside a step
docs.text:
On [n, n + 1) a rate sees step = n and the position t, which moves continuously. A rate that reads step, a "pulse" series or a pulse pattern (AxisPattern.pulse, pulses, periodic) is constant on its unit interval, and the engine restarts the integration at each integer where such a rate can jump. A proportional pulse p on step n acts as the constant rate p for one unit: it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source, not p as in a difference model. To move a fraction at once, use an impulse.

A "step_function" or "linear" series and the patterns AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp read t, so they change at any position, and the engine restarts the integration at their points and bounds. In a difference model t equals step, so they give the same results as a rate that reads step.

A rate can also jump where t reaches a value that it compares t with, such as if(t >= t_on, k1, 0). The engine restarts the integration there too, so the solver cannot step over a short window. This works when the value reads only numbers, pi, e and parameters with a constant or calibrated value, and t is one side of the comparison: write t >= 10, not t - 10 >= 0. A jump that depends on the state, such as if(t >= A, ...), is not found.

A rate of a differential model is continuous, not a fraction per step; see What a rate means. Model.axis_units() gives the rate that the engine of a model reads from a mean span or a probability over a period; see Units of the axis.

from commol import AxisPattern

pulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Pulse")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate=AxisPattern.pulse(at=2, value=0.2))
)
all_in_a = Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0})
ode_pulse = Simulation(
    pulse_model.build(all_in_a, engine="DifferentialEquations")
).run(num_steps=3)
print(round(ode_pulse["A"][2] - ode_pulse["A"][3], 1))  # 181.3 = 1000 (1 − e^−0.2)

docs.title: Reporting at any position
docs.text:
run_at(at) reports at sorted positions on the axis, from the dense output of the solver. Observations (ObservedDataPoint.at), windows (ObservedDataPoint.window) and constraint positions (CalibrationConstraint.at) may lie between integers for a differential model: the calibration reads the engine at those positions (Observations). A difference model reports only at integer steps; the engine rejects any other position and names the object that holds it.

Windows, reports and plots read a value at a position of the results, so a window of 2.5 works once the results hold its ends:

ends = window_ends(window=2.5, end=10)    # [2.5, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0]
ode_windows = ode.run_at([0.0, *ends])
gained = ode.windowed_totals(ode_windows, ["moved"], window=2.5)
print([round(value, 1) for value in gained])  # [221.2, 172.3, 134.2, 104.5]

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text:
SimulationPlotter(simulation, results) draws one subplot per output with seaborn, and returns the matplotlib Figure. With the SimulationReplicates of a stochastic engine, plot_series draws their mean and a band of confidence_level (default 0.95), each replicate reduced to the plotted series first:

from commol import PlotConfig, SimulationPlotter

plotter = SimulationPlotter(simulation, results)  # the results of the first run
plotter.plot_series(output_file="series.png")
plotter.plot_cumulative(output_file="cumulative.png")

plotter.plot_series(
    output_file="custom.png",
    config=PlotConfig(figsize=(16, 10), dpi=150, style="whitegrid", palette="Set2", context="talk"),
    series=["B", "C"],
    x_label="Week",
    tick_every=10,
    position_label=lambda at: f"w{int(at) // 7}",
    linewidth=2.5,
    alpha=0.8,
)
Argument Default Meaning output_file None Where to save the figure. None only returns it. series None (every output) What to plot, one subplot each: an output name (B_g1) or a bin or accumulator id (B), which plots the sum of its outputs (Simulation.outputs_for). An exact output name wins. An unknown entry raises ValueError. observed_data None ObservedDataPoints to draw on the subplot of their label, at their positions (a differential model may observe between integers). An observation with a window draws the windowed line, which reads the results at every window end and start (ValueError when the results do not hold one). calibration_result None A CalibrationResult gives the factor values that scale the model. A Predictive draws the weighted median of its draws and their band of confidence_level, each draw read through the observation operator (sums, windows, factors). prediction_intervals None plot_series only. The PredictionIntervals of a conformal method: the subplot of each of their series, by label, shows the band from lower to upper and the point prediction, dashed. An unbounded interval is left out of the band. config PlotConfig() Figure size, dpi, layout and seaborn style. show_legend True plot_series only. x_label, tick_every, position_label "Step", every plotted position, the position plot_series only. Label the x axis, for example in weeks. The x axis shows results.positions. other keyword arguments — Passed to seaborn.lineplot, such as linewidth or alpha. PlotConfig field Default Values figsize (12, 8) Inches (width, height) dpi 100 Resolution layout None (automatic) (rows, columns) style None "darkgrid", "whitegrid", "dark", "white", "ticks" palette None A seaborn palette or matplotlib colormap, such as "Set2" context None "paper", "notebook", "talk", "poster"

To compare with observations:

from commol import ObservedDataPoint

observed = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=10, output="B", value=45.2),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=20, output="B", value=78.5),
]
plotter.plot_series(output_file="with_data.png", observed_data=observed)

docs.title: Stochastic Simulation
docs.text:
Back to Home

A stochastic engine runs the process of a model as whole units that move at random, with no change to the process: the rates of the model become the probabilities or the hazards of its events. Use it when the variability between runs, an extinction or the behaviour of small amounts matters. This page covers the two stochastic engines of an aggregate model, how a rate becomes an event, whole units, the methods and their cost, and calibration with replicates.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

builder = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stochastic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
)
structure = Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 999, "B": 1, "C": 0})

model = builder.build(structure, engine="StochasticEvents")
simulation = Simulation(model)

one_run = simulation.run(num_steps=100, seed=1)
print(one_run["C"][-1] == int(one_run["C"][-1]))  # True: whole units

replicates = simulation.replicates(100, seed=2).run(num_steps=100)
print(len(replicates))  # 100 runs, one seed each
died_out = sum(run["C"][-1] < 10 for run in replicates)
print(died_out)  # about a third of the runs: the one unit of B leaves before it spreads

The same builder and structure build the deterministic model with engine="DifferentialEquations": only the engine changes.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: You need Engine The mean behaviour of a large amount DifferentialEquations or DifferenceEquations How much runs vary, and the spread of an output StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps The chance that an amount reaches zero and stays there (extinction) StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps Small amounts, where a unit more or less changes the outcome StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps

docs.title: The two engines
docs.text:
Engine Time Method Rate meaning Positions Crate StochasticEvents Continuous Gillespie's direct method (the stochastic simulation algorithm, SSA), or tau-leaping continuous: a hazard per unit of the axis Any finite, non-negative position commol-stochastic StochasticSteps Discrete steps The chain binomial per_step: a probability per step Integer steps commol-stochastic

Their mean-field limits are the deterministic engines: the expected change of the state of StochasticEvents is the right-hand side of DifferentialEquations, and the expected step of StochasticSteps is the step of DifferenceEquations while no cap acts (see below). A rate keeps its meaning: a per_step rate of a difference model is the probability of the chain binomial, and a continuous rate of a differential model is the hazard of the events (What a rate means).

docs.title: How a rate becomes an event
docs.text:
Each flow of the model is one kind of event. An event moves one unit: it takes one from each source of the flow, and adds one to each target and to each accumulator that counts the flow (CompiledModel::flow_changes in crates/commol-model/src/system.rs).

Rate StochasticEvents (propensity) StochasticSteps (draw of a step) Proportional, k Each unit of the source leaves at hazard k: propensity k × source Each unit leaves with probability k: Binomial(source, k) Absolute, r Events at rate r Poisson(r), capped by what the sources still hold No source (inflow), r Events at rate r Poisson(r)
  • StochasticEvents: a flow has no events while a source holds fewer units than an event takes. A negative propensity is an error that names the flow.
  • StochasticSteps: every draw reads the state at the start of the step. The units of one compartment leave by its proportional flows in one multinomial draw (each flow with its probability, staying with 1 − Σ k), so a unit never leaves twice and an amount never goes below zero. The absolute flows then draw in the order of the model, each capped by what its sources still hold. A negative rate, a proportional rate above 1, or proportional rates out of one compartment that sum to more than 1 raise InfeasibleStateError, which names the compartment, the step and the flows (StochasticSteps::step in crates/commol-stochastic/src/steps.rs).
from commol import InfeasibleStateError

too_likely = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Too likely")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.7)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.5)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1")
    .add_transition(id="t_ac", source=["A"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(structure, engine="StochasticSteps")
)
try:
    Simulation(too_likely).run(num_steps=5, seed=1)
except InfeasibleStateError as error:
    print(error)  # At step 0, the proportional rates out of compartment 'A': flows 't_ab' 0.7, 't_ac' 0.5 sum to 1.2, above 1. ...

Model.describe() shows the events in its dynamics section: one row per flow with its change of the state and its propensity or its draw (Describing a Model):

print(model.describe().render("markdown").split("### Events")[1].split("\n\n")[1])
# | Transition | Change | Propensity |
# |---|---|---|
# | t_ab | A -1, B +1 | k1 * A * B / total |
# | t_bc | B -1, C +1 | k2 * B |

docs.title: Whole units
docs.text:
A stochastic engine moves whole units, so it starts from whole amounts (check_model in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs):

Initial amounts What happens The amount of a bin is not a whole number build raises ValueError and names the engine and the bin Every amount is whole Nothing more is needed An amount is not whole build raises ValueError, unless the settings of the engine name a rounding; the message lists both

There is no default rounding: with small amounts the rounding decides which compartments start with a unit, so it is a modelling choice. Half a unit in each of ten groups starts five groups with one unit and five with none.

rounding Start of each run "largest_remainder" The same whole amounts in every run: in each bin, each amount rounded down, and the units left over to the largest remainders, so they sum to the amount of the bin "random" A multinomial draw of the amount of each bin with the fractions of the model, in each run, so the mean start equals the amounts of the model

Both round each bin on its own, so a unit never moves to another bin, such as from a bin of a concentration to a bin of a count.

from commol import StochasticEventsSettings

groups = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Groups")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=[f"g{i}" for i in range(10)])
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * B / total")
)
seeded = Aggregate(
    bin_amounts={"A": 995, "B": 5},
    stratification_fractions={"group": {f"g{i}": 0.1 for i in range(10)}},
)
try:
    groups.build(seeded, engine="StochasticEvents")
except ValueError as error:
    print("largest_remainder" in str(error), "random" in str(error))  # True True

grouped = groups.build(
    seeded,
    engine="StochasticEvents",
    settings=StochasticEventsSettings(rounding="random"),
)
start = Simulation(grouped).run_at([0.0], seed=3)
print(sum(start[f"B_g{i}"][0] for i in range(10)) + sum(start[f"A_g{i}"][0] for i in range(10)))
# 1000.0

Initial conditions that calibration sets go through the same rounding. With no rounding, a calibrated value that is not whole is an error that lists the two options.

docs.title: Seeds and replicates
docs.text:
A run is reproducible from its model and its seed: simulation.run(…, seed=s) gives one run, and simulation.replicates(n, seed=s).run(…) gives n runs with one seed each, in parallel. A run does not depend on the positions it reports at: the output at a position is the state after the last event before it. See Randomness, seeds and replicates for the seeds, SimulationReplicates and its statistics, plots of the mean and a band, and reports.

again = simulation.run(num_steps=100, seed=1)
print(again == one_run)  # True
print(replicates.member_statistics("C", confidence_level=0.9)["ci_lower"][-1] >= 0)  # True

docs.title: Methods and their cost
docs.text:
StochasticEvents takes StochasticEventsSettings, and StochasticSteps takes StochasticStepsSettings (only rounding):

Setting Default Meaning method "direct" "direct": one event at a time, exact. "tau_leaping": a Poisson number of events of each flow in a leap, an approximation tau None The length of a leap of "tau_leaping"; None chooses each leap as Cao, Gillespie and Petzold (2006) do epsilon 0.03 How much a propensity may change in a chosen leap, relative to its value tolerance 1e-8 Relative tolerance of the time of an event when a rate reads t rounding None See Whole units
  • Cost of the direct method. The number of events grows with the total and with the rates: every unit that moves is one event. For a large total, use "tau_leaping" or a deterministic engine.
  • Tau-leaping. A chosen leap is as long as the propensities allow while they change by less than epsilon; a leap that would hold fewer than ten events is one exact event instead, and a leap that leaves an amount below zero is halved and drawn again. A fixed tau is first-order accurate: a smaller tau is closer to the direct method.
  • Rates that read t. Between events the state is fixed, but a rate that reads t, such as k * (1 + sin(t)), still changes. The direct method then integrates the total propensity from the last event until it reaches an exponential draw (a time change, Anderson 2007), within tolerance. A model whose rates do not read t pays nothing for it.
  • Breakpoints. The engine stops at every position where a rate can jump (the impulses, the values a rate compares t with, the points of a series read at t, and every integer when a rate reads step), so no wait and no leap crosses one (CompiledModel::breakpoints).
  • Impulses. At its positions, before the events there, a proportional impulse moves a binomial draw of its source (its rate is the probability that one unit moves, between 0 and 1); an absolute impulse moves its rate, a whole number of units. Each moves at most what its sources still hold.
leaping = builder.build(
    structure,
    engine="StochasticEvents",
    settings=StochasticEventsSettings(method="tau_leaping"),
)
leaped = Simulation(leaping).replicates(100, seed=2).run(num_steps=100)
print(abs(leaped.mean()["C"][-1] - replicates.mean()["C"][-1]) < 150)  # True

docs.title: Calibration with replicates
docs.text:
A calibration of a stochastic model runs replicates runs per evaluation with common random numbers, and compares the observations with the summary of the replicates you choose: "mean", "median", Quantile(q) or "crps" (Stochastic engines).

from commol import (
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
)

mean = replicates.mean()
observed = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=at, output="C", value=mean["C"][at]) for at in (40, 70, 100)
]
unknown = builder.build(structure, engine="StochasticEvents")
unknown.update_parameters({"k2": None})
problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=observed,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k2", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.01, max_bound=0.5)
    ],
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=100),
    replicates=50,
    replicate_summary="mean",
    seed=7,
)
result = Calibrator(Simulation(unknown), problem).run()
print(0.05 < result.best_parameters["k2"] < 0.2)  # True: near 0.1

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The engine is StochasticEvents (continuous time) or StochasticSteps (per-step probabilities), as the rates of the model mean.
  • [ ] The amount of each bin is whole, and the settings name a rounding when the amount of a compartment is not.
  • [ ] Every run has a seed, or keeps the one commol drew (results.seed).
  • [ ] A large total uses "tau_leaping" or a deterministic engine.
  • [ ] A calibration sets replicates, replicate_summary and seed.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

A transition moves an amount at every step: from its source compartments to its target compartments, at the rate you give. This page documents ModelBuilder.add_transition completely: rates, several sources, transitions between categories, stratified rates, impulses, amounts below zero, and what build checks.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Transitions")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 900, "B": 100, "C": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

print(model.describe().render("text"))  # every flow, as the engine computes it

docs.title: add_transition
docs.text: Argument Type Default Meaning id str required The identifier. source list[str] required Bins (or one category) that lose the flow. [] means the flow enters the system. target list[str] required Bins (or one category) that gain the flow. [] means the flow leaves the system. rate str, float, AxisPattern or None None The rate formula; see Rates. With stratified_rates, the fallback rate. None with no stratified rate gives a transition with no flows. stratified_rates list[dict] \| None None Rates for some categories; see Stratified rates. per_compartment bool \| None None Replaces bin names in the rate with each flow's own compartment; see per_compartment. accumulators list[str] \| None None Accumulators that count the flow; see Building Models. impulse_at list[float] \| None None Makes the transition an impulse at these steps; see Impulses. impulse_every tuple[float, float] \| None None (period, offset): an impulse at offset, offset + period, …; see Impulses.

docs.title: Rates
docs.text: A rate is a formula (a string), a number, or a AxisPattern. A formula can use parameters, compartments, bin totals, total, step, constants and functions; see Mathematical Expressions.

docs.title: Absolute and proportional rates
docs.text:
The engine decides for each flow whether its rate is the flow itself or a rate per member of the source:

Case Kind Flow The rate names a compartment, a bin total, total or a total_… variable Absolute rate The transition has no source Absolute rate A stratified rate sets "absolute": True or False As set — Otherwise Proportional rate × source Rate Kind Flow from B to C "k2" Proportional k2 * B "k2 * B" Absolute k2 * B "k1 * A * B / total" Absolute k1 * A * B / total "0.5" with source=[] Absolute 0.5 enters the target

The description of the model shows every flow after this decision, so a proportional rate appears multiplied by its source.

docs.title: Rates that change along the axis
docs.text:
A formula may use step (or t), the current step:

periodic = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Periodic")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365)) * A * B / total",
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 990, "B": 10},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

For pulses, windows, ramps and schedules per group, use Axis Patterns.

docs.title: Several sources or targets
docs.text:
A transition with several sources or targets moves one flow: every entry in source loses it and every entry in target gains it. A bin listed twice loses or gains it twice. The rate must be absolute.

merge = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Merge")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.001)
    .add_transition(id="t1", source=["A", "B"], target=["C", "C"], rate="k * A * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 500, "B": 500, "C": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(merge.describe().render("text"))
# A loses k * A * B, B loses k * A * B, C gains 2 * (k * A * B)

docs.title: The $compartment placeholder
docs.text:
For independent flows with one formula, write $compartment in the rate. The builder creates one transition per source (or per target), named {id}__{compartment}, with $compartment replaced by that compartment:

outflow = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Outflow")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="mu", value=0.01)
    .add_transition(
        id="outflow",
        source=["A", "B", "C"],
        target=[],
        rate="mu * $compartment * (1 + 0.1 * $compartment / total)",
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 400, "B": 300, "C": 300},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

for transition in outflow.process.transitions:
    print(transition.id, transition.rate)
# outflow__A mu * A * (1 + 0.1 * A / total)
# outflow__B mu * B * (1 + 0.1 * B / total)
# outflow__C mu * C * (1 + 0.1 * C / total)
Rule Otherwise Several sources with one or no target, or several targets with one or no source ValueError: the mapping would be ambiguous At least two sources or two targets ValueError: write the compartment name instead A rate is given ValueError

stratified_rates may also use $compartment; each generated transition gets its own copy.

docs.title: Transitions between categories
docs.text:
When source and target are categories of one stratification, the transition moves amounts between them in every bin:

moving = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Moving")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="move", source=["g1"], target=["g2"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 500, "B": 500},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(moving.describe().render("text"))
# move (g1 -> g2):  A_g1 -> A_g2: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2: k * B_g1

A category transition needs exactly one source and one target category. If the target category is split by a conditional stratification, every flow must say which of its categories it enters, with a to condition (see Redirecting the target with to); otherwise build raises.

docs.title: per_compartment
docs.text:
With stratifications, a bin id in a rate means the total of the bin. In a flow from A_g1, "k * A" uses A_g1 + A_g2. per_compartment=True replaces each source and target bin id with the flow's own compartment:

Flow rate="k * A" with per_compartment=True A_g1 -> B_g1 k * A (the total) k * A_g1 A_g2 -> B_g2 k * A (the total) k * A_g2 
own_compartment = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Per compartment")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k * A", per_compartment=True)
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 500, "B": 500},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(own_compartment.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k * A_g1   and   A_g2 -> B_g2: k * A_g2

It applies to the fallback rate and to every stratified rate, and only to transitions between bins.

docs.title: Stratified rates
docs.text:
stratified_rates gives some categories their own rate. Each entry has conditions and a rate, and may set absolute:

group_rates = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Group rates")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2", "g3"])
    .add_parameter(id="k_g1", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="k_g2", value=0.10)
    .add_parameter(id="k_default", value=0.05)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k_default",
        stratified_rates=[
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}], "rate": "k_g1"},
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}], "rate": "k_g2"},
        ],
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 900, "B": 0},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.3, "g2": 0.3, "g3": 0.4}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(group_rates.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k_g1 * A_g1,  A_g2 -> B_g2: k_g2 * A_g2,  A_g3 -> B_g3: k_default * A_g3
Entry key Type Meaning conditions list[dict] All must match the source compartment (AND). rate str or float The rate for matching compartments. absolute bool, optional Forces the rate to be absolute or proportional. Condition key Meaning stratification The stratification id. category Optional. The category the source must have. to Optional. The category the target gets instead; see below.

Which rate applies: for each source compartment, the entry that matches with the most conditions wins; on a tie, the first one in the list. With no match, the fallback rate applies. With three stratifications and one entry for g2, t1, v2:

Source compartment Conditions matched Rate A_g2_t1_v2 3 of 3 The entry A_g2_t1_v1 not all Fallback A_g1_t1_v1 not all Fallback

docs.title: Redirecting the target with to
docs.text:
A condition with category filters the source. A condition with to changes the target category. A condition with only to filters nothing, so it can send the flow into a stratification that the source does not have:

redirect = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Redirect")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(
        id="subtype",
        categories=["s1", "s2"],
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}],
    )
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="move",
        source=["g1"],
        target=["g2"],
        stratified_rates=[{"conditions": [{"stratification": "subtype", "to": "s1"}], "rate": "k"}],
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 500, "B": 500},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5},
                "subtype": {"s1": 0.5, "s2": 0.5},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(redirect.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> A_g2_s1: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2_s1: k * B_g1

A transition without a source starts from the compartments it enters, so its category conditions choose them and build rejects a to.

docs.title: Limiting when a transition runs
docs.text: A transition runs at every step. To limit a flow, write the condition in the rate with if, as in "if(step > 30, k, 0)", or use a AxisPattern, a series parameter or a stratified rate. A comparison alone is a boolean, so "k * (step > 30)" is rejected.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text:
An impulse moves its amount at once, at given steps, and nothing between them. Give the steps with impulse_at=[…] or impulse_every=(period, offset). The rate is then a fraction of the source (proportional) or an amount (absolute), with the same rules, sources, targets, stratified rates and accumulators as any transition.

impulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Impulses")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved by the impulse")
    .add_parameter(id="p", value=0.25)
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="jump", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="p", impulse_at=[1], accumulators=["moved"])
    .add_transition(id="flow", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

jumped = Simulation(impulse_model).run(num_steps=2)
print([round(a, 1) for a in jumped["A"]])  # [1000.0, 675.0, 607.5]
print(jumped["moved"][2])  # 225.0: a quarter of the 900 left at step 1
Rule In both engines Order At step n the state jumps first; then the flows of the step run from the new state. The output at n shows the state after the jump (CompiledModel::apply_impulses in crates/commol-model/src/system.rs). Several impulses at one step Every jump is computed from the state before any of them. Steps A DifferentialEquations model takes any steps, such as 0.5: the engine stops there, applies the jump and restarts. A DifferenceEquations model needs integer steps (ValidationError names the transition). Units The rate of an impulse is an amount, <bin unit>, not a flow per step (Units). describe() Lists impulses apart from the equations, with their steps (Describing a Model).

An impulse is not a pulse rate. A AxisPattern.pulse is a rate: a difference model applies it for one step with the other flows, and a differential model applies it as a constant rate for one unit of the axis, so it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source. An impulse moves exactly p of its source in both engines.

docs.title: Amounts below zero
docs.text:
A DifferenceEquations step never leaves a compartment below zero. After the impulses of a step and after its flows, the engine checks every compartment. An amount below −10⁻¹² × total (the total at the start of the step) stops the run with InfeasibleStateError, a ValueError. The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows out of it, largest first. The tolerance lets a flow that empties a compartment exactly pass. Accumulators are not checked: a net flow may count negative (DifferenceEquations::step in crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs).

from commol import InfeasibleStateError

too_fast = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Too fast")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=1.5)
    .add_transition(id="t", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

try:
    Simulation(too_fast).run(num_steps=3)
except InfeasibleStateError as error:
    print(error)  # The flows of step 0 leave compartment 'A' at -500, ...

A step moves what the flows give, so the usual causes are in the rates:

Cause Example Fix Proportional rates that sum above 1 rate="k" with k = 1.5 moves 1.5 times its source in one step A smaller rate per step, or a shorter step An absolute rate on a bin total With stratifications, "k1 * A * B / total" moves from each compartment of A an amount computed from the total of A per_compartment=True, so each compartment loses an amount from its own amount (per_compartment) A rate that turns negative "k * B * (1 - C / capacity)" once C > capacity: the flow runs backwards and drains its target Bound the factor: "k * B * max(0, 1 - C / capacity)"

A calibration gives a run that stops this way a penalty and goes on; see Calibration. A DifferentialEquations model is not checked: its solver may step below zero by its tolerance.

docs.title: What building checks
docs.text:
build plans every flow in the engine and rejects a transition it cannot simulate as written:

Rejected Message names A source or target that is neither a bin nor a category of one stratification The transition A category transition without exactly one source and one target The transition A rate variable that is not a parameter, bin, compartment or special variable The variable and the available names Several sources with a proportional rate The transition; use an absolute rate or $compartment A stratified rate whose category conditions match no source compartment The transition; use to to reach another stratification A to condition on a transition without a source The transition; use category to choose the compartment it enters A flow that ends in categories no compartment has The transition; add a to condition impulse_at and impulse_every together, a negative step, or a period that is not positive The transition A non-integer impulse step in a DifferenceEquations model The transition and the step

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

Commol checks that every rate of a built Model has the right units. To see the equations the engine simulates, with their units, see Describing a Model.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Model with Units", bin_unit="item", step_unit="day")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="1/day")
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 900, "B": 100, "C": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.

docs.title: Unit checking
docs.text: Model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=False) checks that every flow has the unit <bin unit>/<step unit>, every impulse the unit <bin unit>, and that every function receives a plain number. It checks DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations models alike: in both, a rate is per unit of the axis, and only what its value means differs (see What a rate means). It reads the flows the engine plans (transition_flows), so a proportional rate is checked as its flow, the rate times its source: k2 in 1/day from a bin in item gives item/day. The bin unit of a flow is the unit of the bin it leaves, or of the bin it enters when it has no source; so a category transition in a model of bins in item and kg moves item/day in one bin and kg/day in the other. In such a model total, a subgroup total total_<categories>, a category and neighbors add amounts of different units, so they have none, and a rate that reads one fails the check; read the bins or the compartments instead. A rate that reads the neighbors of a unit is checked as the sums they are. It raises UnitConsistencyError (from commol.utils.equations) and lists every transition that fails.

docs.title: What needs a unit
docs.text:
Item How it gets a unit Bins ModelBuilder(bin_unit=...), or add_bin(unit=...) for one bin. Required: the check names every bin without one. total, total_<category>… The bin unit, automatically Constant parameters add_parameter(unit=...). Required: the check raises if one is missing. Formula parameters Inferred from the formula; a unit is optional t The step unit, automatically: it is a position on the axis step, pi, e Dimensionless, automatically: step counts increments Unit Use for "1/day", "1/week", "1/step" Rates "dimensionless" Ratios, fractions, amplitudes, function arguments Any word that pint does not define, such as "item" A unit of its own dimension; Commol registers it

A unit means what pint defines, for time as for any other quantity: month, year and fortnight are units of time, but quarter is a unit of mass and decade is a number. A word that pint does not define, such as mo, becomes a unit of its own dimension, which no other unit converts to.

docs.title: The step unit
docs.text:
The engine converts no value between units. So one step has one unit, and every rate must use it (UnitChecker._step_unit in py-commol/commol/context/_model/units.py).

The axis of a model is its independent variable: the quantity the model steps along or differentiates over. Time is one case; a length, a dose or any other quantity is another. So the step unit may have any single dimension. Declare it with ModelBuilder(..., step_unit="day") (Model.step_unit); check_step_unit accepts one unit of one dimension with exponent 1, such as day or meter, and rejects 1/day or meter**2. A model that declares no step unit has the step unit step, the default increment of any axis, of its own dimension [step]. The check never guesses the step unit from the parameters.

Model Step unit Flows must be step_unit="day" day <bin unit>/day: a rate in 1/d passes, a rate in 1/week or 1/quarter fails step_unit="meter" meter <bin unit>/meter No step_unit, rates in 1/step or none step <bin unit>/step No step_unit, rates in 1/day step Fails; the error says to declare step_unit

Two names of one unit, such as d and day, are one unit. A flow must have exactly the expected unit: item/week does not match item/day, because the engine would read a weekly rate as a daily one.

along_a_line = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Along a line", bin_unit="item", step_unit="meter")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.01, unit="1/meter")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 1000, "B": 0},
        ),
        engine="DifferentialEquations",
    )
)
along_a_line.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.

Model.axis_units() converts values in units of the step dimension to steps, and gives the rates the engine reads; see Units of the axis.

docs.title: Positions and numbers in a rate
docs.text:
t is a position on the axis, so it has the step unit: with step_unit="day", k * t * A passes when k is in 1/day**2. step counts increments and is dimensionless.

A number written in a rate and added to, subtracted from or compared with a quantity is read in the unit of that quantity, as the engine reads it: if(t >= 10, k, 0) compares t with 10 days, and t - 3 is 3 days before t. The two branches of if and the arguments of min and max must share a unit, and a written 0 takes the unit of the other branch. A number that a function computes, such as exp(2), stays dimensionless.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text: An impulse moves an amount at once, so its rate must have the bin unit: p * A with p in "dimensionless" is an amount of <bin unit>; k * A with k in "1/day" is a flow and fails with expected '<bin unit>'.

docs.title: What the check catches
docs.text:
from commol.utils.equations import UnitConsistencyError

wrong_units = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Wrong units", bin_unit="item", step_unit="day")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="day")  # should be "1/day"
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_ba", source=["B"], target=["A"], rate="k2 * sin(B) * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            bin_amounts={"A": 900, "B": 100},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

try:
    wrong_units.check_unit_consistency()
except UnitConsistencyError as error:
    print(error)
Error Cause Unit mismatch: equation '…' has unit 'day * item' but expected 'item/day' A rate with the wrong unit Cannot convert from 'item' to 'dimensionless' A function such as sin, exp or log received a quantity with a unit The following constant parameters are missing units: … A constant parameter has no unit The following bins have no unit: … A bin has no unit (set bin_unit) The model declares no step unit, so it is 'step' Rates in a unit such as 1/day without step_unit; see The step unit Variable '…' … has no defined unit A variable of a rate has no unit

To pass a quantity to a function, make it dimensionless first, for example sin(2 * pi * step / 365) or exp(-decay * step) with decay in "dimensionless", or sin(2 * pi * t / period) with period in the step unit.

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
Back to Home

A calibration gives one set of parameters. This section shows how far you can trust it: which parameters the data identify, how the inputs move the outputs, and whether the intervals you report cover what they claim. This page defines what every method returns and reads: a weighted parameter sample, the predictive of a sample, and the scores that check it against data. Each method has its own page, listed in the table below.

docs.title: The three questions
docs.text: Question What answers it Which parameters fit the data? The identifiability methods; a sample of the parameters, or a profile of the likelihood or the loss; several starts that end apart with equal losses show that the data do not identify the parameters How do the inputs move the outputs? The predictive of a sample: the run of every draw, and its band; with no data, a sensitivity analysis, which propagates the inputs and ranks them Are the intervals calibrated? Scores of the predictive against observations the method did not see, and coverage studies

docs.title: A band of the model, or a prediction interval
docs.text: A band of the model is the spread of the model's output across the draws of the parameters. It says where the model curve lies, not where the next observation will fall: an observation also carries measurement noise. A prediction interval adds that noise to every draw before it reduces them (the ObservationNoise port of commol-inference). Every reader of observations takes the noise as an argument with no default: NoNoise() gives a band of the model, ResidualNoise(...) adds residuals of a fit, which gives a prediction interval with no noise model (Resampling), and DistributionNoise() draws from the observation models of the problem. Comparing a band of the model with data underestimates the spread, so its coverage of the data is below its level. A conformal interval is a prediction interval with a coverage guarantee, from the scores of observations the fit did not use.

docs.text:

Each uncertainty method adds its row here when it lands.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import (
    Aggregate,
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    ModelBuilder,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    NoNoise,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    ParameterSample,
    Predictive,
    SampleMethod,
    Simulation,
    scores,
)


def basic_model(k1: float | None, k2: float | None):
    return (
        ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
        .add_parameter(id="k1", value=k1)
        .add_parameter(id="k2", value=k2)
        .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
        .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
        .build(
            Aggregate(bin_amounts={"A": 990, "B": 10, "C": 0}),
            engine="DifferenceEquations",
        )
    )


truth = Simulation(basic_model(0.4, 0.1)).run(num_steps=60)
observations = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=step, output="B", value=truth["B"][step])
    for step in range(5, 61, 5)
]
# Fit the first 40 steps; hold out the rest to check the predictive.
fitted = [point for point in observations if point.at <= 40]
held_out = [point for point in observations if point.at > 40]

problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=fitted,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k1", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0),
        CalibrationParameter(id="k2", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0),
    ],
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=2000),
    seed=42,
)
calibrator = Calibrator(Simulation(basic_model(None, None)), problem)

# A sample of the parameters. A method returns one; here it is written by hand.
sample = ParameterSample.equally_weighted(
    names=["k1", "k2"],
    bounds=[(0.0, 1.0), (0.0, 1.0)],
    values=[[0.38, 0.09], [0.40, 0.10], [0.42, 0.11]],
    method=SampleMethod(name="by hand"),
)
print(sample.interval(0.9)["k1"])  # (0.38, 0.42)

# The predictive: every draw run to step 60, and its band of the model.
predictive = Predictive(calibrator, sample, positions=list(range(61)))
band = predictive.band(confidence_level=0.9)
print(band.lower["B"][50] <= truth["B"][50] <= band.upper["B"][50])  # True

# Scores of the band of the model on the held-out observations.
print(scores.coverage(predictive, held_out, NoNoise(), confidence_level=0.9).mean)
print(scores.crps(predictive, held_out, NoNoise()).per_series)

docs.title: The parameter sample
docs.text:
A ParameterSample holds draws of the parameters of one problem, each with a weight. Every method with draws returns one; the plots, the reports, the predictive and the scores read it, never the result of a method.

Field Meaning names One name per column, in the order of the problem's parameters bounds The bounds of each parameter; every value lies inside them values One row per draw log_weights The log weight of each draw, normalized so the weights sum to 1; -inf for a weight of zero groups The chain, replicate or wave of each draw, or None method The name and settings of the method that made it (SampleMethod)

Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust. With equal weights it is the unweighted statistic.

Member Returns mean() The weighted mean of each parameter covariance(), correlation() Weighted matrices, in the order of names; with equal weights, NumPy's cov and corrcoef quantiles(levels), interval(confidence_level) Weighted quantiles by the one convention effective_size() Kish's effective sample size, 1 / Σ wᵢ² draws() One {name: value} mapping per draw resample(count, seed) A sample of equal weights, drawn by weight summary(confidence_level) A ParameterSummary per parameter, for a report 
print(round(sample.effective_size(), 6))  # 3.0
print(next(sample.draws()))  # {'k1': 0.38, 'k2': 0.09}

A sample has no single set of parameters, so Model.apply_calibration_parameters rejects it with a TypeError; apply one of sample.draws(). A sample saves to JSON and loads back equal (model_dump_json, model_validate_json).

docs.title: The one quantile
docs.text:
Every interval of commol is a weighted quantile: the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution, interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights. With equal weights it equals numpy.percentile(..., method="hazen"). A draw of weight zero does not count. weighted_quantiles computes it for any values, and member_statistics reduces ensemble members with it.

from commol import weighted_quantiles

print(weighted_quantiles([0.0, 1.0], levels=[0.5], weights=[1.0, 3.0]))  # [0.75]

docs.title: The predictive
docs.text:
Predictive(source, sample, positions) runs every draw at positions, in parallel in Rust, through the forward model of its source: a Calibrator, or a SensitivityAnalysis of the inputs of the sample. With a stochastic engine every replicate of a draw is a draw of the predictive, with an equal share of its weight and a seed of its own, derived from the seed of the source, so every draw shows fresh noise and the predictive repeats from that seed.

Member Returns band(confidence_level) The weighted mean, median and central interval of every output at every position (PredictiveBand) series_band(outputs, confidence_level, cumulative=False) The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total; each draw is reduced first at_observations(observed_data, noise) Every draw's value of each observation, read through the observation operator the loss uses (sums, windows and factors), with noise drawn from the calibrator's seed: NoNoise(), ResidualNoise(...) or DistributionNoise() (ObservationDraws) runs(), weights The trajectory and weight of every draw

SimulationPlotter.plot_series and plot_cumulative draw the band of a predictive when it is the calibration_result, and simulation_report reduces its draws with their weights when it is the ensemble_runs. applied_parameters_report takes the sample itself (sample=, with a confidence_level).

docs.title: Scores
docs.text:
The functions of commol.scores compare a predictive with observations, and return a Score: the value of each observation, the mean of each series and the overall mean. Which observations to score and the observation noise are arguments with no default: score data the method did not see, such as the held-out positions above, and say whether you score a band of the model (NoNoise()) or a prediction interval (ResidualNoise(...), DistributionNoise()).

Function Score Better coverage(predictive, observations, noise, confidence_level) 1 inside the central interval, 0 outside; the mean is the empirical coverage Close to the level interval_score(predictive, observations, noise, confidence_level) (u − l) + (2/α)(l − y)₊ + (2/α)(y − u)₊, α = 1 − c Lower weighted_interval_score(predictive, observations, noise, confidence_levels) The weighted interval score of Bracher et al. (2021) Lower crps(predictive, observations, noise) Σ wᵢ|xᵢ − y| − ½ Σᵢⱼ wᵢwⱼ|xᵢ − xⱼ|, the CRPS of a stochastic calibration's loss Lower pit(predictive, observations, noise, seed) F(y), randomized where draws tie with y Uniform log_score(predictive, observations, DistributionNoise()) log Σ_d w_d · p(y | μ_d), the log density of y under the mixture of the observation models over the draws; another noise raises a TypeError Higher

docs.title: The entry point
docs.text:
Every method runs through Calibrator.uncertainty(method). A method is a configuration, a subclass of UncertaintyMethod[R] whose type parameter R is its result; the call returns an R, which a static type checker infers from the configuration's type. A configuration with no registered runner raises a ValueError that names the registered ones.

The identifiability methods run through their own entry point, Calibrator.identifiability(method), with a subclass of IdentifiabilityMethod[R]: they answer another question (Identifiability). Both kinds subclass InferenceMethod[R] and share one registry; each entry point refuses the other kind with a TypeError that names the right one. The sensitivity methods, subclasses of SensitivityMethod[R], run with no data through SensitivityAnalysis(simulation, inputs).run(method), the third entry point of the registry (Sensitivity Analysis).

from commol import BayesianBootstrap

result = calibrator.uncertainty(BayesianBootstrap(replicates=20, block_length=1))
print(type(result).__name__, len(result.sample))  # BootstrapResult 20

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] You report a band of the model as a band of the model, not as a prediction interval.
  • [ ] You score observations the method did not see.
  • [ ] The effective size of a weighted sample is large enough for the intervals you read.
